articles.title: New Google Home update comes with Find My Phone fixes, video doorbell improvements, and more — but for some users, there’s still a lot to be done
articles.text:
Google Home is getting a slew of fresh upgrades for Find My Phone and other smart home tools — but it’s not enough for some users
Issues are persisting for some
- Google Home is rolling out updates for Find My Phone and other voice commands
- It's also fixing bugs with video doorbells, security cameras, and Automations
- Despite the upgrades, users are still running into performance issues
If you’re a Google Home early access user, you’ll be glad to learn that the company is rolling out an expansive roster of new upgrades for voice commands, the Google Home app, and more — as per Google’s notes.
Google Home updates are fairly consistent with Google keeping on top of refreshing its smart home services. Just two weeks ago it fixed Gemini’s follow-up question issues as well as streaming playback bugs, which the tech giant also detailed in its Home and Nest help page.
Prior to this, Google announced it had solved issues with Spotify voice commands and smart light controls, however users claimed there were even bigger issues that needed addressing. But despite the new round of improvements, it appears Google still hasn’t been able to solve the issues plaguing users.
Voice commands
Voice command improvements are the main fixes that Google has rolled out. For starters, the company says that Gemini is more proficient in filtering out background chatter in your home when you’re making a voice request, as well as other smaller issues including reduced latency for sharper responses and more fixes to conversation follow-ups.
That said, one of the most valuable upgrades is for the Find My Phone tool, which Google says it has rolled out quality and reliability improvements to improve the experience. Additionally, language recognition for Gemini is getting an upgrade, which the company says will ‘better support households where three languages are commonly spoken’.
Google Home app
As far as the Google Home App goes, the company is rolling out more device controller upgrades, which includes more accurate smart light shutoff, redesigned camera and doorbell tiles to better distinguish active cameras, and improved offline switch status, fixing an issue where Matter switches failed to display their offline status.
Google is also rolling out Bluetooth connection and Wi-Fi pairing fixes for setting up new Nest devices on iOS and Android. Also, when you add a device to your ecosystem, the Google Home app will cache network information on your smartphone, so you can reuse them for setting up new devices in the future.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Camera fixes
For devices such as the AI-powered Nest Doorbell and security cameras, you can expect to see fixes for video history viewing, removing an error that displayed a ‘Video not available’ pop-up when trying to access footage. If you own any of Walmart’s Onn devices, you should now be able to scrub your video timelines a lot smoother.
Google is also launching new ringtone audio previews for video doorbells, which allows you to listen to snippets of chimes right from the Google Home app before setting it as your default. Google says it will be rolling out holiday-themed chimes, while different themes will become available throughout the year.
Automations
The final fix is with Automations, which Google says has eliminated a bug where multi-button switches and sub-devices were missing the names of their parent devices. It’s a small fix, but one that helps you differentiate between buttons.
Is this enough?
The transition from Google Assistant to Gemini has been far from a smooth operation, and users have been reporting severe performance issues since Google made its first steps with integrating Gemini into its smart home devices.
That said, since Google unveiled its latest update, users have welcomed the new improvements — mainly the chime sound previews and upgrades to Automations. However there's a handful of users that Google has yet to convince.
Despite the rollout of Google's upgrades users are finding themselves yet stuck in another cycle of performance issues when using Gemini for Home, and it seems to be the case more so for audio devices and voice commands.
As one user highlights on Reddit, their Google speaker turns itself off in the middle of the night when playing white noise, which, if you rely on sleep sounds to get a full eight hours, is quite frustrating to say the least. The same goes for voice commands, and as one user shared, Gemini is still having issues with switching off devices within a specific time frame.
As it stands, there's still a lot that Google has to come to grips with as it enters the final stages of the Gemini for Home takeover. While some fixes are proving to be successful, there's still work to be done before Google Home users are satisfied.

articles.title: Facturation électronique : une fuite touche une plateforme agréée, des données bancaires ont été piratées
articles.text:
Un nouvel incident frappe le monde de la facturation électronique. VosFactures, un logiciel de facturation en ligne utilisé par de nombreuses entreprises françaises, a été victime d’une cyberattaque. Dans un communiqué envoyé à ses clients fin du mois de septembre 2026, la société indique qu’un pirate a pu accéder à une copie de sa base de données.
 30 jours.
 C’est le temps qu’il aura fallu à ma plateforme agréée de facturation pour se faire pirater. pic.twitter.com/VCNzi4wVku
— Nicolas (@nb4ld) September 30, 2026
Pour rappel, VosFactures figure parmi les plateformes agréées pour la facturation électronique en France. La plateforme a obtenu ce statut en avril dernier, plusieurs mois avant l’entrée en vigueur de la réforme dans l’Hexagone. Une plateforme agréée est un opérateur « qui a fait l’objet d’une procédure d’immatriculation par l’administration », pour une durée de trois ans renouvelable, explique le site des impôts.
Depuis le 1ᵉʳ septembre 2026, toutes les entreprises soumises à la TVA doivent pouvoir recevoir les factures électroniques de leurs fournisseurs. Cela concerne aussi les micro-entrepreneurs et les auto-entrepreneurs. Bercy laisse trois mois aux entreprises pour s’adapter. Passé ce délai, les retardataires risquent entre 15 et 50 euros d’amende par facture, dans la limite de 15 000 euros par an.
La cyberattaque découle d’une faille d’un outil de génération de PDF. Selon le communiqué de VosFactures, « une personne non autorisée est parvenue à exploiter une vulnérabilité affectant un mécanisme de génération de fichiers PDF à partir de modèles de factures ». Le hacker a ainsi accédé à des fichiers de configuration de serveurs, qui contenaient « des clés applicatives et des identifiants techniques ». Avec ces précieuses informations, l’attaquant a pu « exécuter des commandes sur plusieurs serveurs ». Il a aussi pu accéder à la base de données de production de la plateforme.
À lire aussi : Une nouvelle fuite de données frappe l’État français, et l’Anssi fait partie des victimes
Quelles données ont été compromises ?
Selon les investigations de VosFactures, le pirate a pu consulter les données des comptes des entreprises et des utilisateurs, mais aussi celles des clients, des fournisseurs et des partenaires enregistrés sur la plateforme. Certaines données d’anciens documents de facturation ont également été compromises.
Ce n’est pas tout. Les « empreintes cryptographiques des mots de passe » ont aussi été exposées. Il s’agit de versions transformées des mots de passe, brouillés par des algorithmes. Sans la clé de déchiffrement, le pirate n’est pas en mesure de décoder les mots de passe en sa possession. Certaines coordonnées bancaires et informations de paiement ont aussi été piratées au cours de l’intrusion. Néanmoins, les « données complètes de cartes bancaires » n’ont pas été subtilisées. Des factures, antérieures au 1ᵉʳ janvier 2023, ont aussi été dérobées. Selon toute vraisemblance, les factures émises après le 31 décembre 2023 n’ont par contre pas été volées. La société affirme enfin qu’aucune donnée n’a été supprimée durant l’attaque.
Ces données peuvent servir à mettre au point des arnaques particulièrement crédibles, reposant sur de fausses factures ou de faux changements de RIB. Les utilisateurs de VosFactures sont invités à redoubler de vigilance jusqu’à nouvel ordre. Par précaution, ils peuvent également changer leur mot de passe. On recommande aussi d’accueillir avec scepticisme toute demande de modification de coordonnées bancaires par mail ou par SMS.
Une seconde fuite dans le monde de la facturation électronique
Ce n’est pas la première fuite qui entache l’entrée en vigueur de la facturation électronique en France. Il y a quelques semaines, Welyb, une plateforme collaborative très utilisée par les cabinets comptables français pour centraliser les documents de leurs clients, a été la victime d’une attaque sur un portail en ligne. Les pirates ont récupéré des noms, prénoms, adresses postales, e-mails, numéros de téléphone et mots de passe, ainsi que des données professionnelles. Ces incidents relancent le débat sur les dangers inhérents de la réforme. En amont de l’entrée en vigueur de celles-ci, de nombreux experts de la sécurité ont en effet alerté sur les risques de piratage et de vol de données, à l’heure où la France enchaîne les cyberattaques.

articles.title: OpenAI says actors linked to China-based Moonshot AI spearheaded a campaign to extract its models’ hidden reasoning — logged 16,000 extraction requests across 4,000 accounts before cutoff
articles.text:
OpenAI says actors linked to China-based Moonshot AI spearheaded a campaign to extract its models’ hidden reasoning — logged 16,000 extraction requests across 4,000 accounts before cutoff
OpenAI disrupted the campaign from July and has tightened its protections.
OpenAI said in a company blog post that people associated with China-based Moonshot AI were at the core of an effort to pull hidden reasoning from its models. The post says that a “coordinated campaign” to extract “protected reasoning” from its models, which was “consistent with adversarial distillation,” occurred in July. OpenAI isn’t sure whether all of the operators it saw were a single actor.
Activity began on July 1st, “initially at a low volume.” After that came “high-volume spikes” on July 24 and 25, with 16,000 requests using an extraction pattern. The requests came from over 4,000 users. The activity attempted extraction but was “not necessarily successful,” and the campaign was “fully disrupted by July 28.” The post did not clarify any measure of success rate, which models were specifically targeted, or how many of the users were Moonshot-linked.
OpenAI defines protected reasoning as “the model’s internal record for working through a task” and adversarial distillation as the “systematic and unauthorized use of one model’s outputs or reasoning” to train or improve another model. This data is encrypted to hide the model’s chain of thought and is handed to the client as an encrypted block. The client sends that block back with each request, so the provider doesn’t have to store it. One method the operators tried took the encrypted reasoning from one conversation and asked a model in another to decrypt it.
OpenAI says the encryption, in this case, was not broken. There was no direct access to stored user conversations, and no database was compromised. One fix closed a pathway that let someone who already had another user’s encrypted reasoning replay it and recover its contents. Separately, it added checks to detect and hold streamed output that might expose reasoning. It also strengthened protections for hidden reasoning across users, workspaces, organizations, and model families, and worked with third-party providers to disrupt accounts whose activity moved through their services.
Independent security researchers had also brought “related cross-model and conversation-compaction vulnerabilities” to OpenAI through responsible disclosure, and the company confirmed the attack paths they found were real. The paper “Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs,” dated Aug. 10, is explicitly linked by the post. Testing OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, the researchers fed a frontier model’s encrypted reasoning to a corresponding weaker model, which then wrote it out in plain text. The researchers ran their test in early July and, after the providers acknowledged their report, they were “unable to launch the same attacks.”
OpenAI is not alone in facing such threats. Earlier this month, Anthropic’s report “Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026” detailed a single ten-day period in which Moonshot relayed almost 300,000 customer requests to Anthropic using a proxy network of 5,380 fraudulent accounts. The report also says Moonshot saved Claude’s reasoning signatures and, in new sessions, got Claude to convert them back into full reasoning traces, which Anthropic calls “cross-session replay attacks.” In July, Moonshot denied that Kimi K3 was created from a distillation, and at the time OpenAI President Greg Brockman said it was “too early” to tell whether Moonshot had distilled OpenAI’s models.
OpenAI’s next step, meanwhile, is to ensure partner-hosted deployments have the same protections as first-party tools. Additional checks are needed to prevent tool-output attacks. It shared its findings with the Frontier Model Forum and government information-sharing channels, noting that “systems that support portable or replayable reasoning artifacts may face related risks.” The company expects distillation attempts to grow more sophisticated as frontier models improve and as attackers look for cheaper ways to mimic them. The work to protect against those attempts is ongoing.

articles.title: D-Wave opens quantum computing gate-model simulator beta program - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
D-Wave opens quantum computing gate-model simulator beta program
D-Wave Quantum Inc., a commercial supplier of quantum computing hardware and software, today announced the launch of its gate-model quantum computing simulator program in beta test mode, allowing customers to test error-aware programs.
The simulator is built around D-Wave’s dual-rail superconducting gate-model technology, which is designed to detect errors and correct them, allowing more efficient hardware scaling.
D-Wave offers both gate-model and annealing quantum computing systems. Gate-model quantum computers operate like traditional computers, using Boolean logic gates and allowing procedural programming. Annealing quantum computers, by contrast, manipulate energy boundaries to solve optimization problems.
Different from classical computing, gate-model quantum computing manages probability amplitudes across quantum bits and allows it to create specialized probability gates that can exist in superpositions – creating logical connections that can be 1, 0, or both 1 and 0 at the same time. It can also operate on multi-qubit gates that link multiple qubits through a phenomenon called quantum entanglement.
This architecture enables complex procedural logic systems to exist in multiple states at once before an answer is finalized. This essentially lets a quantum circuit run a calculation rapidly because it executes combinations of a program in parallel using physics.
The computer itself runs the circuit multiple times because a single run may not guarantee a correct answer, but since each run is extremely fast – much faster than a similar classical computer – the time it takes is negligible. Finally, the distribution of the answers is examined and the frequency reveals the correct solution.
Chief Executive Dr. Alan Baratz said the beta program marks a major milestone in the company’s roadmap towards advancing fault-tolerant gate-model quantum computing.
“Quantum error correction is a defining challenge in the race to commercially useful gate-model quantum computing,” Baratz said. “By giving leading organizations early access to our simulator, we’re enabling them to explore a fundamentally more efficient approach to fault tolerance and the applications we expect it will unlock.”
The company recently published a research paper in Nature demonstrating a foundational layer of the dual-rail architecture that preserves error detection. In the paper, D-Wave researchers showed how high-fidelity two-qubit entangling gates can operate with error correction.
Fault tolerance matters for quantum computers because qubits are extremely fragile and affected by “noise.” Noise can be anything from changes in the environment, such as shifts in temperature, electromagnetism, stray light particles or vibrations – anything can cause them to lose coherence or even flip information. As a result, quantum computers are built to detect and correct errors, and often to scale the number of qubits side by side so that if noise alters one qubit, its siblings remain unaffected.
Participants in the beta program included organizations spanning commercial and research outfits: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria S.A., FirstQFM, Florida Atlantic University and the Jülich Supercomputing Centre.
“Quantum machine learning models that perform well under ideal conditions may behave very differently when exposed to realistic hardware constraints,” said FAU Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science Dr. Arslan Munir. “D-Wave’s simulator will allow us to investigate how error-aware, qubit-efficient approaches could improve the robustness of quantum machine learning and help establish practical design guidelines.”

articles.title: Como reclamar na Uber? Veja o passo a passo para entrar em contato com o suporte • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Como reclamar na Uber? Veja o passo a passo para entrar em contato com o suporte
A Uber possui uma central de atendimento digital no próprio aplicativo, facilitando o contato para reportar diferentes tipos de incidentes durante um percurso
Fazer reclamação na Uber é essencial para resolver cobranças indevidas, problemas de tráfego e condutas inadequadas de motoristas. Para solucionar essas ocorrências, a plataforma centraliza o suporte de forma totalmente digital por meio do próprio aplicativo.
Basta abrir a guia “Atividades”, selecionar a viagem que você deseja reportar e tocar na opção “Atendimento ao usuário” para entrar em contato com a Uber. Vale dizer que a plataforma não possui um número ou canal oficial de WhatsApp para atendimento geral do passageiro.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog te mostra como reclamar na Uber sobre uma viagem ou um motorista.
Se tiver problemas em uma viagem, você pode reclamar na Uber diretamente pelo aplicativo de forma rápida e intuitiva. O processo é simples e ajuda a solucionar desde cobranças indevidas até condutas inadequadas.
Abra o aplicativo Uber no seu celular e toque na guia “Atividade”, localizada na parte inferior do menu principal.
Navegue pelo histórico recente e toque em cima da viagem específica à qual você deseja fazer reclamação na Uber.
Desça a tela com os detalhes da viagem e toque na opção “Atendimento ao usuário” para visualizar os temas disponíveis para queixa.
Escolha a categoria que melhor descreve o seu caso ou clique em “Mais opções” para enviar uma mensagem detalhada ao suporte da Uber.
Se você enfrentou algum transtorno ou conduta inadequada no trajeto, é possível reportar à Uber sobre as ações do motorista diretamente no aplicativo. O procedimento é rápido, seguro e ajuda a manter a qualidade e segurança da plataforma:
O aplicativo do Uber permite reportar falhas operacionais, cobranças incorretas e problemas graves de conduta de forma simples e rápida. Conheça as principais situações em que você deve entrar em contato com a Uber para garantir seus direitos e solicitar suporte:
Sim, você pode solicitar ajuda para recuperar um objeto perdido no Uber. Basta acessar a aba “Atividades”, selecionar a corrida em questão e tocar em “Encontrar objeto perdido” para entrar em contato com o motorista.
Se você perdeu o próprio celular ou não teve retorno em até 24 horas, é recomendado acessar sua conta pelo site do serviço para reportar o caso. Vale lembrar que a Uber cobra uma taxa de devolução para cobrir o deslocamento do motorista parceiro.
Não existe um canal 0800 para falar com a Uber por telefone ou registrar queixas de passageiros no Brasil. O suporte oficial e o atendimento para resolver problemas acontecem exclusivamente pelo aplicativo ou pela Central de Ajuda na Web.
As linhas gratuitas, como a 0800 006 8086, funcionam apenas como suporte emergencial para motoristas parceiros durante os trajetos. Além disso, não há uma ouvidoria telefônica tradicional, e qualquer número divulgado na internet como telefone da Uber para reclamação pode indicar fraude.
Não existe um número oficial de WhatsApp para o público geral no Brasil entrar em contato com a Uber para resolver problemas de viagens pessoais. Qualquer canal similar ao SAC da plataforma funciona exclusivamente por meio da Central de Ajuda no app ou no site.
A única exceção do serviço de mensagens é voltada para gestores e funcionários do Uber para Empresa, pelo número internacional +1 925-378-4197. Portanto, não caia em fraudes no app de mensagens, pois códigos de verificação e senhas jamais devem ser compartilhados.

articles.title: Estas son las nuevas funciones de Apple Wallet en los iPhone con iOS 27
articles.text:
iOS 27, la más reciente actualización del sistema operativo móvil de Apple, incorpora un conjunto de funciones nuevas para Apple Wallet, la aplicación de billetera digital de la compañía.
Entre las novedades más destacadas se encuentra la posibilidad de dividir la cuenta de un restaurante a partir de la foto de un recibo, una herramienta pensada para quienes suelen terminar pagando la totalidad de la cuenta cuando salen a comer con amigos.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo funciona la división de cuentas con Apple Cash
La función utiliza Apple Intelligence para convertir los ítems de un recibo en elementos seleccionables, de modo que el usuario pueda identificar con rapidez qué le corresponde pagar. El proceso se activa desde el nuevo modo de Siri en la aplicación Cámara: al apuntar el lente hacia un recibo, aparece un aviso que ofrece la opción “Dividir cuenta con Apple Cash”.
A partir de ahí, se puede buscar entre los contactos a las personas con las que se desea repartir el gasto, aunque estas deben contar con la posibilidad de pagar mediante Apple Cash.
Una vez seleccionados los contactos, Apple Wallet despliega la lista de productos incluidos en el recibo para que el usuario elija los suyos, defina cómo repartir el monto total y establezca la propina. La aplicación no tiene capacidad para obligar a terceros a abonar su parte: no actúa como una agencia de cobro.
PUBLICIDAD
Importación de tarjetas físicas y creación de pases personalizados
Otra de las incorporaciones centrales de iOS 27 es la posibilidad de importar tarjetas físicas a Apple Wallet, una demanda que, según describió el medio 9to5Mac, figuraba entre las expectativas de larga data de los usuarios de la plataforma. Apple explicó que tanto en iPhone como en Apple Watch será posible crear y almacenar pases a partir de tarjetas físicas, como las de fidelización o membresía, sin necesidad de cargar con ellas físicamente.
El mecanismo reutiliza el modo Siri de la Cámara: basta con apuntar el iPhone hacia una tarjeta física con código de barras o capturar una tarjeta digital mediante una captura de pantalla para recibir la opción de guardarla en Apple Wallet. También es posible crear un pase directamente desde la aplicación, sin partir de una tarjeta existente.
PUBLICIDAD
Para sumar un elemento nuevo, el usuario debe presionar el ícono de “más” en la parte superior de la aplicación. Allí se despliegan opciones para escanear una tarjeta de débito, crédito, transporte o identificación, o bien elegir “Crear un pase” para trabajar a partir de una tarjeta de presentación.
Al editar los detalles de un pase personalizado, es posible importar y modificar el contenido de una tarjeta escaneada o cargar los datos de forma manual. Apple Wallet ofrece distintas plantillas para estos elementos y permite ajustar el color y el fondo de cada uno. La información puede editarse en cualquier momento posterior si cambia o si se cometió algún error al cargarla.
PUBLICIDAD
Una vez añadidos, los pases quedan disponibles para presentarse como código de barras o código QR desde el iPhone o el Apple Watch. Los modelos más recientes de Apple Watch, además, podrán anclar estos pases digitales personalizados mediante la función Smart Stack.
iOS 27 también suma una función para quienes utilizan Apple Card: la posibilidad de visualizar los pagos recurrentes asociados a la tarjeta. Para acceder a este listado, el usuario debe tocar la tarjeta dentro de Wallet y seleccionar la opción correspondiente en el menú de tres puntos ubicado en la esquina superior derecha.
Nuevas herramientas para desarrolladores
Durante su conferencia anual para desarrolladores, la WWDC, celebrada en junio, Apple había anticipado estas funciones junto con otras orientadas específicamente a programadores externos. Entre ellas se incluye la posibilidad de generar afiches para eventos con múltiples entradas y la incorporación de seguimiento de pedidos para aplicaciones de venta minorista mediante Apple Intelligence.
PUBLICIDAD
La compañía indicó que continuará incorporando funciones adicionales para Wallet a medida que avance con nuevas actualizaciones de iOS 27.

articles.title: Une campagne ClickFix détourne les GPT personnalisés de ChatGPT pour diffuser un malware
articles.text:
Des cybercriminels se servent désormais de GPT personnalisés pour alimenter une campagne ClickFix. Mis en avant dans des annonces Google, ces assistants conduisent les internautes vers de faux contrôles de sécurité qui les incitent à exécuter eux-mêmes la commande à l’origine de l’infection.
Cela devait bien finir par arriver. Les cybercriminels ont trouvé le moyen d’intégrer ChatGPT à leur chaîne d’infection sans compromettre la plateforme elle-même. Les chercheurs et chercheuses d’Huntress ont en effet identifié une nouvelle campagne ClickFix combinant résultats sponsorisés sur Google, GPT personnalisés hébergés sur le domaine officiel d’OpenAI et faux CAPTCHA Cloudflare pour inciter les victimes à exécuter une commande PowerShell. À la clé, un cheval de Troie d’accès à distance installé sur Windows et un contrôle étendu de la machine pour les attaquants.
La solution tout-en-un pour protéger votre entreprise
Votre petite entreprise a de grandes ambitions. Protégez-là contre les pirates. Et développez sereinement votre activité !
De ChatGPT au RAT, une chaîne d’infection bien huilée
Dans le détail, le vecteur d’infection repose sur un GPT baptisé « Plus 5.6 », promu par l’intermédiaire de résultats sponsorisés sur Google. Hébergé sur chatgpt.com comme n’importe quel GPT personnalisé, il profite du domaine officiel d’OpenAI pour inspirer confiance, avant de prétexter des difficultés rencontrées par le service principal et d’orienter l’internaute vers un prétendu site de secours hébergé sur Google Sites.
La page de redirection affiche alors un faux contrôle anti-bot aux couleurs de Cloudflare et, comme dans toute attaque ClickFix qui se respecte, présente l’exécution d’une commande PowerShell comme nécessaire pour accéder au service promis. Lancée par la victime elle-même, cette commande récupère un fichier MSI qui amorce l’installation du malware, sans qu’aucune faille de ChatGPT ait besoin d’être exploitée.
Le programme d’installation dépose ensuite plusieurs composants sur la machine, parmi lesquels un exécutable légitime signé par Canon ou, selon les variantes, par Stardock, que les pirates détournent pour lui faire charger une DLL malveillante, point de départ d’une série de composants chiffrés exécutés en mémoire pour limiter les traces sur le disque et compliquer la détection de l’infection jusqu’au lancement du RAT.
Le cheval de Troie donne alors aux attaquants un accès très large à la machine : contrôle du bureau à distance, recherche de fichiers, reconnaissance du système, capture audio et vidéo ou encore exécution de charges supplémentaires. Pour survivre aux redémarrages, il crée une entrée dans le Registre Windows et une tâche planifiée, baptisées « Canon Configuration Reader » dans un cas et « Stardock DeElevation Tool » dans l’autre.
Huntress a relié au moins 40 incidents à la page utilisée dans cette campagne, mais seuls deux ont formellement pu être rattachés à un GPT personnalisé. OpenAI avait supprimé le premier GPT signalé par les chercheurs le 25 septembre ; deux jours plus tard, Huntress en repérait un second associé à la même opération.
Des indices qui permettent de déjouer l’attaque
On le rappellera encore et toujours : une vérification web se déroule dans le navigateur. Elle peut impliquer de cocher une case, de sélectionner des images ou d’attendre quelques secondes, mais certainement pas d’ouvrir PowerShell (ni l’invite de commandes, ni la boîte Exécuter de Windows) pour y copier-coller une commande et la valider. Le cas échéant, quittez la page.
Si vous cherchez un GPT pour une tâche précise, passez directement par la recherche intégrée à ChatGPT plutôt que par une annonce sponsorisée dans Google. Le GPT Store permet de consulter son nom, sa description et les informations disponibles sur son créateur avant de l’ouvrir.
La présence d’un GPT dans le store du chatbot IA ne garantit pas non plus la fiabilité de ses instructions. Les GPT personnalisés sont créés par des tiers et peuvent légitimement renvoyer vers des sites extérieurs, mais s’ils vous demandent de toucher directement au système, interrompez immédiatement la procédure.
Si la commande a déjà été exécutée, fermer l’onglet ne suffira pas. Déconnectez le PC du réseau, lancez une analyse complète avec une solution de sécurité à jour et changez, depuis un appareil sain, les identifiants sensibles utilisés sur la machine.

articles.title: TP-Link Opens Pre-Orders for Archer 8 Ultra, Its First Wi-Fi 8 Router
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
	
	
	
TP-Link Opens Pre-Orders for Archer 8 Ultra, Its First Wi-Fi 8 Router
TP-Link Systems Inc. today announced the availability of Archer 8 Ultra, its first Wi-Fi 8 router, marking the arrival of a new generation of home connectivity. Wi-Fi 8 represents a turning point for the networking industry. Where previous generations chased peak speeds, Wi-Fi 8 is engineered for consistency, holding performance steady in the harsh, real-world conditions users face every day.
Jim Poder, Senior Vice President of R&D at TP-Link"Wi-Fi 8 sets a new foundation, and we've built beyond it. Archer 8 Ultra combines our Wi-Fi 8 StabilityEngine with intelligent antenna technology and AI-powered optimization to deliver what matters most: a smarter, more reliable network that's easier to use."
Ultra-High Reliability, Powered by Wi-Fi 8 StabilityEngine
Wi-Fi 8 prioritizes real-world reliability while preserving the high speeds consumers expect. TP-Link's Wi-Fi 8 StabilityEngine, built into the core of Archer 8 Ultra, strengthens coverage, eases congestion, and cuts interference through a suite of next-generation technologies:
Archer 8 Ultra is powered by Broadcom's Wi-Fi 8 chipset, built on the upcoming IEEE 802.11bn standard, paired with hardware and software engineering led by TP-Link's U.S.-based designers and developers.
Nineteen gigabits of tri-band Wi-Fi 8 deliver steadier performance and lower latency than Wi-Fi 7 at the same range. Two 10 Gbps auto-sensing WAN/LAN ports easily support the latest multi-gigabit internet plans, while four 2.5 Gbps LAN ports deliver rock-solid wired connections to demanding devices like a PC or game console.
Eighteen high-performance antennas are engineered inside the chassis, covering up to 3,600 sq. ft. for as many as 200 devices. The Multi-Floor Mode feature reshapes the signal to match where devices actually are, steering coverage to multiple floors when they are spread across levels and flattening to a wide, single-floor pattern when they are not. A new Wi-Fi 8 RF chip adds Range Boost, sharpening the router's ability to hear distant, low-power devices, whose weak uplink is the real bottleneck at the edge of coverage.
Manny Patel, Vice President of Marketing, Wireless and Broadband Communications Division at Broadcom"Wi-Fi 8 marks a fundamental shift toward reliability in home connectivity, and Broadcom's platform is engineered to deliver that performance at scale. We're excited to collaborate with innovative pioneers like TP-Link, which is among the first to deliver it to consumers."
Built Smarter, Made Easier
TP-Link's Aireal AI Assistant, built into the Tether app, works on two levels. On the surface, users can interact with it directly, answering plain-language questions about the network and helping them better understand and manage their Wi-Fi. Behind the scenes, it works automatically to keep the connection steady: Wi-Fi Optimizer continuously tunes the router to the clearest channel, Self-Healing resolves common issues, QoS prioritizes the traffic that matters, and ECO Mode trims power draw during off-peak hours to save energy.
Setup has never been easier. Out of the box, a tap of the phone to the router pairs it over NFC through the Tether app, which then walks users through the rest. Guests connect the same way, tapping to join without a password to hand over. The Tether app also monitors network status, manages Parental Controls, and personalizes settings through one intuitive interface.
Secure From the Ground Up
An integrated hardware-level VPN encrypts selected devices' traffic directly on the router and works with third-party VPN providers, while isolated guest and IoT networks keep vulnerability-prone devices off the main network. Users can also opt into TP-Link's HomeShield service for real-time protection, advanced parental controls, and WPA3 authentication.
Pricing and Availability
Pre-orders open today, September 30, 2026, in the United Kingdom, Germany, Australia, Canada and more. For pricing, visit each region's local TP-Link website. A global rollout for Archer 8 Ultra and the upcoming Deco 8 Ultra will be announced over the coming months.

articles.title: A man could face a decade in prison for a fake crocodile photo he made with Gemini
articles.text:
WTF?! Some people love to generate AI slop images that spread false information, especially the kind that make people worry. That's not a good idea if you're in Singapore, where a man who used Gemini to make a fake image of a crocodile in a popular reservoir has been charged over the act and could face up to ten years in prison.
Ye Lin allegedly sent the AI-generated image of a saltwater crocodile at Pandan Reservoir to a colleague in August, presumably as a joke.
But the image led to a crocodile sighting being reported to Singapore's national water agency, PUB. The agency and national parks staff suspended all aquatic activities in the area for two days and started looking for a crocodile that didn't exist in the popular kayaking spot.
The following day, the agency confirmed that the image was a fake and reported it to the police, leading to Lin's arrest.
Singapore takes this sort of thing very seriously. Transmitting a false message is a crime that carries up to three years in prison, a fine of up to S$10,000 (about $7,800), or both.
If that wasn't bad enough, police say Lin tried to hide what he'd done by deleting the image and the Gemini app from his phone. Unfortunately for him, that meant he's also being charged with obstruction of justice, the punishment for which is up to seven years in prison.
It's still not clear how PUB officials were notified of the AI photo. It could be that the person Lin sent it to then forwarded it to someone else who thought it was real.
It doesn't sound like Lin was intentionally trying to start a panic with the image, but Singapore isn't ranked as one of the safest countries in the world because it has a lenient justice system.
Ye said he intends to plead guilty and will not be using a lawyer. His case will be heard again in November.
In the US, generating legal images like these isn't going to result in a potential decade-long jail sentence, though a fabricated image supporting a credible false claim about a bombing or other specified serious offense may fall under federal hoax law. If it really was a crime, a lot of social media users would probably be locked up.

articles.title: The Witcher 3 lead writer says that to create a Witcher remake, you need to 'stay true to the spirit of the original game'
articles.text:
The Witcher 3 writer says you need to 'stay true to the spirit of the original game' but find a way to bring it to a new audience using new tech with the upcoming Witcher remake
Fool's Theory is currently developing the remake
- The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt lead writer Marcin Blacha has explained what it takes to create a worthwhile Witcher remake
- He says CD Projekt Red needs to "stay true to the spirit" of the original game
- However, the remake has to appeal to a new audience using modern technology
CD Projekt Red VP of narration and story director Marcin Blacha has revealed the secret to making a worthwhile Witcher remake, and it's about balancing what made the original game good with appealing to a new audience.
During a panel at Logitech Play 2026 attended by TechRadar Gaming, Blacha, who was a lead writer on The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, explained that the studio needs to "stay true" to the 2007 original, but also design a fresh experience for gamers who didn't play it.
"The secret is to identify what was good in the original game, and find a way to retell it to the audience that, for some reason, cannot participate in this experience," Blacha said. "Those are two different things, and each of them is difficult on its own, because it's not that easy sometimes to recreate this experience."
The writer went on to discuss what the studio calls "Act Four" of The Witcher 1, which takes place in a rural lakeside region "that is very folklorish" and "full of beautiful landscapes," but said it's difficult to recreate that feeling again because it's a different experience for every player and can be "a little bit vague."
"To create a good remake, you need to identify what was good and find a way to recreate it using newer technology, [while] staying true to the spirit of the original game," Blacha added.
The Witcher remake is in development at Fool's Theory and will utilize Unreal Engine 5, as CD Projekt Red is currently all hands on deck making The Witcher 4, the first game in a new trilogy of Witcher games that it wants to release within a six-year time frame.
CDPR has also just launched The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered, which offers a massive collection of improvements that promise an entirely new experience for the decade-old role-playing game (RPG).

articles.title: Google dévoile un clavier à tapis roulant totalement absurde (et on n’y comprend rien)
articles.text:
Depuis l’arrêt des poissons d’avril en 2021, la filiale nippone de Google sort des excentricités chaque 1er octobre, date clin d’œil aux claviers à 101 touches (la date étant le 10/1). Après de précédents projets tout aussi absurdes, Google Japon s’attaque cette fois à la manière de taper à l’ordinateur avec un « clavier sur tapis roulant ». Plutôt que de déplacer ses doigts sur un plateau fixe, cette invention propose que les lettres viennent directement à vous grâce à un mécanisme motorisé.
Un tapis roulant mécanique pour faire défiler les touches
Comme vous pouvez le voir sur la vidéo ci-dessous, ce ne sont plus vos doigts qui bougent, mais le clavier lui-même qui se met en mouvement. Chaque bande comprend 29 touches, et elles sont au nombre de trois. On peut dire que les touches « tombent » sous les doigts, encore faut-il réussir à les attraper au bon moment, sous peine de devoir attendre le tour suivant.
Toujours dans ces explications improbables, Google Japon précise que cela vous permet de taper à une seule main et de libérer l’autre pour utiliser une souris ou boire votre tasse de thé. Vous pouvez également ajouter un second clavier pour gagner en productivité, à condition d’avoir les réflexes d’un jedi.
Fabriquez vous-même le clavier
Si ces arguments vous ont convaincu, vous ne pourrez malheureusement pas acheter le clavier Gboard. Google vous laisse en effet le soin de fabriquer le vôtre en partageant les plans complets et les caractéristiques techniques du produit en open source sur GitHub.
© Google Japon

Comme on n’arrête pas en si bon chemin une équipe aussi créative, Google Japon évoque aussi des déclinaisons potentielles, comme un mode ultra-rapide pour les plus pressés, ou encore de versions plus longues ou plus courtes. On ne sait pas trop quoi penser de cette bizarrerie qui pousse la blague très loin, sans pousser le vice jusqu’à commercialiser le produit.

articles.title: Metaview wants to eliminate recruiting grunt work and speed up hiring after raising $60M - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Metaview wants to eliminate recruiting grunt work and speed up hiring after raising $60M
Artificial intelligence recruiting software startup Metaview Labs Inc. said today the industry is ready for a “Claude Code moment” after it closed on $60 million in a Series C funding.
The round was led by Insight Partners and saw the participation of GV, Seedcamp, Vertex Ventures US, Intrepid Growth Partners, Plural and Garuda Ventures. To date, the company has now raised $110 million in total.
Although Metaview is hitching on the agentic AI wagon, it’s actually pretty old as far as AI startups go. It was founded back in 2018 by former Uber Technologies Inc. and Palantir Technologies Inc. employees Siadhal Magos and Shahriar Tajbakhsh, who serve as its chief executive and chief technology officer, respectively.
In a blog post, Magos said that the role of software engineers has evolved from writing code to orchestrating AI agents that do the grunt work for them, and now he predicts that recruiters are going to follow the same path. His startup has developed AI agents that automate much of the recruitment process, from creating the initial job ads to sourcing and screening candidates, reviewing their resumes and application letters, and then conducting initial interviews.
According to Magos, Metaview’s agents have already conducted more than 6 million interviews so far. Once a candidate’s interview is complete, the agents will transform their responses into usable notes for human reviewers to look through, so they can create a shortlist for in-person interviews. The interview questions themselves and the job qualification criteria are all set by humans first, he added.
There’s an urgent need for automated recruitment, Magos believes. He points out that recruiting is “hard, laborious work” and that there’s minimal technology used in the process. Many companies will scale their recruitment teams during hiring spikes, only to dismantle them when they’re no longer needed, but that’s “expensive, ineffective and painful for all involved,” he said.
The current state of the economy adds to the urgency for automation. More people are looking for work, and “applications per recruiter have increased 412%,” Magos explained. “So recruiters spend their days processing massive application queues, searching profiles, writing outreach, scheduling screens, chasing interview feedback and shuttling information between systems.”
Metaview’s AI agents can automate all of that work, and that’s why more than 7,000 companies are already using them, Magos said. Its highest-profile customers include enterprises such as Deel, Affirm and Replit Inc., which have managed to reduce their average time-to-hire by more than 75%.
In addition to today’s funding, Metaview is adding more capabilities to its agentic recruiting platform. The most notable is fillmore, an autonomous recruiting agent that’s able to research prospective job candidates, construct target lists, generate personalized emails for outreach, manage follow-up conversations and schedule meetings with those who are interested. It’s generally available today and operates entirely within Slack.
By using fillmore to automate this work, “recruiting becomes always-on, while people stay in control of the decisions that matter,” Magos argued.
Metaview is now in growth mode and it has three major priorities. The first is to expand its platform with even more agents that specialize in various aspects of the recruiting process. The second is the opening of its new office in New York City and the expansion of its teams, which currently number around 80 people.
Magos said the company plans to have more than 250 staff on its books by the end of next year, and is hiring for roles such as engineering, product, design and go-to-market. Presumably, its own agents will help to automate much of that process.
Last but not least, Metaview wants to expand its 10x Recruiting program, which offers training in AI for human recruiters. “The shift to agentic recruiting requires a new skill set, not just new software,” Magos said. “The best teams of the next decade will be built by people who know how to use these tools well.”

articles.title: Small Electronics Manufacturers Save Big on ERP - EE Times
articles.text:
Instead of spending large sums and years implementing a traditional ERP system, small and medium-sized electronics manufacturers are finding that modern, SME-focused manufacturing software can provide the functionality they need at a fraction of the cost and implementation effort.
Cost-effective and easy to use
MRPeasy is a manufacturing ERP system designed specifically for small and medium-sized manufacturers. This focus sets it apart from systems that originated as accounting or inventory applications, as well as large enterprise ERP platforms that can require extensive consulting, customization, and IT resources.
For smaller electronics manufacturers, the difference in implementation effort can be substantial.
Poweronics, a power electronics manufacturer producing gate drivers for high-power applications, needed to manage around 1,200 components across its product portfolio. Managing Director Colin Hart self-implemented MRPeasy after starting a free trial.
“The implementation was very straightforward—setting up MRPeasy only took me about three hours,” Hart says. The setup included around 1,500 SKU lines as well as existing bills of materials and sales, purchase, and manufacturing orders.
Britannia 2000 Holdings, which manufactures mission computers, displays, airborne video recorders, and other electronics for the aerospace and defense industry, also implemented the system internally.
“I set it up myself and it was that easy,” says Director Ralph Jones.
Cost is often another major consideration.
Exacta Technologies currently uses MRPeasy across dozens of users and integrates it with systems including Xero and Grafana. Managing Director Chris Landen says the software continues to provide good value even as the company has grown.
“MRPeasy does a lot for what it costs,” he says. “There are systems that cost far more and don’t give you meaningfully better functionality.”
The functionality electronics manufacturers actually need
Affordability only matters if the system can handle the realities of electronics manufacturing.
Electronics companies commonly need to manage large numbers of components, multi-level BOMs and subassemblies, product revisions, long supplier lead times, subcontracted operations, serial and lot traceability, and rapidly changing material costs. Even relatively small manufacturers can therefore have highly complex operations.
Poweronics is a good example. Its approximately 1,200 components need to be coordinated across purchasing, inventory, BOMs, manufacturing orders, and customer demand. After implementing MRPeasy, the company gained much tighter control over inventory.
“We’ve never had a shortage after adopting MRPeasy,” Hart says.
This is particularly important in electronics manufacturing because one missing low-cost component can prevent an expensive finished product from being completed. Reliable inventory records combined with material requirements planning help manufacturers see what they have, what upcoming production will consume, and what needs to be purchased.
For Exacta Technologies, which manufactures custom hardware platforms and high-performance servers, product complexity has increased significantly as the company has grown. MRPeasy is used to manage multi-level and configurable BOMs together with revision and engineering change control, inventory, purchasing, and production planning.
“Our product set is large and complex,” Landen says. MRPeasy enables the company to manage complex BOMs, including their revisions and engineering changes.
Traceability is another key requirement for many electronics companies.
Britannia 2000 operates in aerospace and defense, where the ability to track materials and components through the production process is particularly important.
“With the software, I’m able to track components and achieve traceability throughout the order chain,” Founder Ralph Jones says.
For manufacturers combining internal production with outsourced processes, ERP also provides a way to keep subcontracting within the same production plan.
US-based Technodynamics manufactures explosion-proof LED lighting systems for hazardous environments. Its manufacturing processes involve BOMs, routings, inventory, subcontracting, material tracking, and production costing. The company uses MRPeasy to keep internal and outsourced operations within one manufacturing workflow.
“The more complicated your manufacturing process gets, the more MRPeasy makes sense,” says Senior Production Engineer Alfred Neufeld.
Better control without enterprise-level overhead
The attraction of SME-focused ERP is therefore not simply that it costs less. The goal is to provide enough manufacturing functionality to replace spreadsheets and disconnected tools without introducing another layer of unnecessary complexity.
For electronics manufacturers, this can mean having one system connecting:
- Complex bills of materials and product revisions
- Inventory and component availability
- Material requirements and purchasing
- Production planning and scheduling
- Manufacturing orders and shop-floor reporting
- Lot and serial number traceability
- Routings and subcontracted operations
- Production costs and product pricing
- Customer orders, quoting, and delivery dates
Having this information connected becomes increasingly valuable as a manufacturer grows.
Exacta Technologies originally moved away from a combination of accounting software and spreadsheets because manual processes were becoming difficult to scale. Today, MRPeasy provides the operational backbone for a substantially larger company.
“Since we started using MRPeasy, we have achieved over 100% growth in revenue,” Landen says. “And we have almost tripled our employee count from 25 to 70 without adding the same proportion of administrative overhead.”
This illustrates an important point for growing electronics SMEs: an ERP investment does not necessarily need to come after a company becomes large. Putting proper manufacturing processes in place earlier can make it easier to grow without continually adding spreadsheets, manual coordination, and administrative staff.
Survey shows significant improvements after implementation
MRPeasy’s latest customer survey shows that these individual electronics manufacturing experiences reflect broader trends among its manufacturing customers.
Respondents reported average improvements of:
- 58% in inventory tracking accuracy
- 46% in operational efficiency
- 46% in cost control
- 37% in on-time deliveries
- 28% in overall business growth
And importantly for SMEs, gaining that level of control no longer necessarily requires an enterprise-sized ERP project.
As KCL Manufacturing’s VP of Operations and Manufacturing, Jonathan Greenwald, puts it, MRPeasy provides “robust, value-driven ERP capabilities typically reserved for larger enterprises” while remaining suited to a growing manufacturer.
The experiences of Poweronics, Exacta Technologies, Britannia 2000, Technodynamics, and other electronics manufacturers point to the same conclusion: smaller companies can now access serious manufacturing ERP functionality without taking on the cost and complexity traditionally associated with enterprise systems.
To learn more, please visit mrpeasy.com

articles.title: Cette box Orange apporte le Wi-Fi 7 à la maison sans fibre
articles.text:
Orange 5G+ Home : le très haut débit à la maison sans fibre
Orange propose sa 5G+ Home à 42,99 € par mois, sans engagement, avec une Flybox Wi-Fi 7 capable d’atteindre 1,5 Gbit/s en téléchargement.
Une Flybox Wi-Fi 7 pensée pour toute la maison
Pour profiter d’une connexion rapide à la maison sans passer par une installation fibre, Orange 5G+ Home coûte 42,99 € par mois, sans engagement. L’offre repose sur la nouvelle Flybox 5G+ et le réseau 5G+ de l’opérateur.
La box annonce jusqu’à 1,5 Gbit/s en téléchargement et 250 Mbit/s en envoi, à condition de se trouver dans une zone couverte en 5G+ et de disposer d’équipements compatibles. Des débits qui peuvent suffire largement pour le streaming, les téléchargements, les visioconférences ou encore le jeu en ligne.
| Orange 5G+ Home | Détails | 
|---|---|
| Prix | 42,99 €/mois | 
| Engagement | Sans engagement | 
| Débit max | Jusqu’à 1,5 Gbit/s | 
| Débit montant | Jusqu’à 250 Mbit/s | 
| Wi-Fi | Wi-Fi 7 | 
| Appareils connectés | Jusqu’à 128 | 
| Ethernet | 3 ports | 
| Frais d’activation | 29 € | 
| TV | Jusqu’à 200 chaînes via l’application Orange TV | 
Le principal intérêt de cette offre tient à sa simplicité. Il suffit de brancher la Flybox 5G+ pour créer son réseau Wi-Fi, sans rendez-vous d’installation. Orange annonce une couverture améliorée grâce à quatre antennes Wi-Fi et deux fois plus de récepteurs dédiés à la réception 5G+.
En plus, la connexion est annoncée comme illimitée. La box peut connecter jusqu’à 128 appareils simultanément en Wi-Fi et dispose de trois ports Ethernet. De quoi accueillir ordinateurs, smartphones, téléviseurs, consoles et autres équipements du foyer sans multiplier les installations.
À titre personnel, c’est surtout l’absence d’installation qui retient mon attention dans cette offre : poser une box, la brancher et retrouver immédiatement une connexion à la maison rend la formule assez différente d’un abonnement fixe classique.
Orange ajoute aussi la TV et une remise pour les 18-26 ans
La TV d’Orange complète l’offre avec jusqu’à 200 chaînes accessibles depuis l’application sur smartphone, tablette, PC ou Mac. Pour regarder les programmes directement sur un téléviseur, une option est proposée pour 5 € supplémentaires par mois.
Par ailleurs, les 18-26 ans peuvent bénéficier d’un tarif spécifique à 29,99 € par mois avec le code indiqué par Orange.
Il faut cependant tenir compte des conditions techniques : la 5G+ Home fonctionne uniquement en France métropolitaine, sous couverture 5G+ dans la bande 3,5 GHz. Les 29 € de frais d’activation sont également à prévoir.
Au final, Orange 5G+ Home s’adresse surtout aux foyers qui recherchent une connexion rapide sans installation fixe, avec le Wi-Fi 7, une enveloppe de débit élevée et une utilisation illimitée. L’absence d’engagement ajoute de la souplesse, tandis que le tarif réduit pour les 18-26 ans renforce l’intérêt de l’offre.

articles.title: La revolución del hogar conectado solo es posible con routers que van más allá del WiFi 7: así están dando un salto en 2026
articles.text:
Aunque son varios los operadores que ya han dado el salto al WiFi 7, siguen siendo más los que continúan anclados en el "pasado" con equipos WiFi 6 o WiFi 5. Por eso, y porque cada vez tenemos más dispositivos conectados en casa, hay mucha gente que decide cambiar el router de su operador por otro equipo más avanzado.
Ahí es donde entran fabricantes como Asus, TP-Link, Huawei o FRITZ!, que ya tienen en el mercado multitud de propuestas con WiFi 7 e incluso han presentado algún que otro modelo con WiFi 8. En la nueva generación de routers que nos está dejando 2026, la velocidad ultra rápida y la latencia ultra baja siguen siendo un punto a favor, sí, pero ya no es lo único en lo que saldremos ganando con el cambio.
La estabilidad de la conexión, la capacidad para conectar un número cada vez más grande de dispositivos, la posibilidad de crear una red en malla (mesh) y, por supuesto, las funciones avanzadas de seguridad, son otras prestaciones que debemos tener en cuenta a la hora de elegir el cerebro del hogar inteligente.
Velocidad sí, más ancho de banda también
Durante años, la velocidad en la subida/descarga de datos era lo que más importaba a la hora de mejorar la conexión a Internet en casa. La llegada del WiFi 7 con velocidades casi imposibles de aprovechar y una latencia prácticamente inapreciable parecía marcar la meta definitiva, pero a lo largo de este año hemos comprobado que hay otros factores igual o más importantes.
Ya no sólo necesitamos un router rápido y con una latencia mínima, ahora también tiene que ser capaz de mantener conectados simultáneamente un número cada vez mayor de dispositivos. Desde los móviles a los ordenadores y tablets pasando por la Smart TV, el robot aspirador, las cámaras de seguridad, los altavoces, la impresora, las bombillas... Hasta la lavadora, la nevera y los radiadores se conectan hoy en día al WiFi.
En un hogar donde cada vez hay más aparatos inteligentes, debemos tener un cerebro que no se sature cuando todos ellos estén conectados a la vez. Los routers más avanzados de Movistar y Digi, por ejemplo, sólo operan en las bandas de 2,4 GHz y 5 GHz, pero en el mercado ya existen alternativas tribanda que aprovechan también la de 6 GHz.
Además de tener más carriles, es importante que éstos sean más anchos para evitar un cuello de botella, de ahí que los nuevos equipos WiFi 7 dupliquen la capacidad del ancho de banda, pasando de los 160 MHz del WiFi 6 a los 320 MHz del WiFi 7. Aquí cobra especial relevancia la tecnología MLO (Multi-Link Operation), que permite agregar distintos canales de forma simultánea para transmitir paquetes de datos y garantizar una baja latencia al usar múltiples bandas al mismo tiempo.
Otro factor por el que destacan los últimos routers es la tecnología MU-MIMO (Multi-User, multiple input, multiple output), que permite transmitir datos a múltiples dispositivos simultáneamente en lugar de turnarse, y la tecnología OFDMA (Orthogonal Frequency-Division Multiple Access), que divide un mismo canal de radio en subcanales más pequeños para enviar datos a varios dispositivos dentro de un mismo paquete de transmisión.
Con todo ello, se logra reducir la latencia y evitar los microcortes en entornos con alta densidad de interferencias y dispositivos. Porque tan importante es que la conexión sea rápida, como que sea estable. Y ahí es donde, precisamente, van a incidir los futuros equipos WiFi 8 que empezaremos a ver en 2027.
Un idioma universal para una casa inteligente
Si has sufrido el problema de los "puentes" o hubs en la domótica, sabrás a qué nos referimos. Compras un altavoz inteligente y te toca instalar un aparatito adicional conectado al router; compras una bombilla y viene con otro aparatito; una persiana domotizada y otro más...
El cerebro de tu hogar inteligente debe ser capaz de mantener conectados cada vez más dispositivos y, al mismo tiempo, de poder entenderse con todos ellos sin necesidad de conectar aparatos adicionales.
Por eso los nuevos routers son compatibles con el estándar Matter, el idioma universal que usan marcas como Apple, Google, Amazon o Samsung, y que permite al router comunicarse directamente con cualquier bombilla, enchufe o altavoz inteligente, sin importar el fabricante ni el tipo de dispositivo.
Algunos modelos incluso pueden aplicar la Inteligencia Artificial para aprender los patrones de uso del hogar y priorizar la conexión entre todos esos dispositivos. Así, son capaces de detectar, por ejemplo, que estás en una reunión de trabajo, jugando online o descargando una actualización importante para dar prioridad absoluta a esa conexión de forma automática. Es lo que se conoce como QoS (Quality of Service).
Otros equipos, además, usan la tecnología beamforming para dirigir la señal WiFi hacia la posición exacta de cada dispositivo para mejorar el alcance. Y luego están los que, aprovechando las variaciones en las señales de radiofrecuencia, son capaces de detectar la presencia de una persona dentro de la vivienda sin necesidad de cámaras o sensores, e interpretar sus movimientos para encender luces, ajustar la climatización o activar alertas de intrusión.
Y la seguridad por encima de todo
Hoy en día, con tantos dispositivos IoT baratos conectados a la red del hogar, los protocolos normales de seguridad pueden ser insuficientes. El router tiene que "vigilarlos" a todos los aparatos para adelantarse a cualquier amenaza de seguridad y si detecta, por ejemplo, que una bombilla inteligente intenta conectarse a una página web extraña o enviar datos a otro país, debe aislarla del resto de tus dispositivos para que éstos no se vean afectados.
Como vemos, la velocidad importa, claro, pero hay muchos otros factores a tener en cuenta antes de decantarse por un nuevo router. La capacidad para conectar un número ingente de dispositivos sin saturarse y manteniendo una conexión estable y sin riesgos de seguridad es casi igual de importante, o más si cabe.
Y por supuesto, a la hora de elegir el mejor router del mercado también hay que mirar si ofrece soporte para redes mesh (o de malla), un buen número de puertos (mejor si hay alguno Multi-Gigabit 2.5G/10G, alguno combinado WAN/LAN y uno o varios USB) y funciones como control parental, creación de redes para invitados, cliente/servidor VPN integrado y actualizaciones de seguridad periódicas del fabricante. No es algo tan nuevo como el resto de tecnologías que hemos mencionado, pero sí resulta muy práctico en el día a día.
Sigue con nosotros el Camino a los Premios Xataka 2026
En noviembre celebraremos en Madrid la gala presencial de los Premios Xataka 2026, donde reconocemos los mejores dispositivos tecnológicos del año. Una de las categorías, el Premio de la Comunidad, la decidís solo vosotros.
Este es solo uno de los artículos con los que estamos repasando el estado de cada categoría antes de la gala. Podrás ver todos los artículos de la serie aquí a medida que los vayamos publicando estas semanas.
¿Qué dispositivo crees que debería ganar en la categoría de mejor router de 2026? Déjanos tu candidato en comentarios, comparte este artículo si te ha gustado y estate atento: pronto anunciaremos las votaciones oficiales, además de la fecha, lugar y cómo conseguir entradas.

articles.title: Partie de France, cette marque chinoise prépare son grand retour avec un smartphone pliant impressionnant
articles.text:
Si vous ne connaissez pas la marque Vivo, c’est un peu normal. Un temps implantée en France, elle a connu un départ précipité avant d’amorcer un retour à l’échelle globale. Un peu sur le modèle de ce qu’ont connu les marques chinoises du groupe OPlus avec Oppo, OnePlus et Realme. Ces trois dernières n’en ont pas fini avec les remous d’ailleurs et luttent encore pour trouver leur place.
Vivo, pour sa part, a mis un peu plus de temps pour retrouver ses forces sur le marché chinois, mais ça y est, le temps est venu de retourner à la conquête du monde. Et pas avec n’importe quel format : un smartphone pliant au petit nom de X Fold 6.
La marque vient juste de confirmer qu’elle annoncera prochainement une date de sortie internationale, sans préciser pour l’heure les marchés concernés. Nous ne savons donc pas pour l’heure si la France sera dans le lot.
Annoncé en juin, déjà dépassé ?
Il y a encore quelques mois, nous aurions pu nous contenter, pour décrire le Vivo X Fold 6, de dire de lui qu’il s’agit d’un smartphone pliant. Mais depuis son annonce en juin, la planète Tech a tourné très vite, et désormais, deux formats coexistent pour décrire les Fold. D’un côté, le format traditionnel, dans lequel s’inscrit ce X Fold 6, assez allongé et doté d’un écran plutôt carré à l’intérieur, et de l’autre, le format dit large ou passeport, porté par les Galaxy Z Fold 8 et iPhone Duo.
Résultat, le X Fold 6 a beau ne pas encore être commercialisé chez nous, même s’il finit par l’être, le modèle aura malheureusement un léger train de retard. En effet, le format passeport attire en ce moment à lui toute la lumière, avec de premiers retours de ventes très encourageants chez Samsung, et un engouement autour de l’iPhone Duo certain. Les analystes pensent d’ailleurs qu’avec ce modèle, Apple parviendra dès sa première année sur le marché des pliants à s’inviter à la deuxième place des ventes, malgré la présence de concurrents bien installés depuis une demi-décennie maintenant.
Au niveau des capacités techniques pures, pourtant, l’appareil est loin d’être dépassé. Il intègre une puce Dimensity 9500, la dernière en date, deux écrans 120 Hz, un capteur photo 200 Mpx, une grande batterie de 6900 mAh et une charge rapide à 80 W, sans oublier une étanchéité parfaite.

Na parte de software, o smartphone da Apple sai da caixa com o iOS 26 e deve receber ao menos cinco grandes atualizações do sistema operacional. Ele também traz conexões 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0, Ultra Wideband (UWB) e NFC.
O telefone é equipado com uma bateria de 3.692 mAh que, segundo a marca, tem autonomia de até 30 horas de reprodução de vídeo. Portanto, a dica é usar um adaptador de até 50 W, vendido separadamente, para um carregamento rápido que vai de 0 a 50% em apenas 20 minutos na tomada.
Por fim, o iPhone 17 (R$ 6.299 no Pix com o cupom INFLU300) possui estrutura de alumínio e acabamento traseiro em vidro com Ceramic Shield. Então, o certificado IP68 de resistência à água permite que o aparelho fique submerso por até 6 metros em água doce por 30 minutos.

articles.title: New Mexico Jury Finds Facebook Violated State Law 43.9 Million Times
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
	
	
	
New Mexico Jury Finds Facebook Violated State Law 43.9 Million Times
A New Mexico jury has found that Facebook violated the state's Unfair Practices Act 43,899,725 times, according to the New Mexico Department of Justice. The verdict came on September 25 in State of New Mexico v. Facebook, Inc., a case filed by the state's attorney general in 2021 over the Cambridge Analytica data scandal, following a two-week trial in Santa Fe. Per NMDOJ, the jury found that Facebook made false or misleading statements about how it collected, protected, shared, and used personal information, and about its handling of misinformation and hate speech. NMDOJ says the jury also found the statements willful, including those about Facebook's investigation of third-party apps after the Cambridge Analytica scandal. 
A Meta spokesperson said the company disagrees with the verdict and will continue to defend itself. Meta's lawyers acknowledged past mistakes during the trial but denied selling user data, Reuters reported. Here's the statement:
"Meta's platforms are forums for free expression. We have a First Amendment right to manage those platforms in a way we believe best serves the interests of our community. This means prioritizing free speech, protecting our users' information and giving them control over their data."
The verdict covers liability only. The judge will decide the penalty amount, and the law allows up to $5,000 per willful violation, which NMDOJ says could translate into billions of dollars. The state is also seeking injunctive relief and the maximum civil penalties, and the judge will schedule further proceedings. In March, a separate New Mexico jury ordered Meta to pay $375 million in an unrelated child safety case, according to NMDOJ.

articles.title: 'We don’t see AI as a replacement for human actors, and that isn’t the future we’re building toward' — Hollywood is betting big on AI movies just as audiences start turning against them
articles.text:
‘There is nothing like human’: Hollywood is betting big on AI movies — just as audiences are turning against them and looking for films made by real people
AI movies are attracting serious money — but audiences may be getting more suspicious of them
If you ever need a sign that AI is coming for Hollywood then it must be that Jeffrey Katzenberg, the veteran Hollywood executive who co-founded Dreamworks, has just announced that he’s launching an AI-focused studio.
Crucially, he told The Wrap that AI output was “slop” until very recently, but that in the last couple of months something has changed. Now he wants to make feature films and TV with AI, arguing that falling production costs will mean more films and new forms of storytelling.
At the same time The Gifted, an AI-generated trailer, has just won a competition that puts $2.5m towards turning it into a proper feature film. Future Vision XPRIZE is one of the world's largest film competitions for hopeful and optimistic science fiction filmmaking that answers the question: what does a future worth building actually look like?
You can watch the trailer for The Gifted here.
Unfortunately, the industry focus on AI seems to be happening at exactly the same time that the audience is being turned off by it.
Filmustage, a movie production planning platform, analyzed Google Trends data and found searches rising on both sides of the AI debate. It found that the phrase “movies with no AI” was up 345% in the past month, while “movies made with AI” was up 112% in the same period.
Google Trends percentage increases can often be massive, so we shouldn't read too much into the numbers themselves, but the overall trend is upwards. The motivations behind those searches may be very different, but both suggest audiences increasingly want to know one thing before they watch: was AI involved?
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
I don't think it's hard to understand why. You only have to look at an AI film to understand why people have reservations.
You can judge the trailer for The Gifted yourself, but while it may be a stunning technical achievement that AI has made this three-minute video, if I’m judging it as a movie trailer… then I don’t want to watch the movie.
The flaws are obvious. AI is clearly very good at spectacle: lightning, explosions, collapsing buildings and impossible camera angles. Not to mention lead characters who look almost like famous actors you know, but not quite. (Is that Amy Adams in The Gifted's poster? No, it's not quite Amy Adams.)
The harder test is whether it can sustain believable characters, performances and emotional continuity for two hours rather than three minutes. If it does, then it's going to need much better dialogue than what's presented here.
I remember watching the pure-AI film Hell Grind in a theater recently, and that just about kept my attention for its 90-minute duration, but I was ready for it to be over by the end. It also played to AI’s strengths, by not trying to make its world look ‘real’. It's when AI pretends to be real life that I think it falls down the most.
Pure AI films... still look like AI
Actors, perhaps seeing a future in which their skills are not as widely appreciated, are famously against AI, but even they seem to have accepted the overall trend towards it now.
As Deadline reports, Tom Cruise earned spontaneous applause for a six minute speech during a recent BAFTA “Life in Pictures” conversation in London. Cruise talked about how AI “is coming”, but “people want to see real things”.
“There is nothing like human” said Cruise, citing a summer of blockbuster films as proof that “people want human experience.”
From what I've seen of AI movies, I'd say Cruise is exactly right. AI still can't produce an experience that looks human and the connection to the audience that goes along with that. But with even Tom Cruise acknowledging that AI is coming, and executives like Katzenberg jumping on board, AI movies seem almost inevitable now, especially with the saving in production costs that they bring with them.
But while AI might be economical, it definitely has its problems, and if people are already searching for “movies with no AI” then Hollywood has a branding problem before the AI movie era has even properly begun.
AI as another tool for filmmakers
But perhaps before we assume that AI in films means the end to human actors and an influx of AI slop, let’s talk to one of the AI studios making waves at the moment, Utopai Studios, who creates original films and television series using their own proprietary PAI software.
I talked to Kevin Chong, Chief Commercial Officer at Utopai Studios.
“We don’t think of AI films as a separate genre”, explains Chong. “AI is another tool filmmakers can use to tell stories, just as visual effects, digital cinematography and virtual production became part of the filmmaking process. It can help filmmakers create worlds, achieve a level of scale that might otherwise be difficult or prohibitively expensive, and give creators more choices.”
And what about the end of human actors? “At Utopai Studios, we don’t see AI as a replacement for human actors, and that isn’t the future we’re building toward”, Chong explains. “There may be stories where a completely synthetic character makes sense creatively, just as animation has always created characters that don’t physically exist. But that is very different from saying audiences are going to stop wanting human performances.
“Performance is one of the most human parts of filmmaking”, Chong continues. “Actors bring interpretation, emotion, instinct and life experience to a character in ways that are fundamental to storytelling. AI can become another part of the filmmaking toolkit — including helping extend performances, create environments or enable things that would be difficult to achieve traditionally — but the creative decisions still need to come from people.”
Tom Cruise is right: there is nothing quite like human, but perhaps there will be a way for humans and AI to coexist in the future of movies after all.

articles.title: AI agents inadvertently leak 13,000+ internal screenshots from 300 organizations — list of companies includes Fortune 500 and a frontier AI lab
articles.text:
AI agents inadvertently leak 13,000+ internal screenshots from 300 organizations — list of companies includes Fortune 500 and a frontier AI lab
When agents are too clever for their own good.
There's a private information leak most days, usually by way of misconfigured services or nasty security bugs. Sometimes, though, users will readily hand over private information without being aware of it. That's the case for over 300 organizations, including several Fortune 500 companies and a frontier AI lab, who collectively had 13,000+ private screenshots exposed — all thanks to their development AI agents being arguably too good at their jobs and performing them with little human oversight.
Besides showing pictures of internal and pre-release software, the leaked screenshots reportedly include corporate and client information, financial data, and even screen recordings for a money-movement interface. The report, called PixelLeak, comes from endpoint security firm Glow, and it details how the leaks happened. The root cause is surprisingly simple and likely to induce a forehead slap.
It's become customary in development work related to UI and UX (and other categories) to include screenshots showing previews or before/after comparisons of tweaked features, for review purposes. Said images travel as attachments to the respective code changes, also known as "pull requests" (PRs) in dev parlance.
When using GitHub (and potentially other code repository services), humans see a graphical interface for easily attaching an image to a PR. Meanwhile, bots are limited to using the command-line interface, which currently does not have that feature available for private repositories.
As the efficient and smart agents they are, the clankers came up with a simple solution: publish the PR as usual to the private repository, and include an image placeholder linking to a file that's hosted in a public repository instead. There, problem fixed! The user is happy and likely has no idea what happened unless they notice the problem somehow and start asking the bot some hard questions.
Glow says that in about a third of the affected companies, developers were using gitshot, a command-line tool for attaching screenshots, used in this instance to overcome the aforementioned limitation. Searching for images attached by the tool is quite easy, as one needs but look for the "_gitshot" tag. The report also indicates that in 93% of cases, images were found in repositories under direct control of the developer's username, rather than being tied to the company's GitHub account.
In one particular case, an agent skill (essentially long-winded prompts instructing a bot how to do something) was also an indirect source of leaked information. The agents started incorporating the image hosting workaround as a skill, and after a while, many of them were using it for every development ticket, leading to leaks of information about features months away from public release.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Glow provided sample reasoning output from an agent, explaining precisely why it uploaded the screenshots publicly:
"internal_sweeper is private, and GitHub cannot render images from a private repo in a PR description — its image proxy fetches anonymously, so anything committed here (branch, release asset, whatever) shows up broken for reviewers. The only way to satisfy both "reviewers see the images" and "nothing but index.html in the repo" was to host the PNGs elsewhere, so I created a new public repo, sweeper-demo/pr-assets, holding the two screenshots pinned to a commit SHA."
As mitigation measures, Glow first recommends checking that employees don't use repositories under their own accounts, auditing the accounts and code managed by employees no longer associated with the company, and curtailing the use of "shadow AI" — when employees unadvisedly sign up for their own AI tools without talking to IT first and neatly punch planet-sized holes in the firm's security and data privacy.
Additionally, Glow advises strong vetting of software and code libraries used for development, as well as careful reading of the instructions and rules of any agentic skills.
