articles.title: Samsung lança tablets com bateria de até 23 horas • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Samsung lança tablets com bateria de até 23 horas
Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra e S12+ trazem chip Dimensity 9500, Android 17 e tela AMOLED.
Resumo
- Samsung apresentou globalmente os Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra e Galaxy Tab S12+.
- Os tablets usam o chip Dimensity 9500 e chegam com Android 17, One UI 9 e até 12 GB de RAM.
- As vendas começam em mercados selecionados em 7 de outubro; lançamento no Brasil ainda não foi confirmado.
A Samsung apresentou os Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra e Galaxy Tab S12 Plus, que pertencem à nova geração de tablets premium da marca sul-coreana. Os aparelhos chegam equipados com processador MediaTek Dimensity 9500, Android 17 com One UI 9, telas AMOLED de até 14,6 polegadas e bateria que promete até 23 horas de reprodução de vídeo.
O modelo maior mantém a tela AMOLED Dinâmico 2X de 14,6 polegadas, resolução de 2.960 x 1.848 pixels e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz. Já o Tab S12 Plus traz um painel de 12,6 polegadas com resolução de 2.800 x 1.752 pixels. Nos dois casos, o brilho máximo chega a 1.600 nits.
Ambos começam a ser vendidos em mercados selecionados em 7 de outubro, inicialmente na cor cinza. Segundo rumores, o anúncio no Brasil deve ocorrer na semana que vem. A Samsung ainda não informou os preços.
Como é o novo Galaxy Tab S12?
A nova geração utiliza o chip MediaTek Dimensity 9500, processador de 3 nanômetros apresentado em 2025. Segundo a Samsung, o Tab S12 Ultra oferece desempenho de NPU até 61% maior, CPU 19% mais rápida e GPU 17% superior em comparação ao Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra.
O Tab S12 Ultra tem bateria de 11.600 mAh e autonomia estimada em até 23 horas de reprodução de vídeo. No Tab S12 Plus, são 10.600 mAh e até 21 horas. Ambos suportam carregamento de 45 W. O modelo Ultra mede 5,1 mm de espessura, enquanto o S12 Plus tem 5,3 mm. Os tablets contam ainda com proteção IP68 contra água e poeira e acompanham a caneta S Pen.
A ficha técnica inclui ainda 12 GB de RAM, 512 GB de armazenamento e suporte a cartões microSD de até 2 TB. O Ultra oferece Wi-Fi 7, enquanto o S12 Plus fica com Wi-Fi 6E. Ambos utilizam Bluetooth 6.0.
Android 17, Galaxy AI e Photoshop
Os novos tablets saem de fábrica com Android 17 e One UI 9. A Samsung promete até sete atualizações do sistema operacional e sete anos de atualizações de segurança. Entre os recursos de inteligência artificial estão integração com Gemini, Bixby e Perplexity. A tela também pode ser dividida em até três áreas para executar aplicativos simultaneamente.
Outra novidade está na área de criação. O Adobe Photoshop virá pré-instalado nos Galaxy Tab S12 e terá suporte à S Pen e ferramentas de IA generativa do Firefly. A versão do Photoshop para tablets ficará disponível exclusivamente na Galaxy Store por pelo menos seis meses a partir de 7 de outubro.
Os compradores também terão quatro meses do Photoshop Premium para dispositivos móveis, enquanto aplicativos como Notability, Goodnotes, LumaFusion e Clip Studio Paint terão períodos gratuitos ou descontos, dependendo do mercado.
A nova linha sucede os Galaxy Tab S11 e S11 Ultra, apresentados em 2025 com foco similar em produtividade.

articles.title: Amazon lance un Fire TV Stick 4K plus rapide avec une télécommande Fire TV repensée
articles.text:
Amazon renouvelle son Fire TV Stick 4K avec une navigation annoncée plus rapide et une télécommande redessinée. Le modèle arrive aussi en France, mais son passage à Vega OS ferme la porte aux applications installées hors de la boutique Amazon.
Le Fire TV Stick 4K promet de vous conduire plus vite du démarrage à la lecture d’une vidéo. Pour chiffrer ce progrès, Amazon le compare toutefois à un stick concurrent de prix voisin, et non à l’ancien modèle de sa gamme.
Fire TV Stick 4K : jusqu’à 40 % de temps plus rapide selon Amazon
Du démarrage à la lecture, le nouveau stick serait environ 20 à 40 % plus rapide qu’un modèle 4K concurrent de tarif comparable. Amazon annonce aussi une ouverture des applications plus de 35 % plus rapide et un lancement des vidéos accéléré d’environ 20 %. Ces chiffres viennent du constructeur : ils ne disent pas ce que gagnera une personne qui remplace son Fire TV Stick actuel.
L’appareil conserve la définition 4K dans un boîtier aminci. Il embarque un processeur à quatre cœurs cadencé à 1,7 GHz, 8 Go de stockage et le Wi-Fi 6. Il prend en charge le HDR10+ et le codec AV1, mais pas le Dolby Vision, réservé dans cette gamme au Fire TV Stick 4K Max. L’alimentation peut passer par un câble USB branché au téléviseur, à condition que celui-ci dispose d’un port adapté.
Une touche personnalisable arrive sur la télécommande standard
La nouvelle télécommande adopte une forme asymétrique : le dessus est plat, tandis que le dessous est bombé et lesté pour aider à la saisir dans le bon sens. Amazon a également différencié les touches au toucher et doté le bouton d’accueil d’une surface métallique. Le changement vise un usage très ordinaire : retrouver les commandes sans quitter l’écran des yeux.
Une touche étoile programmable peut ouvrir votre application favorite ou activer un réglage, comme les sous-titres ou la loupe. Jusqu’ici, cette commande était réservée à une télécommande plus haut de gamme. Contrairement à ce que laissaient entendre les premières fuites, Amazon ne présente pas le bouton d’accueil de ce modèle comme rétroéclairé ; des touches éclairées sont annoncées pour une autre télécommande prévue l’an prochain. La nouvelle version fonctionne avec les appareils Fire TV sortis depuis 2019 et sera vendue séparément.
Vega OS élargit son catalogue, sans rouvrir l’installation hors boutique
Le stick fonctionne sous Vega OS. Amazon affirme avoir ajouté plus de 2 000 applications à son catalogue depuis le lancement du système, parmi lesquelles Spotify, Xbox, VLC et des services VPN. Ce choix a sa contrepartie : l’installation d’applications Android hors boutique n’est plus possible. Avant de remplacer un ancien appareil, mieux vaut donc vérifier que vos applications figurent dans l’Amazon Appstore.
Le nouveau Fire TV Stick 4K est disponible dès aujourd’hui en France à 74,99 €. Pour son lancement, Amazon le propose toutefois à 35,99 € pendant une durée limitée. La nouvelle télécommande peut également être précommandée séparément à 15,99 €, avec des premières expéditions prévues fin octobre. L’appareil donne aussi accès à la nouvelle interface Fire TV.
La télécommande peut améliorer le quotidien même sans changer de stick, puisqu’elle est compatible avec plusieurs anciens modèles. Pour le boîtier 4K, la décision dépendra davantage de vos applications : quelques secondes gagnées pèsent peu si celle que vous utilisez n’existe pas sous Vega OS.

articles.title: Japón planea operar 10 millones de robots con IA en 2040 para salvar su economía
articles.text:
El gobierno de Japón se propuso poner en funcionamiento 10 millones de robots impulsados por inteligencia artificial en centros de trabajo antes de 2040, con el objetivo de compensar la reducción acelerada de su fuerza laboral por el envejecimiento poblacional. Hospitales y fábricas ya enfrentan dificultades para cubrir puestos vacantes, lo que llevó a un número creciente de empleadores a recurrir a máquinas para tareas cotidianas.
Según las estimaciones de variante media de las Naciones Unidas, la población de Japón llegará a 112.158.304 personas en 2040, una cifra 6,2% inferior a los 119.584.122 habitantes proyectados para 2030. La edad mediana alcanzará los 54,0 años, con el 35,3% de la población en al menos 65 años y apenas el 10,4% por debajo de los 15 años.
PUBLICIDAD
Un robot humanoide para hospitales y comercios
La startup Zeals presentó en Tokio el D1, una máquina con ruedas y forma humanoide con un costo desde 5 millones de yenes (unos USD 32.000). La unidad, de uso interior, mide 129 centímetros de altura, reconoce rostros a través de una cámara y cada uno de sus dos brazos puede levantar un máximo de 5 kilogramos.
La compañía planea construir 100 unidades para marzo de 2027 y acumular 10.000 horas de funcionamiento, con ventas a través de distribuidores y socios de arrendamiento. Zeals desarrolla su propio software y compra componentes a proveedores estadounidenses y chinos, aunque su meta a futuro es utilizar exclusivamente piezas japonesas.
PUBLICIDAD
A finales de agosto de 2026, un hospital de Nagoya puso a prueba el robot para guiar visitantes y despejar mesas en su comedor. “Es importante recopilar datos de entrenamiento y asegurarse de que sea realmente útil en entornos del mundo real”, declaró Masahiro Shimizu, director ejecutivo de Zeals, a Japan Today.
Aprendizaje y colaboración con empleados
Kakuichi, una empresa de Nagano dedicada a la venta de acero y sistemas de gestión energética, sumará una máquina humanoide entre sus nuevos graduados en abril de 2027. Play Robotics, firma especializada en el estudio de humanoides, colabora con Kakuichi en la instalación y operación del robot de fabricación china llamado Miyazawa Noah.
PUBLICIDAD
Kakuichi tiene previsto asignar el robot a los departamentos de manufactura, ventas y otras áreas para que adquiera habilidades a través del trabajo real. “Desarrollar un robot humanoide también implica formar empleados que hagan pleno uso de él”, afirmó Riu Tanaka, director ejecutivo de Kakuichi.
Las aseguradoras se preparan para los riesgos de la robótica
Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance se asoció con Zeals para comercializar pólizas diseñadas para los usuarios del D1, con expectativas de demanda proveniente de hoteles, hospitales, fábricas y empresas de logística. La aseguradora reconoce que el uso de estos robots estará asociado a ciertos incidentes, tanto físicos como cibernéticos.
“Existen riesgos de causar daños a personas o bienes, así como preocupaciones sobre filtraciones de datos por ciberataques”, señaló Masaki Oshiro, gerente de la primera sucursal de la oficina de Tokio Este de la aseguradora.
PUBLICIDAD
En julio, Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance adquirió acciones de una empresa japonesa que desarrolla inteligencia artificial física, tecnología que permite a los robots aprender nuevas tareas de forma autónoma. La compra buscó darle a la aseguradora una visión más cercana del comportamiento de estos sistemas y de los posibles fallos que pueden presentar.
El hecho de que la firma invierta en un desarrollador mientras ya vende pólizas para estos equipos sugiere que aún evalúa cómo funcionan y con qué frecuencia fallan estas máquinas, mientras Japón avanza en su apuesta por robots para reforzar una fuerza laboral en retroceso.

articles.title: Ras-le-bol des bips agaçants au volant ? Ce constructeur a trouvé la parade idéale avec un simple bouton
articles.text:
Ah, qu’elle serait belle la vie sans ces alertes incessantes au volant ! Vous dépassez la vitesse d’un petit kilomètre-heure et vous voilà sévèrement réprimandé par votre véhicule. Visuellement, avec un panneau rouge clignotant sur l’instrumentation, mais aussi auditivement, avec un bip retentissant pendant une poignée de secondes. Pour éviter un excès de vitesse, c’est pratique. Pour rester zen sur sa conduite, un peu moins…
Car votre voiture peut aussi vous corriger sévèrement si vous vous approchez trop près d’une ligne blanche, qu’elle soit continue ou pas, d’ailleurs. Un petit coup de volant parasite pour vous remettre dans le droit chemin, ça vous dit ? Pas vraiment, et c’est la raison pour laquelle les marques rendent ces alertes désactivables. Mais là vient toute la subtilité : certaines imposent de passer à travers une ribambelle de menus, ce qui empire la chose.
La parade géniale de Dacia : le fameux « My Safety Switch »
Et puisqu’il faut tout désactiver à chaque démarrage, cela vire à la prise de tête. Quelle est donc la finalité de ces alarmes si elles imposent justement de quitter la route des yeux pour les court-circuiter ? C’est bien la question à mille euros que tout le monde se pose… Dacia en tout cas, semble y avoir trouvé une première réponse avec un système simplissime permettant d’avoir la paix en un clin d’œil.
Pas de technologie extraterrestre en vue, il ne s’agit que d’un bouton situé à gauche du poste de conduite. L’interrupteur My Safety Switch coupe toutes les aides en un appui double. Cela ne prend qu’une seconde chaque matin, ce qui fait la différence à la longue. Ce dispositif, également partagé avec Renault et Alpine, ne se contente pas de taire bêtement toutes les assistances. Il est personnalisable selon les préférences de chacun.
Pourquoi les clients en raffolent (et la concurrence commence à copier)
Si vous souhaitez par exemple garder l’aide au maintien dans la voie mais supprimer l’alerte de survitesse, il est parfaitement possible de le faire via le menu My Safety Perso. Cochez et décochez les différentes aides, et vous vous retrouvez ainsi avec une voiture configurée comme bon vous semble en un éclair. A ce jour, on n’a pas trouvé mieux comme système, qui est d’ailleurs le favori des clients Dacia.
Dans une interview accordée à Autocar, Katrin Adt, la PDG de Dacia, affirme effectivement que c’est ce « bouton magique » qui est le plus utilisé dans ses voitures. Pas le bouton pour allumer la radio, ni même pour désactiver le Stop&Start. Non. Un simple basculeur éteignant les aides à la conduite. Stellantis commence maintenant à s’en inspirer, même si la désactivation n’est pas encore personnalisable.

articles.title: El vídeo generado por IA es cada día más común. Por eso Apple sigue empeñada en hacer sus anuncios de forma totalmente artesanal
articles.text:
Una de las series de animación con más éxito de China ha sido generada íntegramente con IA. Hasta ese nivel han mejorado las capacidades de la IA en este tipo de contenidos. Sin embargo, Apple ha optado por otro camino para crear los últimos anuncios animados de sus productos: la creación casi artesanal de la mano de artistas humanos.
El mensaje ya no está en lo que dice el anuncio de forma explícita, sino que va mucho más allá y se posiciona en una idea que cada vez está calando más hondo entre los usuarios: el nuevo lujo es consumir contenido generado por humanos.
La IA es la nueva cadena de montaje. Seedance 2.0 sorprendió a Hollywood con clips de vídeo tan realistas que incluso el guionista de las películas de Deadpool, Rhett Reese reaccionó en su perfil de X asegurando que "Odio decirlo. Es probable que se haya acabado para nosotros". Generar un vídeo, sin plató ni animadores, ya es técnicamente posible, y más rentable para los estudios.
El público, sin embargo, percibe de otra forma el contenido generado por IA. Un buen ejemplo es el rechazo que provocó el anuncio navideño de Coca-Cola de 2025 hecho con IA. La protesta fue casi unánime y el público interpretó el uso de la IA como una pérdida de valor para un contenido con una carga cultural muy potente.
El diccionario Merriam-Webster eligió la palabra "slop" como palabra del año en 2025. La define como "contenido digital de baja calidad que se produce normalmente en cantidad por medio de inteligencia artificial". Es decir, se establece una relación directa (aunque sea de forma cognitiva) entre lo generado con IA y el contenido de baja calidad. Por mucho que, tras ese contenido generado con IA, haya mucho trabajo humano de supervisión.
Un prompt no tiene manos. El mensaje que Apple está transmitiendo a través de sus últimos vídeos de animación anunciando sus nuevos productos va por el otro lado. Les está diciendo a sus usuarios: "mirad, nosotros apreciamos el valor de la creatividad y del talento humano".
De hecho, incluso ha publicado un making of del anuncio de su servicio de juegos, en el que se ve cómo el equipo esculpió y pintó personajes y decorados reales. Después los animó fotograma a fotograma para crear el vídeo. No es una renuncia a la tecnología, es una apuesta por el valor añadido del talento humano frente a la "industrialización" y el carácter clónico de la IA. De hecho, la propia Apple admite que lo combinó con CGI, pero la base es física.
El reloj suizo como espejo. Una analogía de lo que pretende transmitir Apple con este mensaje y la percepción de los usuarios del contenido generado con IA la encontramos en los relojes suizos. Rolex o cualquier otro fabricante podría invertir una determinada cantidad de dinero en crear una cadena de montaje y fabricar miles de relojes al día.
Sin embargo, eso haría que su precio cayera en picado porque su auténtico valor no emana del coste de los materiales en los que están fabricados sus relojes, sino en el valor añadido que les aporta un proceso de fabricación artesanal y una producción limitada.
Este fenómeno no es algo nuevo, tal y como publicaban en The Conversation, en 1899, el economista y sociólogo estadounidense Thorstein Veblen ya estudiaba cómo el público asigna un valor a las cosas formulando su Teoría del consumo ostentoso. "Nos molesta la máquina porque sus creaciones no le cuestan nada", sostenía Veblen. Por eso ven la creación humana como "un bien artesanal" que el consumidor elige apoyar.
Apple vende esa idea. El último anuncio del Mac Mini, hecho con arcilla y la técnica stop motion, supuso nueve semanas de trabajo de todo un equipo de animadores. Lo único digital fue borrar soportes y limpiar detalles. Esa huella de esfuerzo humano importa. Según un estudio publicado en el Journal of Advertising Research, en el lujo la autenticidad depende del esfuerzo que el público percibe. Un anuncio generado por un prompt no deja esa misma huella.
Apple lleva tiempo insistiendo en ese detalle. Su vicepresidente de marketing, Tor Myhren, ya defendió en Cannes en 2025 que "el toque humano es nuestro superpoder". Su serie Pluribus cierra cada episodio con un aviso en los créditos: "Este programa fue hecho por humanos".
A medida que más y más contenido de vídeo y creativo se vaya industrializando mediante IA, el valor de lo "hecho a mano" cobrará más importancia. Apple ha presentado el making of de su último anuncio como prueba de que su apuesta es por el nuevo lujo del "hecho por talento humano".

The Witcher's Henry Cavill Will Build a Video Game on a Googlebook This November
Google has announced that actor Henry Cavill will build a video game on a Googlebook this November, as part of a marketing partnership for its new Android-based laptops. In its blog post, Google describes Cavill as an actor, producer, and tech enthusiast with his own production company and a passion for gaming and fantasy lore, and says he is already using the laptop for personal passion projects. "When Google reached out to me and explained what they are doing with Googlebook, and all of its new, integrated tools, it had me intrigued. Time and technology are marching forward at a breakneck pace, this, and all that Google are trying to do with it, has the whispers of the next generation."

articles.title: Windows 11 26H2 is rolling out, but it doesn't add anything new, it just turns on what was already there
articles.text:
The takeaway: Microsoft has officially released Windows 11 26H2 to the stable channel, rolling it out to all eligible users. The update is described as an "enablement package" that simply switches on dormant features delivered with previous monthly updates. It's a tiny 174 KB download for devices that are already up to date with all cumulative updates.
Windows will automatically notify you when the update becomes available for your device. If you'd rather not wait, open Settings, select Windows Update in the left pane, and turn on "Get the latest updates as soon as they're available." Then click "Check for updates" and hit "Download and install" if the update is offered for your PC. If you'd rather download the new ISO, download it here.
Microsoft calls version 26H2 a "predictable and low-disruption update" and insists it shouldn't raise any stability or compatibility concerns, since it shares the same underlying code as versions 25H2 and 24H2. All three are based on the Germanium release, which introduced fundamental changes to Windows 11, including deep optimization for ARM64 architecture and AI hardware.
Version 26H2 enables several dormant features across the Start menu, Taskbar, File Explorer, Windows Search, Gaming, Task Manager, and Networking. It also activates AI features in Settings, Task Manager, Narrator, and more, along with multiple personalization options, accessibility tools, productivity boosts, and security upgrades.
One of the biggest advantages of 26H2 is its improved support lifecycle. Despite sharing the same servicing branch as 24H2, the new version extends support for Windows 11 Home and Pro editions to October 2028, while devices running 25H2 and 24H2 will remain supported until October 2027 and October 2026, respectively.
For Windows 11 Enterprise and Education, support for 26H2 will run through October 2029, compared with October 2028 for 25H2 and October 2027 for 24H2. Windows 11 26H2 IoT Enterprise will also be supported until October 2029.
Earlier this year, Microsoft detailed how its Windows team has been prioritizing performance and stability over new features, following persistent complaints about crashes, compatibility issues, and sluggish performance.
According to CEO Satya Nadella, the company is trying to win back users by focusing on "core features and fundamentals that matter most to our customers."

articles.title: Use Graph RAG when relationships are part of the evidence
articles.text:
Use Graph RAG when relationships are part of the evidence
Which team owns the service that depends on the vulnerable library? Which customers use that service, and what does each customer’s contract require you to tell them?
A vector search can return the security advisory and service description, along with an ownership page or notification policy. Each result may be relevant. The answer may still lack the context needed to establish the correct relationship.
The missing evidence is in the connections. A particular version of the service uses the library. That service supports a particular customer environment. The contract in force for that customer defines a notification window. If the agent has to infer those relationships from a handful of similar passages, it may not have enough evidence to distinguish the relevant relationships from similar but unrelated ones.
“Use it when the relationships among facts are part of the evidence behind the answer.”
This is where Graph RAG justifies the additional work it requires. Use it when the relationships among facts are part of the evidence behind the answer. Keep vector retrieval because it remains very good at finding the documents and records that matter. Add a graph when similarity alone can’t prove why one fact applies to another.
Where vector retrieval works best
Vector retrieval finds text or records whose meaning is similar to a question, even when they use different words. A query about “ending a subscription” can find a support article about “account cancellation.” A question about memory eviction can find a paper that calls the same idea “context pruning.”
That makes vector search a good default for a large class of RAG applications. Documentation, support articles, product descriptions, and other unstructured knowledge often contain answers in one or two passages. The data is mostly text, the question has a limited scope, and the application doesn’t need to prove a path between several business records.
Similarity has a defined job in that design: rank likely evidence. It doesn’t establish ownership, dependency, authorization, or policy scope. Two records can be semantically close and have no operational connection. Another pair can be directly connected while sharing almost no language.
“A similarity score is an opinion about relevance, while a tenant boundary, effective date, or account identifier is a condition the system must enforce.”
This is why hard metadata constraints must be enforced independently of vector ranking. A similarity score is an opinion about relevance, while a tenant boundary, effective date, or account identifier is a condition the system must enforce. Relationships deserve the same distinction when the question depends on them.
Questions that depend on relationships
Questions about connected systems appear everywhere once an agent moves beyond a self-contained knowledge base:
- Which services depend on this component?
- Who can approve an exception for this account?
- Which customers are affected by this deployment?
- Which controls apply to the data in this environment?
Consider the vulnerability example. A package advisory identifies a library. A deployment record says a service uses that library. A service catalog connects the service to a customer environment. A contract record connects that customer to a notification policy. The answer requires four records and three relationships between them.
Text can describe every step, but an agent assembling the chain implicitly can join the vulnerable library to an unintended service version or associate a shared service with the wrong customer. It can also retrieve a policy that expired last month or miss a dependency updated in the service catalog after the documentation was published.
A graph makes those connections explicit by turning each record into a node. Typed, directed edges can record that a service USES a library or SUPPORTS an environment. A GOVERNED_BY edge ties the contract to the policy. Each connection carries its source and owner, with confidence scores or effective dates added when those details matter.
Start with the relationship types that answer an important question. Mapping the whole company is a long detour with no guarantee of a useful destination.
Graph RAG adds relationship evidence
Graph RAG is an overloaded term. Microsoft’s GraphRAG uses an LLM to extract a knowledge graph from unstructured text, builds a community hierarchy, and supports both corpus-level and entity-focused queries. This article means something narrower: a graph built from relationships your systems already record, where every edge traces to an operational source rather than being inferred from a model’s interpretation of the documents.
The approach combines content retrieval with traversal over known relationships. One practical flow begins by finding candidate entities and passages for the question. The application resolves those candidates to specific records, follows only the permitted relationships, and then retrieves the source documents needed to explain the result. That resolution step is the hardest part of the flow. A question about “the payments service” has to land on the right record when the catalog lists three services with similar names, and an incorrect match can affect every hop that follows. When the match is ambiguous, the application should surface the candidates rather than pick the closest name.
“The graph answers ‘What is connected?’ The source material answers ‘What does the policy say?’ You need both.”
The graph answers “What is connected?” The source material answers “What does the policy say?” You need both. A path from a customer to a contract does not contain the notification terms unless those terms are modeled there, and copying every paragraph into the graph creates another version of the truth to maintain.
Traversal also needs limits. Specify which edge types the request may follow, how many hops it can take, which tenant or account boundary applies, how current each connection must be, and what confidence is acceptable. Apply those limits as query and access constraints before the results reach the model, not as suggestions in the prompt.
Missing edges matter, too. If the service has no recorded owner, or two records disagree about which contract is active, the agent should report that condition. It should report that condition rather than infer a path between the available facts. “I can identify the affected service, but I can’t verify its current owner” is a useful answer. An unsupported conclusion during an incident can send notifications to the wrong customers.
The graph therefore needs an owner and a defined update path, just like the operational data behind it. Its access rules must also preserve enough provenance for an audit history. Otherwise, you risk presenting undocumented assumptions as authoritative-looking edges.
Keep the graph near operational data
Many relationships already exist in relational tables. A foreign key connects a service to a team. A deployment table connects a service version to an environment. An entitlement table connects a customer to a product. Copying those facts into a separate graph system creates update delays and another permission model. It also leaves an uncomfortable question during every investigation: Which copy is current?
Oracle AI Database can be a useful option when graph and vector search need to stay near the relational records they depend on. SQL property graphs can be defined over existing tables and views, then queried through GRAPH_TABLE. AI Vector Search can rank related text in the same database. This lets an application use graph patterns against current business data, then add semantic retrieval without turning every lookup into a reconciliation job across several stores.
The query itself is plain SQL. Finding every service that uses OpenSSL, along with the customer environments those services support, is a single pattern match:
SELECT *
FROM GRAPH_TABLE (ops_graph
  MATCH (lib IS library WHERE lib.name = 'openssl')
        <-[IS USES]- (svc IS service) -[IS SUPPORTS]-> (env IS customer_environment)
  COLUMNS (svc.name AS service_name, env.customer_id AS customer_id)
);
The decision rule matters more than the specific database. The platform should let the team inspect the exact path the agent used and trace each node and edge to its source, under the same access rules that protect the underlying records. If moving the relationships breaks those properties, the copy makes the answer harder to validate.
Choose Graph RAG for defined questions
Ask one question before adding a graph: Does the answer require joining facts across entities, following dependencies, or proving why one record applies to another?
Repeated multi-hop questions are a strong signal. So are decisions controlled by ownership, entitlements, dependencies, or policies. Incidents caused by missing or stale connections give an even clearer starting point because the consequences of an unsupported path are already understood.
A self-contained knowledge base probably doesn’t need Graph RAG. Neither does a workload where one document usually answers the question. And if no operational system owns the relationships, building a graph won’t fix the underlying data problem. It may only hide it behind a nicer query interface.
“Evaluate the path as carefully as the prose it produces, because a fluent response may not reveal an incomplete join.”
Pilot one decision instead. Impact analysis is a good candidate: given a component change, identify the affected services and customers, then cite the records that establish each connection. Entitlement-aware support is another: determine which product and policy apply to an account before retrieving the support guidance.
Use known source data and define success before building. Check whether the agent resolved the right entities and followed current relationships within the allowed boundary. Verify that the retrieved documents support the answer. Evaluate the path as carefully as the prose it produces, because a fluent response may not reveal an incomplete join.
Better context needs better evidence
A graph is useful only if it supplies evidence the agent cannot reliably retrieve in another way. Start with relationships people already use to make a decision, then prove that making those connections explicit improves the result.
Vector retrieval will still find the advisory and the contract language. The graph explains why they belong in the same answer. If the agent cannot show both the facts and the connections behind its conclusion, it should communicate the remaining uncertainty.

articles.title: TV TCL C6K com painel MiniLED de 55” cai quase R$ 1 mil no Magalu • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
TV TCL C6K com painel MiniLED de 55” cai quase R$ 1 mil no Magalu
TCL C6K traz painel QLED com tecnologia superior de iluminação e taxa de 144 Hz; TV 4K boa para jogos recebe desconto de 24% no Pix com cupom
A smart TV C6K de 55″ está saindo por R$ 3.024 no Pix com cupom INFLU300 no Magazine Luiza. O aparelho da TCL, com tela QLED 4K de tecnologia Mini LED e taxa de 144 Hz para jogos, recebe desconto de 24% sobre o preço original de R$ 3.999.
O painel QLED de resolução 4K da C6K conta com a tecnologia Mini LED, que oferece um melhor controle da iluminação de fundo, com 512 zonas independentes. Aliado ao HDR10+ que concede alto contraste, o televisor reproduz cores mais vivas e próximas da experiência de um OLED, sem o risco de burn-in.
Sua taxa de atualização variável elevada de até 144 Hz, número mínimo para o público gamer de PC, torna esse aparelho interessante para quem joga. O AMD FreeSync Premium Pro elimina efeitos de “tearing” e reduz bastante o input lag, melhorando em muito o desempenho durante sessões de jogatina.
O sistema operacional com Google Assistente integrado suporta comandos por voz e facilita o acesso a várias ações. O aparelho oferece acesso a vários apps de streaming como Netflix, Globoplay, Spotify e Apple TV, e também suporta jogos na nuvem por meio do Xbox Game Pass e Nvidia GeForce Now.
O sistema de som de 2.1 canais do televisor conta com um subwoofer integrado e potência de até 40 W. Além disso, conta com suporte a Dolby Atmos, oferecendo uma performance sonora acima da média para a categoria, com graves profundos e áudio 3D em séries, filmes, games e transmissões esportivas.
A smart TV TCL C6K de 55″ (R$ 3.024 no Pix com cupom INFLU300) traz duas portas HDMI 2.1 (144 Hz e 120 Hz), duas HDMI 2.0 (60 Hz), uma USB-A 3.0, uma LAN/Ethernet e uma saída de áudio digital. Por fim, possui conectividade a Bluetooth 5.4, Wi-Fi 5 e HDMI 2.1 (eARC e ARC).

articles.title: Data resiliency: how Oracle protects enterprise data - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Trusted data resiliency anchors Oracle’s ransomware defense strategy
For enterprises, data resiliency ultimately comes down to an ability for useful work to continue.
The definition sounds simple, yet making sure that data in critical systems is fully protected and accessible as rapidly as possible is a complicated task. This is the work behind Oracle Corp.’s resilient data architecture, which is driven by a combination of Oracle Exadata, built-in security offered by Oracle AI Database, and deeply ingrained data protection technologies enabled by Zero Data Loss Recovery Appliance.
“These days, with the advent of all these vicious ransomware attacks, we not only have to protect the production systems, we also have to protect the backup systems,” said Ashish Ray (pictured), senior vice president of Oracle Database, product management, at Oracle. “This means the backup systems by themselves have to be a different system, different levels of control, different ownerships, different network segregation. All of these have to happen at the same time, plus immutable backups, plus data encryption. All these technologies come together as part of Oracle’s resilient data architecture.”
Ray spoke with Dave Vellante at Oracle’s “AI Cyberattacks Are Escalating: How to Secure Your Data Now” event, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Oracle’s resilient data approach helps enterprises recover from attacks. (* Disclosure below.)
Trusted data resiliency
A key element in Oracle’s resilient architecture involves an ability to validate and restore data in its transactional state. Transactional assurances are taken care of at a deep granular level, according to Ray.
“When we talk about resilience, it has to be trusted resilience,” Ray told theCUBE. “It means you have to recover to a known valid transactional state, and that should lead to business outcomes. The beauty of all of these technologies is it can mark the state at a very granular point. You can go back to the granular point without any data loss. That’s what really trusted data resilience is.”
That level of precision also depends on knowing that backed-up data is actually usable when recovery is needed. Oracle’s Recovery Appliance validates backup integrity as data is ingested and continuously checks recoverability, helping identify corruption or missing recovery data before a restore becomes necessary.
“Data that is backed up but cannot be validated is Schrödinger’s data,” Ray said. “The data could be backed up, and you cannot rest on the laurels because the moment when you start trying to restore, recover the data and use it, you may find out that the data cannot be used because maybe there was some underlying validation checks, underlying corruptions that happen, the data could be compromised.”

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine reaches gameplay with KytyPS5 emulator — PS5 exclusive joins Ghost of Yotei in reaching gameplay, performance still in single digits
articles.text:
Marvel's Wolverine reaches gameplay with KytyPS5 emulator — PS5 exclusive joins Ghost of Yotei in reaching gameplay, performance still in single digits
Insomniac Games likely isn't working on a PC version of Marvel's Wolverine, but that might not stop PC gamers from playing it.
Insomniac Games' Marvel's Wolverine is the hot new PS5 game right now, but that's all it is — there's no PC version in the works, and given Sony's reported decision not to bring single-player games to PC, that seems unlikely to change anytime soon. However, that doesn't mean PC gamers are out in the cold after it was confirmed that an experimental PS5 emulator has been shown to be able to run the early portions Marvel's Wolverine, though only at single-digit frame rates.
While the KytyPS5 emulator was already able to start the game up, that was all it was able to do. That was great if you just wanted to be able to move around the game's menus, but it wasn't much use beyond a proof of concept. Now, things have progressed considerably, with VideoCardz pointing to an X social media post showing the emulator rendering the game's cinematics and gameplay.
The latest build of KytyPS5 can indeed play the game, but it does so at a single-digit frame rate. That's a long way short of making the action-packed title playable on anything other than a PS5 or PS5 Pro. But it's a start, and a much more promising one than was the case previously.
The frame rate situation probably says more about the emulator than the game itself. KytyPS5 is still very much in the early stages of its development, which means that issues are to be expected — especially for a title that has only been available for a few weeks. The emulator's developers are also focused on making it boot more games rather than making a handful work flawlessly, so it's unlikely it will be ready for prime time for a little while yet.
None of this is to detract from the work that has been done to get this point, though. The rapid progress that Marvel's Wolverine has seen is promising for the future of PS5 emulation on PC. KytyPS5 uses Vulkan 1.3 for its graphics output and uses an in-house system to decode the PS5's RDNA 2 GPU instructions. It's also available for both Windows and Linux right now, with an even more experimental version in the works for macOS.
This news also comes as another PS5 emulator has reached something of a milestone of its own. The developers behind SharpEmu, another experimental PS5 emulator, have been able to run a number of PS5 games at a playable 60 FPS. But even then, the success is modest —the developers only got six of 55 games to that point. A further six reached the point of gameplay, albeit at lower frame rates.

articles.title: 'The real prize isn’t just doing more work; it’s redesigning work': New report claims AI is being used more in the office, but it's creating more work for many
articles.text:
'The real prize isn’t just doing more work; it’s redesigning work': New report claims AI is being used more in the office, but it's creating more work for many
AI is fundamentally redesigning work
- AI usage is far from even when it comes to managers vs. regular workers
- Workers are facing more work or increased complexity due to AI
- Redesigning work is more important than upping quality or quantity
New PwC research has claimed 19% of UK workers now use AI every day at work, up from 15% last year, but despite some progression, there are still clearly some biases when it comes to who uses AI and how they use it.
For example, while 85% of senior execs and 73% of managers have used AI, only 35% of non-managers have used it.
But even if more knowledge workers were to use artificial intelligence as part of their daily routines, PwC argues that AI isn't actually making work any easier.
AI adoption isn't equal, but nor are its impacts
Even though employees claim AI has helped improve the quality of their work (70%), use more of their skills (63%) and bring value to the workplace (58%), the report actually argues that nearly half (44%) of workers have seen their workloads increase following the use of AI, with a similar number (45%) worried their job's complexity has also increased.
With this growing complexity in mind, PwC UK Chief Innovation and Technology Officer Claire Reid explained that employers and employees need to "rethink how work gets done" instead of just increase quality or quantity.
"The real prize isn’t just doing more work; it’s redesigning work so that people and AI together can deliver better outcomes," Reid summarized.
Still, the discrepancy in use among different levels of seniority is hard to ignore, and PwC could have the answer. Many fear negative consequences if they experiment with AI, are confused about their employer's policy or simply need more training. A clearer strategy and greater communication could be enough to change this and enable more workers (and therefore employees) to benefit from AI's more positive impacts.

articles.title: Jio IPO nears launch: DRHP filed, SEBI clears path
articles.text:
Jio IPO nears launch: DRHP filed, SEBI clears path
Reliance’s digital arm moves closer to listing with a Rs 37,700‑crore fresh issue; final price band and subscription dates expected soon.
One of the most anticipated IPOs in India is the Jio IPO. In 2019, at the AGM of Reliance Industries Limited, Mukesh Ambani, Managing Director of Reliance Industries, mentioned the company’s plans to list Jio separately within five ears. After gaining a considerable market share and expanding its portfolio over the recent years, Jio Platforms Limited filed its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI on June 19, 2026.
This upcoming IPO will give retail investors an opportunity to invest in one of the most interesting and modern businesses of the Reliance Group. Here is what investors should know about the Jio IPO.
What is the Jio IPO?
Jio Platforms Limited is the flagbearer for Reliance's digital connectivity and digital services businesses. Its key operating subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm, provides mobile, broadband and enterprise connectivity services across India. The business also has a presence in digital entertainment, cloud, artificial intelligence, and other digital services.
Jio IPO shall be a fresh issue of up to 27 crore equity shares with a face value of Rs 10 each. The final issue price will be determined through the book-building process.
As there is no Offer for Sale (OFS) component, no existing shareholders will be selling their shares, and the entire proceeds of the issue will go toward raising capital for the company.
Jio IPO Key Details
Particulars Details
Company Jio Platforms Limited
Promoter Reliance Industries Limited
IPO Type 100% Fresh Issue
Fresh Issue Up to 27 crore equity shares
Face Value Rs 10 per share
Proposed Listing On NSE and BSE
The issue size of the upcoming IPO of up to 27 crore equity shares represents approximately 2.9% of the post-issue share capital. Market reports have placed the potential issue size at around Rs 37,700 crore.
Jio IPO plan & timeline
- August 12, 2019: At Reliance Industries' 42nd AGM, Mukesh Ambani said the group planned to separately list Jio within five years.
- August 29, 2025: At the company's AGM, Jio's IPO was indicated for the first half of 2026, subject to the necessary regulatory approvals.
- June 19, 2026: Jio Platforms Limited filed its DRHP with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). The company had appointed 19 investment banks as Book Running Lead Managers (BRLMs) for the proposed IPO.
- August 28, 2026: SEBI issued its observation letter on Jio Platforms' DRHP, taking the IPO process to another regulatory stage.
- September 2026: The price band, subscription dates, anchor allocation, and listing timeline have not yet been announced. These details are expected closer to the IPO.
Jio's business ahead of the IPO
Jio enters the IPO process with a large customer base and an expanding digital business. At the end of FY26, Jio Platforms reported 524.4 million customers. Revenue from operations stood at about Rs 1.47 lakh crore, while its EBITDA was Rs 76,255 crore and Profit After Tax (PAT) was around Rs 30,049 crore.
The business has also been moving beyond traditional telecom offerings to also include fixed broadband, enterprise connectivity, cloud services, digital entertainment, IoT, and AI-related products.
What investors should know before applying?
The first point to watch is the valuation. The final price band will determine the valuation at which investors enter the company. A large IPO does not automatically mean an expensive or attractive valuation.
The second is debt reduction. A substantial part of the IPO proceeds is planned for repayment or prepayment of borrowings. Up to Rs 27,500 crore has been earmarked for this purpose.
The third is business concentration. Telecom remains an important part of Jio's operations. Investors should consider competition, pricing, subscriber growth, capital expenditure and regulatory changes along with the company's newer digital businesses.
Finally, investors should wait for the RHP and final IPO details before making an application. The price band, lot size, subscription dates and final issue size will provide a clearer picture of the public offering.
Conclusion
The Jio IPO has moved closer to launch with the filling of its DRHP and receipt of SEBI’s observation letter. With the final price band, issue size, and subscription dates still pending, investors should assess the company’s valuation, financial performance, proposed use of proceeds and business outlook before applying.

articles.title: Gemini 4 Argon s'attaque à ChatGPT et Claude : Google dévoile son IA la plus puissante
articles.text:
Google sort enfin l’artillerie lourde. Le géant de Mountain View a présenté Gemini 4 Argon, son nouveau modèle d’intelligence artificielle haut de gamme. C’est aussi et surtout le premier modèle de la famille Gemini 4. Il faudra s’armer de patience avant de pouvoir converser avec l’IA.
 Today we’re introducing Gemini 4 Argon.
It delivers frontier performance in complex workflows across real-world software engineering, knowledge work, and cybersecurity defense with an industry-leading 1M token output limit. pic.twitter.com/oDaCoOLu5E
— Google (@Google) September 30, 2026
Comme l’explique le géant américain, Argon est taillé pour les tâches longues, qui exigent de nombreuses étapes de réflexion. Argon a été « conçu pour assurer un raisonnement approfondi tout au long de flux de travail complexes et à long terme ». Selon Google, Argon peut produire jusqu’à 1 million de jetons en une seule réponse, contre 64 000 auparavant.
Sur les benchmarks mis en avant par Google, Argon devance Claude Opus 5.5 d’Anthropic et GPT-6 Astra d’OpenAI. En interne, Argon a d’ores et déjà fait ses preuves, précise Google. « Des milliers de Googlers soulignent les forces de ce modèle pour les tâches de codage spécialisées, la recherche approfondie et la qualité de la rédaction », assure Google. Une équipe d’agents animés par Argon a notamment appliqué des optimisations dans les centres de données de Google, « libérant ainsi plus de 300 Tio de mémoire », en toute autonomie.
À lire aussi : Chez Google, l’IA n’a jamais coûté aussi cher (et le moral n’a jamais été si bas)
Argon, l’arme de Google pour la cybersécurité
C’est néanmoins sur la cybersécurité que Google met le paquet. Selon l’entreprise de Mountain View, Argon est capable de « détecter, valider et corriger de manière autonome les vulnérabilités logicielles critiques ». Sur un test de correction de failles, le modèle se montre aussi performant que GPT-6 Astra. Au cours des tests, le modèle « a mis au jour une faille critique exposant des données personnelles sensibles dans un logiciel de santé utilisé par des hôpitaux du monde entier ». C’est un risque majeur « qui avait échappé aux modèles précédents », souligne Google.
 Lots of discussion out there about our next model(!), so I wanted to give an early look as soon as possible. Introducing Gemini 4 Argon!
It shows frontier performance in complex workflows, cyber defense and software engineering. Teams are using it extensively at Google, from… pic.twitter.com/sv4VNmQ0YT
— Sundar Pichai (@sundarpichai) September 30, 2026
Pour l’heure, Argon est uniquement « déployé auprès d’un groupe de spécialistes de la cybersécurité de confiance », par le biais d’un programme baptisé Fairwind. Google indique que « le déploiement sécurisé de fonctionnalités de pointe à ce niveau exige une approche progressive ». En miroir d’OpenAI et d’Anthropic, Google préfère offrir l’accès de son modèle de pointe à des sociétés triées sur le volet. Dans le cadre du programme, les spécialistes et les équipes internes de Google obtiennent un accès à une version d’Argon « sans aucune restriction de sécurité ». Pour Tulsee Doshi, responsable produit de Gemini, l’objectif est de mettre au plus vite un modèle puissant « dans les mains des défenseurs ».
À lire aussi : Google relance la bataille de l’IA avec 3 nouveaux modèles Gemini
L’IA la plus résistante de Google
Avant d’ouvrir les vannes au grand public, Google promet de renforcer les garde-fous de l’IA. Le modèle est d’ailleurs conçu pour « refuser les requêtes malveillantes tout en préservant la recherche scientifique légitime ». Selon Google, Argon serait aussi le modèle de Google le plus résistant aux « injections d’instructions », ces pièges qui permettent de manipuler une IA.
Pour éviter que l’IA n’aille au-delà des intentions de l’utilisateur, Google déploie aussi des restrictions « qui surveillent le raisonnement et les actions d’Argon et interrompent l’exécution si nécessaire ». Enfin, Google précise que les environnements de test sont isolés et scellés. L’annonce d’Argon tombe un jour après la signature par Sundar Pichai, PDG de Google, d’un accord sur la sécurité de l’IA avec Donald Trump et d’autres géants de la technologie.
Google évoque un déploiement dans un avenir proche, sans date précise. Sans surprise, les abonnés à Google AI Ultra seront les premiers à tester Argon. Avec l’arrivée de Gemini 4, Google cherche à rattraper le retard accumulé sur OpenAI et Anthropic, surtout en matière de cybersécurité. Promis pour juin dernier, Gemini 3.5 Pro a même fini par être abandonné par Google à cause de performances jugées décevantes.

articles.title: Rusia ha encontrado un arma para machacar Ucrania. El ingrediente secreto no es un misil: son 500 toneladas de fibra de carbono
articles.text:
En el frente de Donetsk, Ucrania ha empezado a organizar algunas operaciones como si la guerra tuviera dos turnos. Kiev intenta entregar a los robots las tareas que más vidas cuestan mientras Rusia prepara una industrialización todavía más gigantesca de la guerra no tripulada. Documentos internos de Rosatom revelan un proyecto para construir otros 28.000 drones de ataque anuales. Mientras Ucrania trata de sacar al soldado de algunos de los lugares más peligrosos del frente, Rusia multiplica las máquinas que hacen que esos lugares sean cada vez más peligrosos.
Turno de día y de noche. La lógica la explicaba en Insider el comandante Serhii Tischenko, del 96º Batallón de Apoyo del Tercer Cuerpo de Ejército ucraniano: de noche es mejor enviar los vehículos terrestres no tripulados porque al enemigo le cuesta más detectarlos. Durante el día resulta más práctico lanzar los asaltos porque los soldados pueden localizar con mayor facilidad los drones FPV rusos.
En la reciente Operación Vivaldi alrededor de Limán, esta división del trabajo ha permitido que los UGV entren primero para abrir caminos entre campos minados y que después avance la infantería. El robot no sustituye al soldado: trabaja antes que él para reducir las probabilidades de que encuentre una mina en el siguiente paso.
Dos semanas convertidas en dos días. La ventaja no consiste únicamente en alejar personas del peligro. Según el Tercer Cuerpo, un solo vehículo terrestre puede desplegar en dos días un campo minado de más de 400 metros de profundidad que a un equipo humano le llevaría unas dos semanas preparar.
Algunos de estos UGV sobre ruedas u orugas transportan hasta 400 kilos y Ucrania los combina con grandes hexacópteros capaces de sembrar hasta 40 minas antipersona en una salida y pequeños drones que lanzan cargas para despejar campos minados rusos. Durante Vivaldi, el 96º Batallón realizó estas operaciones a lo largo de unos 29 kilómetros del frente.
Volver “herido”. Detrás de toda esa automatización hay un recurso que Ucrania tiene muchos más problemas para reemplazar que una máquina: personas. Los UGV no se cansan, no pierden concentración durante una tarea repetitiva y pueden enviarse deliberadamente a lugares donde hacerlo con zapadores sería extremadamente peligroso.
Si uno pisa una mina o recibe un impacto, puede repararse o sustituirse. Tischenko resume así la doctrina que Kiev lleva año y medio intentando extender por sus fuerzas: es preferible gastar dinero en robots que arriesgar la vida de soldados. La cuestión, por tanto, ya apunta únicamente a qué puede hacer una máquina en combate, más bien apunta a qué tareas dejan de justificar que un ser humano se exponga para realizarlas.
Rusia y sus planes. Al otro lado del frente, Moscú está llevando esa misma revolución hacia una escala industrial diferente. Planes internos de Rosatom obtenidos por POLITICO describen la ampliación de la fábrica Alabuga-Volokno, en Tartaristán, para producir otras 500 toneladas anuales de fibra de carbono de grado aeroespacial antes de 2029.
No es baladí. Es un material ligero y resistente imprescindible para estructuras de los Geran rusos derivados del Shahed iraní. El experto David Albright calculaba que esa capacidad bastaría para fabricar los fuselajes de aproximadamente 28.000 Shahed-136 adicionales cada año, un incremento cercano al 78% respecto a los más de 36.000 drones kamikaze que Ucrania estima que Rusia puede producir actualmente.
Alabuga y dejar de depender de China. El proyecto revela, además, que Rusia no pretende limitarse a fabricar más drones: quiere controlar una parte mayor de su cadena de suministro. Moscú necesita actualmente importar materiales precursores para fabricar fibra de carbono de altas prestaciones y los documentos contemplan una nueva planta de PAN en el complejo industrial de Alabuga, precisamente para sustituir importaciones y abastecer sectores estratégicos como aviación y defensa.
El movimiento encaja en una ambición mucho mayor: Rusia pretende producir alrededor de 130.000 drones para su programa nacional de sistemas aéreos no tripulados en 2030 y elevar esa cifra hasta 350.000 en 2035. Alabuga es una de las piezas industriales que deben permitir semejante salto.
Cuándo se combate. Los dos movimientos en cada una de las aceras muestran hasta qué punto el dron ha dejado de ser un complemento para empezar a reorganizar la propia guerra. Rusia fabrica Geran cada vez más numerosos, rápidos y autónomos de componentes extranjeros. Ucrania responde introduciendo máquinas allí donde hasta hace poco necesariamente tenía que enviar personas.
En algunos sectores de Donetsk eso ya está produciendo una imagen que resume hacia dónde se dirige el frente: cuando oscurece salen los robots a preparar el terreno, y cuando vuelve la luz, los soldados intentan aprovechar el trabajo que hicieron durante la noche.
Así, cada máquina enviada primero significa una oportunidad menos de que sea una persona la que tenga que descubrir dónde está la siguiente mina.

articles.title: Revolut installe ses comptes en France, mais refuser le transfert impose de clôturer son compte
articles.text:
Revolut transférera les comptes de ses clients en France vers sa banque française du 2 au 5 décembre 2026. IBAN, cartes et paiements resteront inchangés, mais la garantie des dépôts passera sous régime français. Pour refuser le transfert, il faudra clôturer son compte.
Le transfert des comptes Revolut ne demande aucune démarche aux clients concernés. Il change pourtant l’établissement qui tient leur argent : leur compte quittera la succursale française de Revolut Bank UAB, banque établie en Lituanie, pour Revolut Bank S.A., la nouvelle banque française du groupe.
Le transfert des comptes Revolut change de banque, mais votre RIB ne bouge pas
L’opération est prévue entre le 2 et le 5 décembre 2026, d’après le courriel adressé aux clients et que nous avons également reçu. Elle fait suite à l’obtention, le 10 août, de la licence bancaire française de Revolut. Jusqu’ici, ses clients en France relevaient d’une banque lituanienne disposant d’une succursale dans l’Hexagone.
Pour les quelque 8 millions de clients que Revolut revendique en France, la distinction est surtout juridique. L’agrément bancaire français ouvre aussi la possibilité de proposer, à terme, d’autres produits, notamment des crédits et des livrets réglementés. Le transfert de décembre ne signifie pas qu’ils seront disponibles dès cette date, Revolut se garde de donner un calendrier précis pour le moment.
La banque en ligne indique que l’IBAN et le code BIC resteront identiques, tout comme les cartes et les fonctionnalités de l’application. Les prélèvements automatiques et les paiements programmés ne devraient donc pas nécessiter de mise à jour. L’établissement assure également que l’historique des transactions et les relevés resteront accessibles après la migration.
Le changement le plus tangible concerne la protection de l’argent déposé. Les dépôts éligibles relèveront du Fonds de garantie des dépôts et de résolution français, à la place du dispositif lituanien. Le plafond, lui, reste de 100 000 € : changer de fonds de garantie n’augmente pas le montant couvert.
Refuser le transfert revient à quitter Revolut
Le courriel ne présente pas de choix permettant de conserver son compte chez Revolut Bank UAB. Si un client ne souhaite pas passer à la banque française, la solution indiquée est de clôturer son compte. À l’inverse, accepter l’opération ne suppose aucune action de sa part. Le transfert sera réalisé automatiquement début décembre.
Sur le papier, rien ne bouge : même IBAN, même carte, même application. Seul le garant de vos dépôts change de nationalité. Reste une question que décembre ne tranchera pas : ces 8 millions de clients, transférés sans avoir rien demandé, feront-ils de Revolut leur banque principale, ou continueront-ils d’y voir un compte d’appoint, désormais domicilié à Paris ?

articles.title: SteelSeries brings ultra-wideband wireless to gaming mice, chasing lag-free tracking
articles.text:
Editor's take: SteelSeries keeps making gaming peripherals with hefty price tags. The Danish manufacturer has now launched redesigned versions of two popular rodents, bringing the ultra-wideband "revolution" to people looking to – in the company's own words – "keep beating kids" in online games.
After revealing its multi-platform luxury controller Aeon Pro, SteelSeries is now introducing yet another proposition for esports professionals or affluent multiplayer enthusiasts looking to get the most out of their frag sessions. The new Sensei Pro and Rival Pro gaming mice mark the 25th anniversary of the brand, providing high-performance wireless connectivity and other exclusive features.
The Sensei Pro and Rival Pro support ultra-wideband (UWB) technology, which should greatly improve signal stability during movement tracking. Ultra-wideband operates at much higher frequencies compared with traditional 2.4GHz mice, cutting through radio interference for a truly "lag-free" wireless gaming experience.
The new mice also feature an 8K polling rate, which should further reduce lag while improving stability and speed. The Sensei Pro is a symmetrical mouse built around 20-year-old design principles and should offer a comfortable "grip" for ambidextrous use. Meanwhile, the Rival Pro is an ergonomic rodent designed for a right-handed grip.
Additional features supported by both the Sensei Pro and Rival Pro include an "infinite" power system (IPS) with two separate batteries. Gamers can use one power source while the other is recharged inside the receiver. SteelSeries said that IPS technology can last for up to 120 hours (60 hours per battery) at a 1K polling rate, while battery life drops to 32 hours (16 hours per battery) at 8K.
Both the Sensei Pro and Rival Pro are available in black or white, with standard and "Mini" sizes offered for each color. All models come with a $180 price tag, with SteelSeries selling the mice directly through its online store. Meanwhile, third-party retailers should start selling the devices on October 13.
SteelSeries chose to introduce the "anniversary edition" of its Sensei Pro and Rival Pro mice with a cringey video clip about adult players who purchase premium pointing devices to beat kids in online shooters.
It's a strange flex no matter how you look at it, with SteelSeries ultimately declaring that if you still lose to kids with such a pricey, advanced mouse, you definitely "suck" at online gaming. Or maybe get a wired mouse for a fraction of the price and see how it goes.

articles.title: Intel Media Driver Gets "Crescent Island" Xe3P GPU Support
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Intel Media Driver Gets "Crescent Island" Xe3P GPU Support
Intel has added its highly anticipated "Crescent Island" Xe3P GPU IP as a supported platform to its Media Driver in the 2026Q3 release. This confirms that the company is working on bringing another GPU generation to the masses soon. With the Intel Media Driver 2026Q3, we learn that the GPU will support video acceleration as well. This means that video editing, video decoding and encoding, and processing will all be available on "Crescent Island," which we initially believed to be a GPU dedicated solely to AI inferencing. However, Intel will also power media processing workloads for workstations, and we expect to see similar features in video standards, like AV1 decode, as seen in "Panther Lake" and the upcoming "Nova Lake" with their respective integrated graphics.
If readers recall, Intel unveiled more details at Hot Chips 2026. Based on the Xe3P GPU IP, the graphics card is designed as a 350 W, air-cooled, PCIe format compatible with any configuration. The GPU itself features 32 Xe3P cores, 256 XMX engines, 32 MB of unified L2 cache, and 160 GB of LPDDR5X memory. This memory configuration is exclusive to Intel-branded "Crescent Island" graphics cards, while the company allows its ODMs to equip the card with up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X memory for maximum VRAM capacity.At Hot Chips 2026, we saw that the Xe3P silicon for "Crescent Island" has no graphics processing elements to output any imagery, as the silicon is designed purely for AI inference workloads that include long context, agentic tasks. However, now being part of the media kit, perhaps Intel sees this GPU as acceleration-only, dedicating 3D output to another GPU, or there may be a version with 3D graphics output. We have yet to see how many SKUs we will get with "Crescent Island," and whether any of them will include 3D video output capability.

articles.title: Novo Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K traz mais desempenho e melhora controle remoto • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Novo Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K traz mais desempenho e melhora controle remoto
Novo Fire TV Stick 4K já está em pré-venda no Brasil. Novidade chega com sistema operacional Vega OS e controle remoto com teclas mais táteis.
Depois de alguns vazamentos e rumores, a Amazon fez o anúncio oficial do novo Fire TV Stick 4K. A novidade promete ter inicialização mais rápida e traz um controle remoto redesenhado. O dispositivo foi anunciado para vários países, incluindo o Brasil. Por aqui, o preço sugerido é de R$ 579.
O novo Fire TV Stick 4K conta com um chip quad-core de 1,7 GHz (modelo ainda não revelado) e com 8 GB de capacidade de armazenamento. No quesito conectividade, há suporte para Wi-Fi 6 e Bluetooth 5.3, além de uma porta HDMI.
Assim como o Amazon Fire TV Stick HD, anunciado em maio, a versão 4K pode ser alimentada apenas pela porta USB da TV ou do monitor, dispensando a sua conexão a uma tomada, ao contrário dos modelos anteriores.
Em termos de desempenho, a Amazon afirma que o Fire TV Stick 4K é até 40% mais rápido do que o modelo equivalente de uma marca rival (presumo que a empresa esteja falando da Roku) e, com relação à geração anterior, é 35% mais ágil na abertura de aplicativos, além de ter 20% mais desempenho na reprodução de conteúdo.
Como o próprio nome deixa claro, o principal atributo do dispositivo é a sua capacidade de reproduzir vídeos em 4K, desde que a TV ou monitor seja compatível com essa resolução, é claro. Também há suporte para padrões como HDR10, HDR10+, HLG, H.265, H.264, VP9 e AV1.
Já o sistema operacional é o Vega OS, da própria Amazon. Ao contrário do antecessor Fire OS, esse sistema não é baseado no Android, mas suporta aplicativos de diversas plataformas de streaming, como Netflix, YouTube, Globoplay, Apple TV e, obviamente, Amazon Prime Video. Também há suporte para a Alexa+, como não poderia deixar de ser.
O Fire TV Stick 4K também renova o controle remoto. O acessório agora tem uma borda reta na parte superior, enquanto a inferior é bastante curvada. Porém, a característica mais notável, segundo a Amazon, está no fato de o controle ter sido projetado para ter botões mais táteis, de modo que o usuário consiga usá-los sem olhar para o dispositivo.
A tecla de início, por ser a mais pressionada, ganhou uma superfície metálica que facilita a sua localização via toque. Também há um botão “estrela” que pode ser configurado pelo usuário para abrir seu aplicativo favorito, embora teclas que levem a plataformas específicas (como Netflix e Prime Video) continuem por lá.
No Brasil, o novo Fire TV Stick 4K tem preço oficial de R$ 579 (sem considerar descontos ou promoções). O dispositivo já está em pré-venda no site da Amazon.
As entregas estão previstas para começar em 2 de novembro de 2026, embora possam ser efetuadas antes para determinadas localidades.

articles.title: Cómo evitar que los hackers roben tu cuenta de IA y tengan acceso a tus datos confidenciales
articles.text:
Los ciberdelincuentes ya no necesitan robar una contraseña para tomar el control de una cuenta de inteligencia artificial. Un nuevo tipo de ataque permite secuestrar sesiones activas en servicios como Claude y ChatGPT, sin superar la autenticación en dos pasos ni conocer las credenciales originales. Según un informe de la firma de ciberseguridad ESET, esta tendencia ya afectó a usuarios del asistente desarrollado por Anthropic, y un análisis de SOCRadar detectó 482 empresas con cuentas de IA expuestas en los últimos 90 días.
El robo de cookies y tokens reemplaza al robo de contraseñas
Cuando un usuario inicia sesión en una herramienta de IA, el servicio genera identificadores como cookies o tokens de sesión que evitan tener que introducir la contraseña en cada acceso. Programas maliciosos conocidos como infostealers pueden extraer esa información de un ordenador infectado, ya sea Windows o Mac.
PUBLICIDAD
Con esos datos en su poder, los atacantes reutilizan los identificadores para acceder a la cuenta haciéndose pasar por su propietario. Como el sistema reconoce una sesión ya autenticada, no siempre vuelve a pedir la contraseña ni el código de verificación en dos pasos.
“Una cookie robada es una sesión activa”, señaló el investigador de Okta Jeremy Kirk en declaraciones recogidas por SOCRadar. “Los ciberdelincuentes buscan específicamente los tokens de sesión y las claves API porque a menudo es posible reutilizar esos secretos y eludir la autenticación basada en credenciales”, agregó. Cambiar la contraseña, en estos casos, no sirve de nada: el intruso permanece conectado.
PUBLICIDAD
ChatGPT concentra el 90% de las cuentas corporativas expuestas
El análisis de SOCRadar sobre registros de robo de datos de los últimos 90 días identificó 5.434 registros vinculados a 1.500 direcciones de correo corporativas distintas. De las 482 empresas afectadas, 295 aparecieron en registros activos durante ese período, lo que indica que la exposición es reciente.
Una sesión de ChatGPT u OpenAI apareció en 358 de esas empresas, alrededor del 90% del total analizado. Otras plataformas como Zapier, Notion, Hugging Face, Replit, Lovable y ElevenLabs quedaron muy por detrás. Esto no señala necesariamente una falla de seguridad de OpenAI, sino un patrón de uso: muchos empleados se registran con su correo corporativo desde dispositivos personales, al margen de las políticas internas de sus empresas.
PUBLICIDAD
Claude y Gemini apenas figuran en esos datos, lo que SOCRadar interpreta como una señal de “IA oculta” y no como prueba de mayor seguridad. Anthropic lo confirmó a fines de agosto, cuando un malware comenzó a secuestrar sesiones de Claude para agotar cuotas de uso pagado, lo que obligó a la compañía a cerrar sesiones de forma masiva y emitir reembolsos por fraude. Los usuarios lo notaron en Reddit cuando sus límites de uso “se recargaron y luego se agotaron” de la noche a la mañana.
Las claves API alimentan un mercado clandestino
Durante julio, agosto y septiembre de 2026, foros clandestinos ofrecieron abiertamente claves API de Claude, cookies de cuentas Pro de ChatGPT y sesiones de Cursor, en algunos casos con garantía de reembolso. Esta práctica, conocida como LLMjacking, consiste en robar claves guardadas en notas o archivos de configuración para ejecutar cargas de trabajo de IA a costa de la víctima, que termina pagando la factura mientras el atacante obtiene la potencia de cálculo.
PUBLICIDAD
El riesgo se agrava con las plataformas de automatización: una sesión robada de Zapier otorga autorización permanente para acceder a sistemas de CRM, correo electrónico y almacenamiento de archivos, lo que permite a un atacante crear flujos de trabajo que extraigan datos de forma programada sin necesidad de robar credenciales adicionales.
Por sector, las empresas tecnológicas concentran el mayor número de casos, con 144 compañías y el 40% de los registros totales, aunque los sectores financiero, sanitario, industrial, minorista y energético también presentan una exposición significativa.
Las medidas recomendadas para proteger las cuentas
El historial de conversaciones dentro de una cuenta comprometida representa un riesgo adicional: empleados suelen pegar código fuente, datos de clientes y contratos en las indicaciones de la IA, información a la que un atacante accede directamente sin necesidad de vulnerar los sistemas internos de la empresa.
PUBLICIDAD
Entre los controles recomendados figuran implementar el inicio de sesión único en las plataformas de IA, usar sesiones de corta duración con rotación de tokens, limitar y rotar periódicamente las claves API, e identificar accesos desde ubicaciones inusuales o fuera del horario laboral. El informe también sugiere tratar la aparición de un empleado en un registro de robo de datos como un incidente de seguridad de punto final, y no como un simple restablecimiento de contraseña, además de identificar primero las cuentas de IA ocultas dentro de la organización.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Token economics reshape AI infrastructure - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
CoreWeave expands its AI stack as inference surges: theCUBE’s Fully Connected keynote analysis
Token economics are becoming a defining measure of artificial intelligence infrastructure efficiency.
As AI workloads move beyond training, the economics of producing useful intelligence are starting to shape infrastructure decisions. CoreWeave is building around that shift, expanding beyond GPU compute into networking, storage and software while inference demand grows faster than training. That transition is changing how customers weigh capacity, utilization and the cost of producing tokens at scale, according to Dave Vellante (pictured, left), chief analyst at theCUBE Research.
“Today they’re at 50/50, and they expect to be 10/90 by next year,” Vellante said. “Both curves are growing. If you look at CoreWeave’s numbers, they’re off the charts.”
Vellante spoke with Executive Analyst John Furrier (right) as a part of the keynote analysis at the Fully Connected event, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how inference growth and system-level optimization are changing the economics of AI infrastructure. (* Disclosure below.)
Token economics shift the infrastructure equation
The shift toward inference puts more emphasis on how efficiently an entire AI system can turn compute into usable output. That favors architectures optimized across silicon, networking, storage and software rather than around a single component. That transition is a move toward system-level performance, Furrier explained.
“If that shift happens, these data centers will look a lot different with the game still the same,” he said. “Pump out as many tokens per watt as possible. Get the intelligence shipping. You got the perfect storm on the supplier side with Dell, ecosystems booming and CoreWeave in pole position.”
The commercial implications extend beyond performance. CoreWeave’s customers are also pushing for shorter contracts, spot pricing and on-demand access, Vellante noted. Those models carry higher prices than long-term take-or-pay agreements, suggesting that flexibility itself is becoming part of the economics surrounding AI capacity.
“The prices for those types of structures are much, much higher, and people are willing to pay,” Vellante said. “It’s going to be really interesting to see as that 98% starts to go down toward 50/50, how that’s going to sort of affect the market.”
CoreWeave builds beyond GPU capacity
GPU availability may bring customers to CoreWeave, but the company is broadening its stack to keep them there. Its strategy now includes networking, storage and a software layer built around observability, security and continuous improvement, giving it more control over the infrastructure surrounding AI workloads, Vellante added.
“What you’re seeing CoreWeave do strategically is they’re expanding out beyond compute,” he said. “They’ve got networking; they’ve got storage. They announced [CoreWeave] Forge today … they’ve got this software layer, which is observability. They’ve got security in there. They’ve got this closed-loop system between evaluation, observation, runtime curating … that’s sort of how they’re saying their software layer is now intact.”
That broader systems approach also reinforces CoreWeave’s relationship with Nvidia Corp. That silicon remains critical, but commercial advantage increasingly depends on how efficiently the full infrastructure stack turns those resources into useful tokens, Furrier explained. That makes hardware availability only one part of a larger performance equation.
“This is becoming increasingly a systems game; it’s a systems race,” he said. “Silicon matters enormously. What’s useful commercially is how quickly the entire system turns into useful tokens. At the end of the day, that’s the key.”
