articles.title: Galaxy Buds On? Right on! Samsung's first ever clip-on open earbuds have been unveiled
articles.text:
Samsung finally announces its first ever clip-on open earbuds, with a neat Galaxy Buds 4 feature… but you can't buy them yet
Samsung Galaxy Buds On aren't 'on' sale right now
- Samsung unveils its first ever ear-cuff style buds, Galaxy Buds On
- Clip-on, C-bridge style open earbuds with head gestures and other features
- Only announced for Korean market for now, global launch TBC
We've been hearing leaks about new open earbuds from Samsung for months now, but I'm going to have to find a new rumored product to speculate about, because the brand has finally unveiled these new buds. Behold! The Samsung Galaxy Buds On.
This is the brand's long-awaited attempt to attack the best open earbuds market, and it's great timing, because recent figures show it's a booming sector. These are earbuds which don't block your ear canal, letting you hear your surroundings. Originally, they were targeted at outdoor runners and cyclists, but now I see them used all the time by couriers, drivers and commuters.
That said, the Samsung Galaxy Buds On can only be used by buyers in Korea right now, because the earbuds have only been confirmed for the sole market. According to the brand, they'll be released in other markets later, but there are no specific release dates just yet.
The buds will go on sale on October 27, for 299,000 won, which converts to around $220 / £170 / AU$320. For a little speculation mixed with a dash of context, that's roughly half-way between the Korean price of the Galaxy Buds 4 and Galaxy Buds 4 Pro, so I'd expect them to land for somewhere around $200 / £190 / AU$350 if we're going half-way between the prices in each region.
Let's get (Samsung Galaxy Buds) On with it
Enough price guessing: what's going on with these earbuds? Well, from the outside, they come in a case very similar-looking to the Galaxy Buds 4 models, with a clear top, and I appreciate the shared design bone.
Otherwise, they look like pretty standard open earbuds, with a bud and counterweight joined by an arch. Unlike many other brands which release clip-style buds, Samsung hasn't spent ages waxing lyrical about the design of the arch, simply describing how it analysed different ear shapes to make sure the speaker and battery were balanced well.
Audio-wise? Again, we've got little, but apparently they'll use something called 'TwinBoost speakers' which sounds more like car technology you'd hear bragged about in F1. That implies there are dual drivers per bud, but we'll have to wait to see to find out.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
What Samsung has described, in detail, is the range of features the Galaxy Buds On will get. There's an audio leakage avoidance tech, like in the Xiaomi OpenWear Stereo Pro, so people nearby won't hear that you're listening to the Runescape Soundfont cover of Pink Pony Club while you're on a run. There are touch controls on the counterweight but also head gestures and voice command functionality, as in the Galaxy Buds 4 models.
If you own a Samsung Galaxy phone, you can use the buds with Galaxy AI, and enjoy a fast-pairing mode too. The battery life of the buds is said to be 9.5 hours, which is much better than the other recent Galaxy Bud models too.
Samsung has confirmed that it'll reveal more about the Galaxy Buds On when their Korean official release date lands on October 27, so we'll have a better idea then. We'll also let you know when we find out about an international release date.

articles.title: Xbox Disc to Digital feature rolls out to all Xbox players to enable playing disc-free, but selling your media revokes access — hybrid physical media plan lands as Sony phases out discs by 2028
articles.text:
Xbox Disc to Digital feature rolls out to all Xbox players to enable playing disc-free, but selling your media revokes access — hybrid physical media plan lands as Sony phases out discs by 2028
This is a quality-of-life feature and not designed for game preservation, though.
All Xbox gamers can now get digital versions of their game library with the rollout of the Disc to Digital feature, which allows them to secure a digital license for the game tied to the physical media and associated with their Xbox profile. The gaming company said on X that players on Xbox Series X and Xbox One could take advantage of this licensing program, allowing them to play their games without needing to insert the disc into the console.
Xbox has been experimenting with a feature that would let you digitize your physical game library since early July of this year, with the company rolling it out to Xbox Insiders first in late August. Now that Disc to Digital licensing is available to all Xbox users, gamers with extensive physical game libraries could get digital licenses for their titles, allowing them to install and play those games on Xbox consoles where they’re logged in. However, Microsoft says not all Xbox One and Xbox Series X titles are eligible for this feature, and that eligibility may change over time. The company said that this could be due to changes in technical factors, licensing, publishing rights, manufacturing, and more. You also need to have access to the qualifying disc to retain the digital license — if you lose, sell, or give away the eligible title, your digital license may be limited or revoked.
While this move is more of a quality-of-life feature than a full game preservation strategy, it still gives hope to gamers who prefer the “ownership” of physical games on discs over the licenses you get when buying them online. This is especially crucial after Sony announced that it will kill the PlayStation disc by 2028. This decision received a lot of criticism, with a Change.org petition to reverse the decision reaching more than 200,000 signatures a week after the company made the announcement. Despite that, it has doubled down on the decision, saying that it will move forward cautiously and stop manufacturing physical media for new releases by January 2028.
While Sony is moving towards a disc-less future, it seems that Xbox is choosing a hybrid path that allows gamers to own their physical games while still giving them the convenience of having a copy of the title in their digital library without requiring another purchase. Former Xbox CEO Phil Spencer said a couple of years ago that it won’t abandon physical media despite the success of Game Pass, and this move shows its commitment to the promise, even if Spencer has since retired.

articles.title: Emergence AI Targets Fabless Chipmakers With Neuroformal AI - EE Times
articles.text:
Emergence AI said it is moving its neuroformal AI technology into active deployments with fabless semiconductor companies, while integrated device manufacturers (IDMs) among its customers are asking the company to extend the work into the fab.
The startup also targets the data generated during manufacturing to identify early signs of degradation before a problem affects a large number of wafers.
In an interview with EE Times at SEMICON India 2026, Satya Nitta, co-founder and executive chairman of Emergence AI, said, “You cannot make chips any faster, but what you can do is definitely get more chips per wafer yielding with AI.”
Nitta said demand for chips exceeds supply and every fab is running at capacity, so more wafers cannot be pushed through. The way to ease the shortage is to get more chips per wafer yielding, which requires analyzing the data, he said.
Nitta said neuroformal AI pairs the creativity of large language models (LLMs) with the discipline of symbolic AI, an older approach based on formal rules that was “all of AI” before the deep learning era. “Algorithms propose, and symbolic AI verifies,” he said. The aim is to develop AI that gives “provably correct” answers that engineers can depend on for mission-critical problems, because LLMs are probabilistic.
Nitta became executive chairman and chief scientist about a month ago, when Emergence AI appointed Ian Eslick as CEO, according to a LinkedIn post by Nitta. He said he will lead the company’s long-term research agenda, advance neuroformal AI, and deepen key partnerships, while Eslick leads the company through its next stage of commercialization and scale.
Eslick founded Silicon Spice, an MIT spinout that Broadcom acquired for $1.2 billion, and later led major technology initiatives at U.S. Bank and SoFi, according to the post.
Fabless companies and yield analysis
Nitta said Emergence AI started with the fabless part of the semiconductor value chain. Fabless companies design the product but do not control the manufacturing process, he said. They have data on the chip itself, such as functional, parametric, and overall yield, but not on what happens in the fab.
He said the analysis can show whether a yield excursion stems from a process issue in the fab, a design issue, or a test issue. “Wafer and final test issues are not uncommon,” he said. “The probe cards do not make perfect contact. I may have to retest it.”
He said AI agents can analyze this data at scale and remember patterns seen across products. As an example, he described an agent that finds the same pattern across 30% of 1,500 products, with failures in a ring oscillator block, and suggests redesigning that block. “These are the kinds of things that AI agents can do that are beyond human cognitive limits,” he said.
Nitta said the company’s domain-specific agents also carry out root-cause analysis. They have to distinguish a spurious correlation from the actual cause, using an understanding of device physics.
Asked whether the company competes with today’s LLMs and GPTs, Nitta said, “I would not say directly competing. We are saying that the LLMs are necessary but not sufficient.” He also said LLM-based AI is “useful but incomplete for mission-critical problems.”
Physics-driven failures in advanced packaging
Nitta said the company is beginning to move into advanced packaging. Because many packaging technologies are still being developed, he said, the question is less about what went wrong in the process and more about fundamental root causes.
One example is a coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch. “It is much more a physics problem,” he said.
He said AI agents would need to run finite-element and multiscale physics simulations to show, for example, that a liner material and copper are incompatible, or that a glass substrate and copper have a large CTE mismatch, causing things to fall apart in thermal cycling. He said that if the via were redesigned, the aspect ratio changed, or the liner thickness increased, “the process window is more mature.”
Nitta said Emergence AI is in active discussions with several advanced packaging companies that could lead to memoranda of understanding. He said he expects several announcements about these engagements in the next two to three months. The company has no active engagements with semiconductor tooling companies, he said.
Nitta said some of the fabless customers are IDMs, which have “both the fabless component and fabs.” The work starts in the fabless part, he said, and the IDMs are now asking the company to work in the fab. The work in the fab is “still at a very early stage,” he added.
Some of the fabless customers are among the largest companies in the industry but he could not name them on the record.
India: focus, talent, and open-source
In India, the company’s focus is limited to semiconductors, Nitta said. Emergence AI is primarily working post-tape-out and is not currently involved in chip design, though that could change in the future. He said verification is one of the longest steps in chip design and that neuroformal AI can accelerate the process.
The company is also talking with several potential Indian customers, but Nitta said he could not name them. “We are in the middle of several discussions,” he said.
Nitta said Emergence AI intends to grow its talent pool to 500 engineers and R&D scientists within two years. EE Times had earlier reported a timeframe of three to four years.
This summer, the company conducted a summer school on Lean, an open-source programming language and proof assistant, for more than 150 students, under the guidance of professor Siddharth Gadgil, chief scientist of Emergence India Labs and a professor at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), and professor Ilya Sergey at the National University of Singapore. Nitta said talent for this work is scarce, so the company is creating it. The company has identified a group of people to whom it is extending talent retention offers.
Nitta said the company has open-sourced parts of its technology from the beginning and is now open-sourcing some of its Lean work with Gadgil and Emergence India Labs. He said aspects of the neuroformal AI work will also be open-sourced to build a community and widen the pool from which the company recruits.
He pointed to Agent-E, an open-source web navigation system the company released in 2024 that automates complex browser tasks using simple natural language. He described it as “the very first autonomous web agent build that was fully open-source” and “the very first time somebody actually open-sourced a complex hierarchical agentic system.” Agent-E is available on GitHub. Nitta indicated that the neuroformal AI work will follow a similar path.
He added that the semiconductor industry is only beginning to explore what autonomous agents can do. “I am delighted to see that even in India, there is enormous growth and support from the central government,” Nitta said. “But we are just scratching the surface.”

articles.title: Las gafas inteligentes de Apple llegarían antes de 2027 con funciones de IA
articles.text:
Apple prepararía el lanzamiento de sus primeras gafas inteligentes antes de que termine 2027, según adelantó Mark Gurman en su boletín Power On para Bloomberg. El dispositivo, lejos de ofrecer la experiencia de realidad aumentada que muchos asocian al nombre ‘Apple Glass’, llegaría en una versión más básica, centrada en audio, cámara y funciones de inteligencia artificial, sin pantalla para proyectar imágenes.
La compañía, además, estudiaría en paralelo un posible sucesor de su visor Vision Pro, aunque ninguno de los dos proyectos ha sido confirmado oficialmente.
PUBLICIDAD
Posible calendario de lanzamiento de las gafas inteligentes de Apple
Las previsiones sobre la fecha de llegada de este producto han variado en los últimos meses. Gurman sitúa ahora el objetivo interno de Apple antes de que concluya 2027, una ventana que coincide con lo que ya había anticipado el analista Ming-Chi Kuo en junio de 2025.
El propio Gurman manejó en septiembre de ese año una fecha distinta, más cercana en el tiempo, para unas gafas sin funciones de realidad aumentada. Sin embargo, en mayo de 2026 corrigió el rumbo y volvió a colocar el proyecto hacia el final de 2027, una estimación que la información más reciente confirma.
PUBLICIDAD
Estas fechas corresponderían a objetivos internos de Apple, no a compromisos oficiales, por lo que están sujetas a cambios. Tampoco existe certeza sobre si una eventual presentación del producto a finales de 2027 implicaría su disponibilidad inmediata en tiendas, ya que ambos hitos no siempre coinciden en los lanzamientos de la compañía.
En síntesis, las gafas inteligentes de Apple podrían debutar antes de que termine 2027, aunque sin pantalla integrada en su primera versión: incorporarían audio, cámara y funciones de inteligencia artificial, en un formato más cercano a unas gafas de uso diario que a un visor de realidad mixta.
PUBLICIDAD
Un primer modelo sin pantalla pensado para el uso diario
A diferencia de lo que sugiere el nombre con el que se conoce al proyecto, las primeras Apple Glass no proyectarían contenido visual ante los ojos del usuario. Según describe Gurman, se trataría de unas gafas con audio, cámara y funciones inteligentes, pero sin pantalla para mostrar interfaces o imágenes.
El planteamiento acerca este dispositivo, en términos conceptuales, a las Ray-Ban Meta más que a un equipo de realidad mixta como el Vision Pro. La razón respondería a las exigencias distintas que plantea un producto pensado para acompañar al usuario a lo largo del día frente a un visor de uso más específico.
PUBLICIDAD
Apple ya cuenta con interacción por voz mediante Siri a través de los AirPods, pero la incorporación de cámaras en unas gafas abriría posibilidades adicionales, vinculadas a lo que el usuario tiene frente a sí en cada momento. Por el momento no se han confirmado especificaciones técnicas ni prestaciones concretas del dispositivo.
La compañía reservaría la incorporación de elementos visuales para una generación posterior del producto. Esto significa que el nombre “Apple Glass” no implicaría, en su primera versión, unas gafas de realidad aumentada completas, sino un paso previo dentro de una posible familia de dispositivos que Apple no ha detallado públicamente.
PUBLICIDAD
Otros dispositivos inteligentes en desarrollo
El interés de Apple por integrar inteligencia artificial en objetos de uso cotidiano no se limitaría a las gafas. El boletín de Gurman menciona también otros formatos que la compañía explora en paralelo, como unos AirPods equipados con sensores de cámara.
A esta línea de trabajo se suma una pulsera de actividad sin pantalla, pensada igualmente para acompañar al usuario durante el día sin depender de una interfaz visual tradicional. Se trata de iniciativas independientes entre sí, pero que comparten un mismo objetivo: extender funciones inteligentes a dispositivos de uso continuo.
Paralelamente, Apple continuaría trabajando en un posible sucesor del Vision Pro, su visor de realidad mixta. Este desarrollo se mantendría como un proyecto separado del de las gafas inteligentes, orientado a un tipo de experiencia distinta a la que busca un dispositivo ligero de uso diario.

articles.title: WhatsApp renforce son contrôle parental pour les ados
articles.text:
Superviser l’utilisation que font vos ados de leur compte WhatsApp sans pour autant s’immiscer dans leur vie privée est un difficile équilibre. Pour vous permettre de guider votre progéniture dans l’utilisation de la messagerie, WhatsApp introduit de nouvelles options dans son contrôle parental.
Ces nouvelles options, spécifiquement destinées à la supervision des comptes des adolescents, visent à encourager le dialogue familial en permettant aux parents d’avoir une visibilité adaptée à l’utilisation que fait leur enfant mineur de l’application.
Des options pour mieux accompagner l’ado dans l’usage de WhatsApp
Ces nouvelles options intégrées au contrôle parental, totalement facultatives, viennent s’ajouter aux protections déjà existantes au sein de l’application. Elles ont pour but principal d’aider les parents à accompagner leurs ados dans l’utilisation qu’ils ont de la messagerie. Pour fonctionner, il est donc nécessaire de relier le compte du parent à celui de l’ado.
Mais le champ d’action des parents est suffisamment restrictif pour ne pas empiéter sur l’intimité de leur progéniture. Les parents peuvent ainsi définir les paramètres de confidentialité de leur ado, notamment pour ce qui est de choisir qui a le droit de voir sa photo de profil et ses informations personnelles, ou de l’ajouter à des groupes.
Dans le cas où l’ado souhaiterait assouplir les règles mises en place dans les paramètres de confidentialité de son appli, toute modification de ces paramètres devra être validée par un parent qui devra saisir un code PIN parental.
Les parents seront informés par des notifications lors de certains événements. Ce sera par exemple le cas quand l’ado rejoint ou quitte un groupe, si un groupe dans lequel votre ado se trouve s’agrandit significativement ou encore lors de l’ajout d’un nouveau contact.
Certaines fonctionnalités de WhatsApp seront par ailleurs encadrées. Les parents pourront ainsi choisir qui est autorisé à voir les Statuts de leur ado, mais aussi quels Status ces derniers sont autorisés à consulter. Il en sera de même pour ce qui est de l’accès aux Chaînes WhatsApp.
Contrôler l’activité sans bafouer l’intimité
Trouver la juste limite entre un contrôle parental strict et trop permissif peut sembler délicat. Si la question ne se pose pas pour les ados de moins de 13 ans, pour les plus vieux, la question de préserver leur intimité est indispensable. Si toutes les conversations (messages et appels) restent chiffrées de bout en bout avec le contrôle parental activé, la confidentialité des échanges des ados est elle aussi préservée.
Car personne en dehors de la discussion, pas même les parents superviseurs, n’est en mesure de lire le contenu des conversations, d’écouter les appels ou d’accéder aux contenus échangés par l’ado. Surtout, les adolescents sont automatiquement informés de ce qu’implique la mise en place du contrôle parental sur leur compte WhatsApp.
WhatsApp précise que le déploiement de ces nouvelles options de contrôle parental est en cours et se fera de manière progressive. Il est donc probable que vous ne voyiez pas ces nouveautés immédiatement dans votre application.

articles.title: Mercredi (Netflix) : où en est la saison 3 de la série avec Jenna Ortega ?
articles.text:
Mercredi (Netflix) : où en est la saison 3 de la série avec Jenna Ortega ?
Netflix a donné des nouvelles de sa série sur Mercredi Addams, dont la troisième saison se profile sur le service de streaming.
Le prochain chapître de l'histoire de Mercredi Addams arrivera prochainement sur Netflix, qui vient d'annoncer la fin du tournage de la saison 3 de la série portée par Jenna Ortega. Que sait-on déjà de ces nouveaux épisodes de Mercredi ? Il est temps de faire le point.
Mercredi bientôt de retour
La saison 3 de Mercredi a été annoncée avant même la sortie de la saison 2, la série créée par Alfred Gough et Miles Millar ayant connu un tel succès sur Netflix que la plateforme de SVOD n'a pas hésité à prolonger les aventures de la fille de Gomez et Morticia Addams à l'académie Nevermore.
Mais cette saison 3 ne montrera pas seulement Mercredi dans les couloirs de son école, puisqu'on sait que son histoire l'amènera aussi à Paris pour une épopée en compagnie de son oncle Fétide (Fred Armisen). Que vont-ils faire de leur temps dans la capitale, il faudra patienter jusqu'à la sortie de cette saison 3 pour le découvrir.
Côté casting, Ortega est toujours entourée de Catherine Zeta-Jones (Morticia Addams), Luis Guzmán (Gomez Addams), Isaac Ordonez (Pugsley Addams), Emma Myers (Enid Sinclair), Hunter Doohan (Tyler Galpin), Joy Sunday (Bianca Barclay), Moosa Mostafa (Eugene Ottinger), Georgie Farmer (Ajax Petropolus), Billie Piper (Isadora Capri), Luyanda Unati Lewis-Nyawo (Sheriff Ritchie Santiago), Victor Dorobantu (La Chose), Evie Templeton (Agnes DeMille), Joanna Lumley (Hester Frump) et Fred Armisen (Uncle Fester).
De nouvelles têtes rejoignent aussi cette sombre aventure dont Eva Green (Penny Dreadful) sous les traits d'Ophelia, la tante de Mercredi, Winona Ryder (Stranger Things) dans la peau de Tabitha, mais aussi Chris Sarandon (Princess Bride), Noah Tayler (Peaky Blinders), Oscar Morgan (A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms), Kennedy Moyer (Task), Lena Headey (Game of Thrones), Andrew McCarthy (St. Elmo’s Fire) et James Lance (Ted Lasso). Cela en fait du beau monde pour faire face à Mercredi !
L'intrigue de la saison 3 demeure teintée de mystère mais comme la fin de la saison 2 voyait le personnage d'Enid Sinclair coincé sous sa forme de loup-garou et s'enfuir, il serait logique de voir Mercredi partir à sa recherche dans la saison 3.
Celle-ci n'a pas encore de date de sortie même si on croise les doigts de La Chose pour qu'elle arrive sur Netflix d'ici à la fin 2027. La saison 1 est sortie en novembre 2022 tandis que la saison 2, divisée en deux parties, a débarqué sur le service de streaming en août et septembre 2025. Il ne serait donc pas surprenant que Netflix s'en tienne à une diffusion autour de l'automne pour la troisième saison.

articles.title: Practical tips every Indian household should knowHow to choose the right family health insurance plan
articles.text:
Practical tips every Indian household should know How to choose the right family health insurance plan
From sum insured and hospital networks to waiting periods, exclusions, and claims support, here are key factors Indian families should consider before choosing a health insurance plan.
Choosing a health plan for the family is among the most important financial decisions a household can make, yet it is often made in a hurry, based on a friend's recommendation or the lowest premium on offer.
The right health insurance policy does much more than pay hospital bills. It gives your loved ones access to timely treatment, protects the savings you have built with care, and brings peace of mind during some of life's most stressful moments.
With so many options available, a structured approach can help you pick a plan that genuinely fits your family.
Start by understanding your family's health needs
Before comparing policies, take stock of your household. Consider the age of each member, any existing medical conditions, lifestyle habits, and whether you are planning to grow your family. A young couple, a household with school-going children and a joint family with senior parents will each have very different priorities. Clarity at this stage makes it much easier to shortlist plans that address real needs rather than generic ones.
Choose a sum insured that reflects reality
The sum insured is the maximum amount the policy will pay during a policy year. It should reflect the cost of treatment at the hospitals you would realistically choose, especially if you live in a large city where healthcare costs tend to be higher. With floater plans, the cover is shared among members, so it should be large enough to handle more than a single hospitalization in the same year. Medical costs also rise over time, so leaving some headroom is a sensible choice.
Check the hospital network near you
A strong network of hospitals offering cashless treatment can make a significant difference during an emergency. With cashless facilities, the insurer settles eligible bills directly with the hospital, subject to policy terms, so the family does not have to arrange large sums at short notice. Check whether trusted hospitals near your home and workplace are part of the insurer's network.
Look closely at coverage details
Not all policies cover the same things. Review whether the plan includes in-patient hospitalisation, pre- and post-hospitalization expenses, day-care procedures, ambulance charges, and domiciliary treatment. Families planning to have children should look at maternity and newborn cover, which usually comes with a waiting period. Some plans also offer benefits such as restoration of the sum insured, preventive health check-ups, and wellness programs.
Understand limits, waiting periods, and exclusions
The fine print often determines how useful a policy will be at claim time. Room rent limits, co-payment clauses, and sub-limits on specific treatments can increase out-of-pocket expenses. Waiting periods apply to pre-existing conditions and certain specified illnesses, and every policy has a list of exclusions. Reading these sections carefully helps you avoid surprises later.
Consider the needs of senior parents
Including parents under the same policy can be convenient, but it may raise the premium and increase the chance of the shared cover being used up. Many families evaluate whether a separate policy for parents offers better overall protection. When comparing health insurance plans for family, weigh convenience against adequate coverage for every member, especially those with higher health needs.
Compare plans on value, not price alone
A low premium can be tempting, but it may come with restrictive conditions that reduce the value of the cover when you actually need it. Compare plans on the overall benefits they offer, the flexibility of their terms, and the long-term renewability of the policy. A slightly higher premium for broader, more reliable coverage is often the wiser choice for a family.
Evaluate the claims experience
A policy is only as good as its claims support. Look at how easy it is to raise a claim, the availability of customer support, digital tools for tracking claims and the insurer's reputation for service. Clear communication and a transparent process matter a great deal when a family member is unwell.
Be honest in your proposal form
Always disclose medical history, lifestyle habits, and existing conditions accurately. Complete disclosure builds a strong foundation for smooth claims, while incomplete or incorrect information can lead to complications when you need the policy most.
Review your policy regularly
Family circumstances change. Marriage, the arrival of a baby, children growing older, or parents moving in are all good moments to reassess your cover. Renewing on time keeps protection continuous and preserves benefits such as completed waiting periods.
Conclusion
The best family health insurance plan is not necessarily the cheapest or the most feature-heavy. It is the plan that matches your family's health profile, covers treatment at the hospitals you trust, and offers dependable support when you need it. By approaching the decision thoughtfully, you can give your loved ones the security they deserve.
(Disclaimer: The views and opinions expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of YourStory.)

articles.title: Google Home éteint enfin les lumières quand le curseur de luminosité tombe à 0 %
articles.text:
Dans Google Home, abaisser la luminosité à 0 % pouvait laisser les ampoules allumées au minimum. Une mise à jour envoie désormais une commande d’extinction, y compris pour les groupes de lumières. Le correctif est en cours de déploiement dans l’application Android.
Le détail compte : régler une ampoule au plus bas et lui demander de s’éteindre sont deux commandes différentes. Jusqu’ici, le curseur de Google Home pouvait afficher 0 % tout en laissant une lueur dans la pièce.
Google Home envoie enfin un ordre d’extinction à 0 %
Le correctif concerne les lumières individuelles et les variateurs de groupes. D’après 9to5Google, amener leur curseur à 0 % déclenche maintenant une commande d’arrêt, là où les ampoules restaient auparavant allumées à leur intensité minimale. Google évoque ainsi la disparition de la lueur résiduelle et de la consommation qu’elle entraînait, sans chiffrer cette dernière.
La correction arrive avec la version 4.31.27.1 de l’application, et 9to5Google ne signale le déploiement que sur Android. Cette mise à jour de l’application est aussi différente des améliorations de Gemini pour Home, distribuées séparément aux utilisateurs de son accès anticipé.
La même vague de correctifs touche d’autres commandes domestiques. Dans l’onglet « Tous les appareils », les interrupteurs Matter déconnectés doivent désormais apparaître grisés : un bug pouvait auparavant masquer leur état hors ligne ou empêcher les tuiles de réagir aux pressions. L’appui long sur une tuile de favoris est également corrigé pour ouvrir le contrôleur de l’appareil ou l’éditeur de routine.
Google a aussi revu la reconnaissance des stores bannes et des rideaux, qui pouvaient être classés à tort parmi les stores. Pour les nouveaux appareils Nest, des corrections visent les interruptions de connexion Bluetooth et d’association Wi-Fi lors de l’installation sur Android et iOS. L’application peut en outre conserver sur le mobile les identifiants réseau afin de les réutiliser à l’ajout d’un autre appareil.
Gemini progresse à la voix, mais reste en accès anticipé
Côté assistant, Google annonce une fiabilité accrue de la commande « Hey Google, trouve mon téléphone », sans préciser la nature du correctif. La mise à jour vise également à améliorer la reconnaissance des conversations avec des bruits et des voix en arrière-plan qui empêchent la détection de chaque mot, les commandes personnalisées des routines et la reconnaissance des demandes dans les foyers où plusieurs langues sont parlées par les membres de la famille. Ces changements concernent Gemini pour Home en accès anticipé, pas tous les utilisateurs de l’application.
Cette distinction n’est pas nouvelle : de précédentes corrections de Google Home mêlaient déjà retouches de l’interface et progrès de l’assistant vocal. Pour les lumières, en revanche, le bénéfice attendu est immédiat et facile à vérifier : à 0 %, l’ampoule doit s’éteindre, pas simplement devenir difficile à voir.

articles.title: Uno de los libros que marcó la infancia de millones de personas tendrá nueva película. Y no será una adaptación convencional
articles.text:
No recuerdo la edad que tendría cuando leí mi primer libro, sí recuerdo cuál fue: 'El Principito', la joya literaria publicada por Antoine de Saint-Exupéry en 1943. Desde entonces, la obra se ha traducido a más de 600 lenguas y dialectos, con más de 200 millones de copias de todos ellos. Lo que le faltan son películas, no ha tenido demasiadas adaptaciones a la gran pantalla.
Está Jesús y después el Principito. Solo la Biblia supera al título de Exupéry por el número de traducciones. De hecho, Exupéry tiene hasta un récord Guinness por ser el autor con la obra más traducida de la historia. Ha dejado huella en una buena cantidad de niños. Que después se convirtieron en adultos imaginando que un sombrero puede ser mucho más que un sombrero. La carga imaginativa y nostálgica que lleva implícita 'El Principito' convierten a la historia en carne de superproducción de Hollywood.
Según ha revelado Variety, 'El Principito' va camino de las salas de cine. No será una adaptación tal cual de la obra infantil, sino que combinará la narración del libro con pasajes reales de la vida de Saint-Exupéry. Parece que se plantea como una especie de biopic combinado con ficción fantástica.
El director. A los mandos de la producción estará Morten Tyldum, responsable de, entre otras, la película 'The Imitation Game' (descifrando Enigma en España). El director está de actualidad por una de las obras más reconocibles de Apple TV+: 'Silo', donde Tyldum dirige algunos de los episodios.
Otro de los nombres que se han anticipado para 'El Principito' es Simon Beaufoy, ganador del Óscar a mejor guion adaptado por 'Slumdog Millionaire'. O '¿Quién quiere ser millonario?' en España, que nos gusta cambiarles el título a las películas.
Entre imagen real y efectos visuales. La película prevé combinar la historia del libro con la del autor. Para ello, se rodará con actores reales, mientras que el Principito cobrará vida mediante efectos visuales. Como el libro está narrado en primera persona, con un aviador explicando cómo se encontró al Principito, no sería extraño que convergieran los actores reales y los fantásticos en algunas partes de la cinta.
Según explica Morten Tyldum a Variety:
"Veo en esto una historia muy cinematográfica y épica, que nos brinda la maravillosa oportunidad de plantear las grandes preguntas”.
"Es un relato sobre el amor, el duelo y la pérdida; habla de la esperanza, de escuchar los dictados del corazón y de entender la vida como una gran aventura".
Un reto complicado. Pese a ser una de las obras literarias más traducidas del planeta, 'El Principito' apenas ha tenido tres grandes adaptaciones cinematográficas en más de 80 años. En series de televisión sí hay más material, como la realizada en 2010, animada en 3D. Esta serie fue producida por Aton Soumache, el mismo productor que se encuentra detrás de la nueva película en desarrollo. Y que ya produjo la película de 2015.
Hacer una adaptación de un clásico que ha marcado tantas infancias no parece un reto sencillo. Como mi libro de cabecera que es, tengo curiosidad por ver dónde desemboca el proyecto. Creo que reflejar la vida de Exupéry supone un aliciente a la propia historia de 'El Principito', el tiempo dirá si la combinación termina fraguando en una buena película.

articles.title: We're losing the night sky as light pollution makes it 10% brighter every year
articles.text:
Editor's take: I've always wanted to capture an image of the Milky Way galaxy – or, at the very least, see it with my own eyes in real time. I've got the photography know-how to pull off what would be a frame-worthy shot of our galaxy, as well as the desire to make it happen, but the opportunity simply hasn't presented itself yet. And if the statistics are to be believed, I might never get to cross this one off my bucket list.
Man-made light pollution is the culprit, and it's not just from above. You've no doubt heard of the growing headache that orbiting satellites are causing astronomers trying to photograph the night skies. Compounding the matter is the modern amenity that is artificial light on the ground. Thanks to technologies like LED lighting, large cities and neighborhoods are brighter than ever.
And we're not just talking small numbers here. According to one report, the average night sky got brighter by 9.6% per year from 2011 to 2022. That equates to a roughly doubling of the sky's brightness every eight years. Another study notes that four out of five people live under light-polluted skies. Given those odds, it's likely that you've never even seen the night sky as it was intended.
As Tove Danovich with The Guardian highlights, access to a dark sky is about more than just stargazing. Light pollution can confuse nocturnal animals that use moonlight to navigate, and being in a brightly lit environment around the clock can throw off the circadian rhythm of most all living creatures – humans included.
Some communities are already taking steps to reduce ground-based light pollution. Flagstaff, Arizona, has rules in place to regulate how much light can be used at night, what type, and where it can legally shine. New York state is also considering similar restrictions. But as Danovich correctly notes, such restrictions do nothing to combat space-based light pollution sources like satellites designed to beam sunlight to Earth at night.
Indeed, it feels like darkness is quickly becoming a luxury.

articles.title: Official Minecraft Dungeons 2 Fix Coming to Steam Deck Following Fiddly Community Fixes
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Official Minecraft Dungeons 2 Fix Coming to Steam Deck Following Fiddly Community Fixes
Minecraft Dungeons 2 recently launched on Steam to a decent-but-not-stellar 32,556 peak concurrent players, but not without its fair share of complaints. Both Windows and Linux users alike seem to be experiencing issues launching the Steam version of the game, with SteamOS and Linux users being entirely unable to launch the game under Valve's Proton translation layer. Fortunately, there is light at the end of the tunnel, as Microsoft has officially confirmed in a Minecraft forum post that it is working on Steam Deck support, which consequentially means SteamOS and general Linux support via Valve's Proton. 
In the meantime, several community members have posted community solutions in Minecraft Dungeons 2 Steam reviews. As one user explains it after some experimentation, there appear to be missing dependencies related to the Microsoft Store API that prevent Minecraft Dungeons 2 from launching via Proton. The current community fix is documented on a GitHub repo and involves setting a launch option in Steam and running a script to install dependencies and copy DLL files into the correct location. As the creator describes it, the workaround creates "A local stand-in for Microsoft Gaming Services so Minecraft Dungeons 2 can start under Proton."
A local stand-in for Microsoft Gaming Services so Minecraft Dungeons II (Steam app 1912410) can start under Proton. The game loads xgameruntime.dll; this repository builds it. It does not modify the game or ship Microsoft's library.
As always, it's important to note that, unless you're well-versed enough at tinkering in Linux, it's never a good idea to paste commands into the terminal, especially when those commands copy files and run scripts on your machine. Doing so without understanding what the commands and scripts are doing is unsafe.
		
		Sources:
				Alextibtab on GitHub, 				Steam, 				Minecraft forum, 				via GamingOnLinux

articles.title: PS5 emulation is suddenly making big strides on PC
articles.text:
For a long time, PC gamers could access many PlayStation 5 games only if the publisher invested in a bespoke port (something Sony has recently said it will be scaling back). Now, though, rapid advancements in PS5 emulators and other tools are making recent PlayStation titles increasingly playable on generic PCs.
SharpEmu was the first of these emulators, advancing from a “very early alpha stage” in May to a current state that can “load the eboot.bin of real games, execute native CPU instructions, and partially handle GPU-related functionality.” The most recent release boasts 10 tested games that reach a “playable” state, including six that developer CursedIfElse says are “fully playable at 60 fps.” That includes simple 2D games like Tetris Forever but also 3D titles like Astro Bot and the PS5 Demon’s Souls remaster running at playable frame rates.
“SharpEmu has prioritized hardware accuracy from the very beginning, and we’re finally starting to see that investment pay off,” CursedIfElse wrote on social media this week. “It was built completely from scratch, and this is how far we’ve come.”
Amid that SharpEmu progress, fellow PS5 emulator KytyPS5 launched its first public version last week. The major expansion of PS4-focused emulator Kyty “can boot 2D games and a selection of 3D games, including titles built with Unreal Engine 4/5, Unity, and custom engines,” according to its GitHub page.

articles.title: Trump anuncia IA própria do governo dos Estados Unidos • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Trump anuncia IA própria do governo dos Estados Unidos
America.gov foi reformulado e agora usa chatbot de IA para acessar serviços públicos. Projeto foi liderado pelo cofudandor do Airbnb.
O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, anunciou uma nova ferramenta de inteligência artificial do governo. A ferramenta integra o site reformulado America.gov e, segundo Trump, deve simplificar o acesso a informações e serviços públicos. A ordem assinada nesta terça-feira (29/09) também prevê que todas as agências governamentais integrem seus conteúdos públicos à IA.
A assinatura do documento aconteceu horas antes do anúncio oficial, durante uma reunião entre o presidente e líderes de IA do mercado. O encontro foi promovido para discutir os riscos da tecnologia, tendo em vista as preocupações recentes sobre o ritmo do desenvolvimento em IA.
O site reformulado do governo já está disponível em formato de chatbot. Por lá, é possível fazer perguntas como em qualquer outra ferramenta do tipo, mas as respostas partem de um banco de dados próprio do governo dos EUA. Em algumas respostas, a IA chegou a contradizer declarações do presidente Trump, como destaca a Forbes.
Durante o anúncio da inteligência artificial, o presidente Trump destacou alguns tipos de uso com a nova plataforma. Entre os exemplos estão dar entrada em aplicações de passaporte, selecionar planos de saúde e facilitar o acesso de veteranos aos benefícios oferecidos pelo governo.
O site foi desenvolvido pelo cofundador do Airbnb, atualmente chefe de design do governo, Joe Gebbia. Segundo ele, o objetivo é que as pessoas pesquisem exatamente o que precisam e “nunca mais voltem para o labirinto”. O acesso, portanto, será unificado pela plataforma.
Além de revelar a nova plataforma do governo, Trump aproveitou a situação para indicar que busca caminhar na outra direção das últimas declarações de desenvolvedores de IA. Ao invés de diminuir o ritmo da tecnologia, o presidente dos EUA quer acelerar seu desenvolvimento.
Trump afirmou que pretende mudar a nomenclatura usada para se referir à tecnologia. A ideia é chamar as IAs de “superinteligências”, termo associado à Inteligência Artificial Geral (AGI) e frequentemente usado nas discussões sobre o futuro da inteligência artificial.
Nesse novo estágio, em termos técnicos, a IA seria capaz de agir por conta própria e até mesmo corrigir seus erros – o chamado autoaperfeiçoamento recursivo. Segundo o presidente dos EUA, o movimento será maior que a Revolução Industrial, e “quem ‘ganhar’ a superinteligência, vence”.

articles.title: Prominent tech CEOs sign voluntary White House AI safety accord - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Prominent tech CEOs sign voluntary White House AI safety accord
The chief executives of five tech giants have signed a voluntary artificial intelligence safety accord backed by the White House.
U.S. President Donald Trump posted the document on Truth Social late Tuesday. The White House Accord on Super Intelligence, as it’s called, was signed by Jensen Huang, Sundar Pichai, Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk and Dario Amodei. Greg Brockman, the president of OpenAI Group PBC, signed as well.
“We believe every company is responsible for developing its own technology safely and in a way that builds trust with customers and the public,” the signatories stated.
The accord urges frontier model developers to adopt four sets of AI safety best practices. Several of the best practices have already been implemented by the six participating companies.
The accord’s first recommendation is that AI labs develop “robust internal controls.” According to the White House, those controls should track AI models’ capabilities in sensitive areas such as biology and evaluate their alignment with safety requirements. The accord states that companies should also implement systems that can block AI models from launching cyberattacks.
Top AI labs already have such guardrails in place. However, they don’t always succeed at blocking malicious activity. Last month, OpenAI disclosed that the model behind the Hugging Face Inc. breach had bypassed an internal mechanism meant to isolate it from the web.
The accord’s second focus is AI labs’ organizational structure. It argues that model safety controls should be managed by a dedicated team. Additionally, the signatories call on AI labs to appoint an external auditor to verify that their controls work as expected.
Boards should also have a role in AI safety initiatives, the accord argues. Its closing recommendation is that every AI lab form an independent board committee to oversee the work of its model controls team. Additionally, such committees would be tasked with reviewing reports from AI safety auditors and overseeing risk remediation efforts.
The White House stated that representatives of the participating companies will meet regularly to establish AI safety “standards and best practices.” The tech industry has already started working on such standards. Last year, startup AIUC Inc. released a framework for carrying out AI safety audits. It developed the standard with input from several prominent AI companies and more than 250 Fortune 500 executives.
Trump told reporters that the White House is considering forming a 10-person AI safety committee. He added that he plans to name an “AI czar” by the end of the week. Separately, Trump signed an executive order that will require federal agencies to refer to AI as SI, or super intelligence, in official correspondence and documents.

articles.title: Hear Control Resonant's 'Sibling Theme', a track that its composer says 'is a subset of the origin theme'
articles.text:
Exclusive: Listen to Control Resonant's 'Sibling Theme', a track that its composer says 'soothes and comforts' Dylan and Jesse's 'dented childhood memories'
The full soundtrack is now available
- We can exclusively reveal 'Sibling Theme' from Control Resonant's official soundtrack
- The track represents Jesse and Dylan's bond and is a "subset of the origin theme"
- Composer Petri Alanko says the track "carries the emotions, as if it soothes and comforts the siblings’ dented childhood memories"
Remedy Entertainment's Control Resonant has launched on PC and consoles, and to mark the release, we've got a track from its official soundtrack to debut exclusively for fans.
The 'Sibling Theme' represents the bond between Control and Control Resonant protagonists Jesse and Dylan, with composer Petri Alanko describing it as a "subset of the origin theme," which you can now listen to on YouTube.
"If you listen to the instruments and the harmonies, there’s more than a vague resemblance in it," Alanko told TechRadar Gaming in an exclusive interview.
"At its core, 'Sibling Theme' was originally a much more vibrant version, an instrumental version of 'The One I Once Knew', but it just felt overwhelming under intimate childhood memory-driven sections, and I toned it down, but nothing quite clicked there, until I tested the harmonies and the melody line with just an electric piano."
Alanko, who also created the music for the first game, added that "a delicate moment needed a delicate solution," and he's pleased with how 'Sibling Theme' "carries the emotions, as if it soothes and comforts the siblings’ dented childhood memories."
"The acting of the protagonists is also really one-of-a-kind when the track plays; a lot of emotions are being surfaced," he said.
In addition to our exclusive reveal of 'Sibling Theme', fans can also listen to the official soundtrack on all available music apps and YouTube, featuring 13 tracks.

"Creating a soundtrack is always a labour of love: it’s a transition into a world where dream-like events pass you by and leave their mark, maybe forever," Alanko said in a press release. "The scope of Control Resonant was well beyond everything I have been involved with, so were the emotions under the surface.
"It was incredibly intense trying to hold back tears when the twists and turns were thrown at you, and emotionally Control Resonant went deeper under my skin than I expected. Under the action, it is a story about devotion, dedication, and determination."
Control Resonant is now available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, Series S, and PC.

articles.title: New PS5 Relapse jailbreak enables homebrew and Switch emulation but is hamstrung by rapidly-changing firmware revisions — jailbreak unlocks firmware 13.60, but newer games already demand firmware 14.00
articles.text:
New PS5 Relapse jailbreak enables homebrew and Switch emulation but is hamstrung by rapidly-changing firmware revisions — jailbreak unlocks firmware 13.60, but newer games already demand firmware 14.00
Some games may require an unsupported version of the PS5 firmware, including the new Wolverine title.
A new PS5 jailbreak has been released with support for all PlayStation 5 consoles running firmware 7.00 through 13.60, meaning all consoles that haven't been updated within the last week or so are compatible. That includes the latest PS5 Pro console, too.
The new jailbreak, called Relapse, uses browser and kernel exploits to unlock kernel read and write access, including support for additional payloads like the homebrew enabler etaHEN.
However, while support for consoles all the way up to firmware 13.60 opens the door to more jailbreakers than ever before, the free-for-all might be short-lived. As VideoCardz reports, some games are already requiring the latest 14.00 firmware in order to download updates.
One example is the new Marvel's Wolverine game, with gamers reporting that the disc-based version requires PS5 firmware version 13.40. Downloading the latest 1.001.005 game update bumps the required firmware to version 13.60, which shouldn't be a problem for the Relapse jailbreak. But the fly in the ointment appears to be the digital version of the game. Some gamers have reported that the same update for the digital version of the game requires firmware version 14.00, pushing the PS5 beyond the firmware supported by Relapse.
This news leaves PS5 jailbreakers with a familiar Catch-22 situation. Some games, especially future releases, may require a newer version of the PS5 firmware in order to run. But installing those newer PS5 firmwares will break the jailbreak, giving gamers a decision to make — do they want to play the latest games or maintain their jailbreak?
Marvel's Wolverine aside, there are a number of reasons that gamers may wish to jailbreak their PS5 or PS5 Pro consoles. Doing so bypasses Sony's software restrictions, giving gamers the chance to install and run non-standard software and games. That can include pirated titles, of course, but it also means that emulators, including one for Nintendo Switch games, and mods can be used on a PlayStation. Naturally, those who choose to do this accept the inherent risks involved and do so at their own risk.
More information about Relapse can be found on the jailbreak's GitHub page.

articles.title: Local Day : AliExpress baisse 10 produits tech jusqu'au 7 octobre, du Galaxy S25 FE à la Forerunner 265
articles.text:
Du 1er au 7 octobre, AliExpress organise son Local Day avec sept codes promo à paliers, de 2 € à 60 € de remise selon le montant du panier. Sur les quelque 160 références mises en avant par la plateforme, nous en avons retenu dix, du Honor 600 à la DJI Osmo Pocket 4, pour ce qu’elles valent une fois le code appliqué.
Le Local Day est une opération d’une semaine : du 1er octobre à 0 h au 7 octobre à 23 h 59, heure de Paris, AliExpress applique des codes de réduction sur une sélection d’articles. Le principe est simple : plus le panier est élevé, plus la remise grimpe, de 2 € dès 18 € d’achat avec FRLD02 à 60 € dès 475 € avec FRLD60.
Nous avons écarté les références sans marque connue, ainsi que celles dont le prix, code compris, restait supérieur à ce que nous avions déjà relayé ces derniers mois. Restent dix produits : quatre smartphones, une tablette, une montre et un compteur vélo Garmin, une caméra de poche, un processeur et un casque de réalité virtuelle. Les prix indiqués sont ceux communiqués par AliExpress pour l’événement, code déduit, et chaque ligne précise le code à utiliser.
Local Day AliExpress : nos 10 offres, code promo compris
- Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro 5G à 249,43 € avec le code FRLD30 au lieu de 279,43 €
- Samsung Galaxy S25 FE à 416,59 € avec le code FRLD60 au lieu de 476,59 €
- Xiaomi Pad 7 à 228,28 € avec le code FRLD30 au lieu de 258,28 €
- AMD Ryzen 5 9600X à 142,36 € avec le code FRLD12 au lieu de 154,36 €
- Garmin Forerunner 265 à 211,67 € avec le code FRLD20 au lieu de 231,67 €
- DJI Osmo Pocket 4 à 351,28 € avec le code FRLD45 au lieu de 396,28 €
- Honor 600 à 323,09 € avec le code FRLD45 au lieu de 368,09 €
- Garmin Edge 540 à 200,45 € avec le code FRLD20 au lieu de 220,45 €
- Meta Quest 3S à 253,71 € avec le code FRLD30 au lieu de 283,71 €
- Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro 4G à 177,02 € avec le code FRLD20 au lieu de 197,02 €
Six offres qui méritent qu’on s’y arrête
Ces dix offres ne répondent pas au même besoin, et leur intérêt varie autant que leur remise. Quatre de ces produits sont passés par notre banc de test, à commencer par le Honor 600, noté 9/10 : notre test du Honor 600 détaille ce qui en fait aujourd’hui notre smartphone de référence. Voici ce que chacun apporte, et ce qu’il faut accepter en échange.
- Honor 600 : commercialisé à partir de 549,90 € au printemps, il passe à 323,09 € avec le code FRLD45. Son écran compte parmi les plus lumineux du marché, son autonomie nous a impressionnés et il est certifié IP68, IP69 et IP69K contre l’eau et la poussière. En contrepartie, il reste moins puissant qu’un haut de gamme, n’a pas de téléobjectif optique et arrive chargé d’applications préinstallées.
- Xiaomi Redmi Note 15 Pro 5G : c’est le choix de l’endurance. Dans notre test, il tenait deux jours loin d’une prise, avec un écran OLED de 6,83 pouces qui reste lisible en plein soleil et une certification IP68. Ses performances restent modestes, et l’interface pousse des publicités jusque dans les notifications, ce qui peut agacer au quotidien.
- Samsung Galaxy S25 FE : lancé à partir de 749 €, il descend à 416,59 € avec FRLD60, le code le plus élevé de l’opération. Vous y gagnez un très bon écran, One UI 8 avec Galaxy AI et sept ans de mises à jour. Sa puce Exynos 2400 et sa charge peu rapide le placent toutefois en retrait des Galaxy S25 et S25+.
- Xiaomi Pad 7 : une grande tablette pour lire, regarder des séries et jouer, avec un écran de 11,2 pouces en 3,2K à 144 Hz, une batterie de 8 850 mAh et quatre haut-parleurs. La dalle est un LCD et non un OLED, le modèle n’existe qu’en Wi-Fi, et le stylet comme le clavier se paient à part. Vérifiez la capacité de stockage sélectionnée sur la fiche avant de valider votre panier.
- Garmin Forerunner 265 : nous l’avions relayée à 267,65 € le 22 septembre, elle passe à 211,67 € avec le code FRLD20. Son écran AMOLED, son GPS multibande et ses suggestions d’entraînement quotidiennes en font une montre pour qui prépare un 10 km ou un semi-marathon. Elle n’affiche pas de carte et a laissé sa place à la Forerunner 570 dans la gamme Garmin.
- DJI Osmo Pocket 4 : commercialisée à partir de 479 € en avril, elle passe à 351,28 € avec le code FRLD45. Nous lui avons attribué 9/10 pour son ralenti 4K à 240 images par seconde, son profil D-Log 10 bits et ses 107 Go de stockage intégré. La coque de protection rigide a disparu de la boîte et le zoom numérique 4x reste peu exploitable. L’offre porte sur la version simple, pas sur le pack Combo.
Les codes du Local Day font-ils vraiment la différence ?
Rapportés au montant minimal d’achat, les sept codes représentent tous entre 11 et 14 % de remise : 60 € sur 475 €, 30 € sur 239 €, 12 € sur 89 €. Le code seul ne transforme donc pas un prix moyen en affaire. Ce qui compte, c’est le prix de base proposé pendant l’opération. La Forerunner 265 passe ainsi nettement sous le prix auquel nous l’avions relayée le 22 septembre, alors que d’autres produits de la liste d’AliExpress restaient, code compris, plus chers que nos relevés précédents : nous ne les avons pas retenus.
Autre point à garder en tête : aucune de ces offres n’est vendue par la boutique officielle de la marque, mais par des revendeurs présents sur AliExpress. Les fiches que nous avons consultées indiquent une expédition depuis l’Europe, le plus souvent depuis la France, et AliExpress annonce une livraison en 3 à 7 jours. Si vous hésitez entre plusieurs smartphones, notre comparatif des meilleurs smartphones permet de situer le Honor 600, le Galaxy S25 FE et les deux Redmi Note face au reste du marché.
Local Day AliExpress : vos questions
Quelles sont les dates du Local Day AliExpress 2026 ?
L’opération commence le 1er octobre 2026 à 0 h et se termine le 7 octobre 2026 à 23 h 59, heure de Paris. Les codes promo ne sont valables que pendant cette période.
Quels codes promo utiliser pendant le Local Day ?
AliExpress propose sept paliers : FRLD02 (2 € dès 18 €), FRLD06 (6 € dès 45 €), FRLD12 (12 € dès 89 €), FRLD20 (20 € dès 159 €), FRLD30 (30 € dès 239 €), FRLD45 (45 € dès 355 €) et FRLD60 (60 € dès 475 €). Ils s’appliquent uniquement aux articles inclus dans l’opération.
Les produits du Local Day sont-ils vendus par les marques ?
Non, les dix offres de notre sélection sont proposées par des revendeurs présents sur AliExpress, et non par les boutiques officielles des marques. Le nom du vendeur et le pays d’expédition figurent sur chaque fiche produit.

articles.title: TSMC’s 3-nm Ramp Looks Different in Historical Context - EE Times
articles.text:
TSMC’s 3-nm process is approaching an important milestone. In the second quarter of 2026, it accounted for 30% of wafer revenue, just behind 5 nm at 33%. Recent industry reports suggest that 3 nm could become TSMC’s largest revenue-generating process family during the second half of the year.
But its current size does not tell us how quickly it got there. To compare ramp speed, I used TSMC’s quarterly disclosures to track each node’s share of wafer revenue over its first six quarters as a separate line item, for 10 nm, 7 nm, 5 nm, and 3 nm. Aligning the nodes by age, not calendar date, makes the ramps directly comparable.
In the second reported quarter, 10 nm had already reached 25% of wafer revenue. At the same point, 7 nm was at 23%, 5 nm at 20%, and 3 nm at 15%. By the sixth reported quarter, the picture looked very different. 10 nm had fallen to 6%, 5 nm was at 23%, 3 nm at 26%, and 7 nm had reached 35%.
The newest process generation has not automatically produced the fastest revenue-share ramp. The starting conditions were different.
TSMC’s 7-nm process inherited a large part of the manufacturing platform already developed for 10 nm. The company said more than 95% of the tools were compatible between the two processes and expected that commonality to support a very fast yield ramp. Its commercial ramp benefited from a considerable amount of process learning carried over from the previous generation.
5 nm involved a different transition. TSMC planned extensive use of EUV at 5 nm in part to reduce process complexity, while 7 nm had been developed around much of the established 10 nm tool base.
Revenue-share curves capture more than customer adoption. They also reflect how much manufacturing learning a new process inherits before the first meaningful revenue appears.
The demand behind each node was changing at the same time. 10 nm was strongly associated with performance-driven mobile products, although TSMC also targeted server and graphics applications. By 7 nm, the process was being positioned for both mobile and high-performance computing. 5 nm was optimized from the outset for both mobile and HPC.
The size of the manufacturing operation changed too. TSMC’s annual capacity was just over 12 million 12-inch-equivalent wafers in 2019. By 2024, it was approximately 17 million.
Revenue grew much faster than capacity. When 7 nm reached 35% of wafer revenue in the fourth quarter of 2019, TSMC reported consolidated quarterly revenue of roughly NT$317 billion (~$9.95 billion). When 3 nm reached 26% at the same stage of its ramp in the fourth quarter of 2024, quarterly revenue was roughly NT$868 billion (~$27.2 billion).
Those figures should not be multiplied directly because TSMC reports node mix as a percentage of wafer revenue while the company figure is consolidated revenue. But they show how much the economic base underneath the ramp had changed.
The generations also overlap. In the fourth quarter of 2024, 3 nm represented 26% of wafer revenue, while 5 nm was still 34%, and 7 nm another 14%.
2 nm is now the next test. Everyone will watch how quickly it gains share. But the percentage alone will again reflect several things at once, including how much manufacturing learning carries over from the previous generation, which products move first, and how much economic value TSMC generates from each increment of leading-edge capacity.
3 nm may not be TSMC’s fastest revenue-share ramp, but it may still become one of its largest.

articles.title: 11 000 € et 4 vraies places : Dacia prépare un séisme pour concurrencer la Citroën Ami en 2027
articles.text:
La Spring est trop chère ? Dacia vise encore moins cher avec la version de série du Hipster, qui devrait arriver sur le marché l’année prochaine. Ce crossover inédit débarquera sur le segment L7e des quadricycles lourds avec un habitacle spacieux et quatre vraies places. Son prix devrait tourner autour des 11 000 €, ce qui le placera légèrement au-dessus d’une Citroën Ami pouvant uniquement accueillir deux occupants.
La cible toute désignée est pourtant bel et bien chez Stellantis : il s’agit de la future Fiat Multiplina qui n’est autre que la déclinaison quatre places de la Topolino, dont la production en série approche aussi à grands pas. Katrin Adt, la PDG de Dacia, n’a pas encore confirmé la mise en série du véhicule en affirmant seulement « rester à l’écoute » des demandes. Pourtant, une source proche du projet confirme la chose.
A lire aussi : La nouvelle Dacia Spring est là ! C’est la voiture électrique la moins chère du marché
Une production en Chine pour tailler les coûts au maximum
Le Hipster sera produit l’année prochaine en Chine dans l’usine de Shiyan où était fabriquée la Spring de première génération. Outre des économies substantielles sur l’outillage et le processus industriel, un tel choix influencera aussi grandement la conception du futur modèle. D’après les mêmes sources, moteur, batterie et châssis seront entièrement produits dans cette usine afin de minimiser encore les coûts.
Aussi, le Hipster reprendra le maximum de composants de la première Spring pour abaisser la facture finale. Il ne faudra donc pas s’attendre à un véhicule moderne, mais essentiel avec une masse extrêmement réduite pour satisfaire les exigences de la catégorie L7e. L’engin ne devra ainsi pas excéder les 450 kg, se limiter à une puissance de 20 ch et ne pas dépasser les 90 km/h en vitesse de pointe.
15 kWh et 150 km d’autonomie : taillée pour la ville
Une petite batterie de 15 kWh fera alors l’affaire en offrant près de 150 km d’autonomie. C’est encore moins que les 250 km de la nouvelle Spring mais toujours bien suffisant au quotidien. Le gabarit contenu du Hipster facilitera aussi la vie avec des dimensions proches du concept faisant 3 mètres de long, 1,55 mètre de large et 1,53 mètre de haut. Ses formes cubiques resteront au programme pour favoriser l’espace intérieur.
Le style sera lui aussi fidèle au concept avec un capot court mourant sur une mini calandre adoptant des feux en pixels. Les protections en plastique engloberont toute la carrosserie pour protéger le Hipster des petits chocs urbains, alors que les grandes surfaces vitrées permettront une bonne visibilité extérieure et une belle luminosité intérieure. L’habitacle sera ultra minimaliste avec une planche de bord évasée et un support pour smartphone.

articles.title: Why procurement and legal teams still struggle to work as one
articles.text:
Why procurement and legal teams still struggle to work as one
Despite the necessity of working together, legal and procurement teams often find themselves at odds. While both play a critical role in the business, their different priorities can create friction. Can technology bridge the gap and help them work together more effectively?
It's a story as old as the world of business is. Your procurement team is coming to you all excited; they've found the perfect new supplier for that new project. The pricing looks good, the forecasted timeline is excellent, everything looks great. Then you get to actually see the light in their eyes die out. The legal team needs to review the contracts, ensure that this new supplier is up to the same regulatory standards as previous ones, and make sure that everything is above board and the company isn't putting itself at risk.
So, what's the problem? If everyone is rowing together, why is the boat going in circles? Well, these different departments are going to be using separate processes and systems, and those systems might not dovetail into each other as neatly as they could. Data from data-cubed.com suggests that 20-30% of operational expenses are wasted on inefficiency around process bottlenecks and poor communication. But modern problems have modern solutions, and an agentic orchestration layer like the one Tonkean provides could be the solution for the friction that these disparate departments commonly experience.
Why procurement and legal clash so often
The salient reason that procurement and legal, out of all the different teams, are so often going to clash is that they are often part of the same commercial process. The friction occurs because they are dealing with that commercial process from different perspectives.
The procurement team is all about getting commercial value. They want things to happen at speed, perform well, and be costed well.
The legal team is there to make sure the organization's legal interests are looked after. Compliance with regulations must be ensured, risk mitigated, and contractual obligations met.
Cross-department friction is exacerbated by siloed systems
It's almost certain that every department within your organization is using some sort of specialist technology. Specialist systems are, in many cases, necessary for modern business function. But they can exacerbate the friction that occurs between departments when a process necessitates two different teams' attention.
When we look specifically at the workflows of legal and procurement teams, the issue with siloed systems can become obvious. Problems such as the following are likely to be familiar:
- Each team has different versions of the same information.
- Employees are submitting the same information multiple times into different systems.
- Multiple systems need to be updated manually.
There is likely to be a lot of manual entry, taking up valuable time, when systems should be heavily digitized. Data-cubed.com suggests that the average employee might spend as much as 65% of their week on work that isn't actually creating value. More than half of employees spend at least two hours a day on repetitive tasks like data entry, instead of on skilled work. But siloed systems aren't the only point of friction, and lack of context is often a point of friction that agentic orchestration can solve.
What exactly is an agentic orchestration layer?
You should think of an agentic orchestration layer as connective tissue. Something that sits between and over all of the people, business processes, AI agents, and systems that your organization is using.
The idea isn't to reinvent the wheel and throw out the baby with the bathwater; the existing technology that different teams are using should continue to be used. That technology and those systems are in use for a reason, after all. Instead, the idea is to improve the level of coordination that is possible across these disparate systems and processes.
An agentic orchestration layer is a way for separate teams to use enterprise technologies while coordinating the work that occurs through those technologies and connecting them.
Connecting departments without changing tools
There are obvious advantages to ensuring that all of your organization's departments are more coordinated, but thinking about changing every department's suite of tools for one universal system probably makes you break out in a cold sweat. It's an unattractive and expensive idea, and most importantly, it's an unnecessary one.
Existing systems should not need to be replaced, but systems such as procure-to-pay applications, document management tools, communication platforms, e-signature systems, CLMs, and ERP platforms should all be connected.
Agentic orchestration allows for a common operational layer to be overlaid on top of existing enterprise tools. Departments will be connected without needing to change tools and sacrifice their current functionality.
AI agents power the coordination
One of the best uses for agentic orchestration is achieved through using AI agents as part of an organization's processes.
The idea is that an employee would not need to separately reach out to each different department for clarification or information when starting a process; they can instead simply run their queries by an AI agent in the orchestration layer. This agent would then be able to determine which departments are required based on previously determined organizational policies and to start the process of actioning that request.
This sort of coordination will save time and unnecessary communication, as only the relevant departments will be contacted by AI agents as part of any process. The usage of AI agents to streamline job processes was estimated by Forbes to be something that around 42% of business owners believed in.
A single business process, orchestrated as one
Collaboration within organizations is not about replacing departmental tools; it's about connecting them around a shared process. An agentic orchestration layer will do that.

articles.title: 150 recettes et 6 modes de cuisson sur le nouveau Cookeo Simplicity à moins de 200 €
articles.text:
150 recettes et 6 modes de cuisson sur le nouveau Cookeo Simplicity à moins de 200 €
Moulinex élargit sa célébrissime gamme de multicuiseurs Cookeo avec la déclinaison Simplicity, commercialisé au prix de 199,99 €. Ce multicuiseur de 6 litres intègre 150 recettes guidées et propose 6 modes de cuisson automatiques au quotidien.
Après les versions Infinity, Wifi 9-en-1, Touch Pro, Touch Mini WiFi et bien d'autres qu'il serait fastidieux de toutes énumérer ici, le Cookeo de Moulinex revient dans une itération baptisée Simplicity dont la puissance atteint 1600 watts. Lancé au tarif de 199,99 €, soit le prix le moins élevé pour un Cookeo jusqu'ici, ce multicuiseur est proposé en quatre coloris : blanc, gris clair, marron et terracotta. Bien évidemment, un Cookeo, même à moins de 200 €, reste un Cookeo et on le reconnaît immédiatement grâce à ses formes arrondies et à son écran en façade. Il conserve également la structure globale de la gamme avec sa cuve amovible d'une capacité de 6 litres, un format dimensionné pour préparer des repas allant jusqu'à 6 personnes. L'appareil est livré avec son panier vapeur ainsi qu'une cuve dotée d'un revêtement antiadhésif, deux éléments compatibles avec un nettoyage au lave-vaisselle. Son couvercle ergonomique s'actionne par un mécanisme d'ouverture et de fermeture réalisable en un seul geste.
Moulinex Cookeo Simplicity
Fonctionnalités et modes de cuisson
Le panneau de commande embarque donc un bel écran et une molette. Grâce à celui-ci, l'utilisateur choisit l'un des six modes de cuisson distincts : cuisson sous pression, cuisson à la vapeur, cuisson lente, dorage, réchauffage et maintien au chaud automatique. Le mode sous pression (qui peut monter jusqu'à 80 kPa, selon la fiche technique) est conçu pour accélérer la cuisson des aliments tout en préservant leurs qualités nutritionnelles, le fabricant indiquant une conservation atteignant jusqu'à 80 % de la vitamine C contenue dans les ingrédients. L'appareil propose également un départ différé pour programmer le lancement de la cuisson selon son emploi du temps. En complément des programmes automatiques, un mode manuel laisse l'utilisateur définir lui-même ses propres paramètres.
Le système d'assistance embarqué comprend 150 recettes préprogrammées, détaillées étape par étape directement sur l'écran d'affichage. Celles-ci couvrent différents types de préparations, des entrées aux desserts, incluant des formules express réalisables en moins de 10 à 15 minutes ainsi que des options végétariennes. Et si tout cela ne suffisait pas, l'application mobile gratuite MyMoulinex donne accès à un catalogue de recettes supplémentaires, des filtres par ingrédients pour limiter le gaspillage et des fonctionnalités de gestion de listes de courses.
Compatibilité et réparabilité
Sur le plan matériel, ce multicuiseur reste compatible avec des accessoires optionnels de la marque, notamment le couvercle Extra Crisp vendu séparément, qui permet d'ajouter une fonction de cuisson à air chaud pour dorer ou gratiner les plats. Enfin, l'appareil s'inscrit dans la politique de durabilité du fabricant avec un engagement de réparabilité garanti pendant 15 ans.

articles.title: La IA de Meta, Muse, enfrenta una nueva acusación: usuario asegura que accedió a sus mensajes privados sin autorización
articles.text:
El agente de inteligencia artificial Muse, desarrollado por Meta, afronta una nueva denuncia por un presunto acceso no autorizado a información personal. El periodista tecnológico Jason Aten aseguró que la herramienta leyó sus mensajes privados de la aplicación Mensajes de Apple y transfirió más de 187.000 registros de sus conversaciones a sus servidores, pese a que no había habilitado el permiso de acceso total al disco de su Mac.
El caso fue expuesto por Aten en una columna publicada en Inc, en la que relató cómo descubrió que Muse había accedido a su historial de mensajes después de instalar la aplicación en su iPhone y su Mac Mini. Según el periodista, el agente de IA utilizó información de una conversación privada para sugerirle que podía convertirla en una columna, sin que él hubiera autorizado expresamente esa consulta.
PUBLICIDAD
La denuncia vuelve a poner el foco en los permisos que necesitan los agentes de inteligencia artificial para acceder a los datos personales y realizar tareas de forma autónoma. También plantea interrogantes sobre los mecanismos de seguridad que utilizan estas herramientas para gestionar información privada.
Cómo Muse habría accedido a los mensajes privados de un usuario
El incidente comenzó después de que Aten mantuviera una conversación por Mensajes con Stephen Robles, copresentador de su pódcast, sobre los nuevos iPhone de Apple. Poco después, recibió una notificación de Muse en la que el agente le sugería que ese intercambio podía convertirse en una columna informativa y se ofrecía a recopilar los datos necesarios.
PUBLICIDAD
La propuesta sorprendió al periodista, que aseguró no haber autorizado el acceso a sus mensajes, calendario ni a otros datos personales. Por ese motivo, decidió preguntarle directamente a Muse cómo había obtenido la información sobre la conversación.
El agente respondió que recibía el contenido de las notificaciones que aparecían en el Mac vinculado, es decir, el mismo texto que se muestra en los avisos del sistema operativo. Sin embargo, Aten investigó el funcionamiento de la aplicación y descubrió que, según sus comprobaciones, Muse había sincronizado directamente la base de datos local de Mensajes.
El periodista afirmó que la herramienta había transferido más de 187.000 registros de su historial, hasta alcanzar la fila 187.462. Esta circunstancia contradice la explicación inicial que le proporcionó el agente sobre el origen de la información.
PUBLICIDAD
Aten también señaló que tenía desactivada la opción de acceso total al disco de macOS, un permiso que permite a las aplicaciones acceder a una parte considerable de los archivos almacenados en el equipo.
Qué respondió Meta ante la denuncia sobre Muse
Después de descubrir lo ocurrido, Aten intentó ponerse en contacto con Meta en dos ocasiones, pero aseguró que no recibió respuesta directa de la compañía. Posteriormente, David Singleton, directivo de Meta Superintelligence Labs, se pronunció sobre el caso en Threads.
Singleton afirmó que Muse fue diseñado teniendo muy presentes la seguridad y la privacidad de los usuarios. También aseguró que la compañía se toma muy en serio cualquier informe relacionado con posibles problemas de seguridad.
PUBLICIDAD
El directivo explicó que la integración con la aplicación Mensajes es opcional y que requiere activar tanto el conector correspondiente como el acceso total al disco de macOS. Según esta explicación, el funcionamiento denunciado por Aten dependería de la configuración de determinados permisos.
Sin embargo, el periodista cuestionó esa respuesta, ya que considera que no debería ser necesario que los usuarios descubran por sí mismos que una aplicación accede a información privada. También señaló que las explicaciones de Singleton parecían dar por hecho que había habilitado todas las opciones necesarias para permitir ese acceso.
PUBLICIDAD
