The Galaxy Tab S12+ features a larger 12.6-inch display and slimmer bezels than its predecessor, offering more screen space without sacrificing portability. Both models feature Dynamic AMOLED 2X displays reaching up to 1,600 nits of peak brightness—delivering clear, vivid visuals indoors, or out. The upgraded seamless Vision Booster now adjusts brightness in real time based on lighting conditions for comfortable viewing.Sound gets a major upgrade as well, with 4-channel spatial audio—twice as many channels as the previous generation—delivering a richer, more immersive experience whether users are streaming content, following a tutorial, or editing.
Making Everyday Tasks More Intuitive and Effortless
Building on an industry-leading hardware foundation, the Galaxy Tab S12 series turns its large screen into a flexible workspace that makes it easy to keep up with different tasks without missing a beat. Running Android 17 with One UI 9 and the latest Galaxy AI, it brings research, note-taking, creation, and AI assistance into one place, giving users more freedom to explore new ideas, capture what matters and put what they learn into practice.
Thanks to the Galaxy Tab S12 series' immersive screen, users can split the screen into up to three sections in Multi Window layout. For example, users can take notes in Samsung Notes on one side while playing a lecture and opening an AI assistant on the other. As key takeaways or questions come up, users can capture them with the S Pen directly in Samsung Notes, while Note Assist summarizes their notes - all without pausing the lecture.Both models come bundled with an ergonomic S Pen, offering precise, intuitive input for note-taking, annotating materials, and sketching concepts. For a more structured, professional workstation, the Pro Keyboard elevates productivity with a premium aluminium finish and a Galaxy AI Key that enables instant access to AI assistants, while the Book Cover Keyboard Slim delivers flexibility with comfortable viewing angles and an effortless typing experience.The Galaxy Tab S12 series helps users bring information together and get real-time support the moment curiosity strikes. The Galaxy Tab S12 series comes equipped with a six-month trial of Google AI Pro, providing expanded access to Google's most capable AI models from day one. Users can ask Gemini about anything unclear or dive deeper into subjects they want to explore the moment a question comes up. With Gemini Notebook, users can bring together notes, images, recordings, and files in one workspace and create summaries, podcasts, and even quizzes to make key information easier to understand.
As exploration expands into deeper research, Samsung Browser helps users stay focused without losing track of what they have already discovered. By understanding webpage content, context across multiple tabs, and browsing history, it can summarize information across open pages or surface a relevant source viewed days earlier - helping users spend less time searching through past tabs and more time capturing the key insights that matter most.A Complete Ecosystem Designed To Take Skills and Creativity Further
The Galaxy Tab S12 series gives users the ideal place to put knowledge into practice, bringing together professional-grade apps alongside benefits worth approximately $600 to help them take their skills further.
Adobe Photoshop16 comes preloaded on the Galaxy Tab S12 series—a first for Android tablets—bringing pro-grade image editing and design to the tablet. The interface is optimized for tablets, and S Pen support makes it more intuitive to move ideas from hand to screen. Photoshop includes AI-powered features including AI Assistant and generative AI features powered by Adobe Firefly like Generative Fill and Image to Video, helping creatives edit faster and effortlessly. Exclusively for the Galaxy Tab S12 series, users receive four months of free access to the Photoshop mobile plan.
Notability, newly preloaded on Galaxy Tab, helps users capture their ideas, organize notes, and build knowledge more efficiently with S Pen optimization and AI-driven study tools with a six-month free trial, plus 20% off the first subscription.
Goodnotes delivers clean note-taking and organization with one year of free access and LumaFusion enables professional-grade video editing, offered at a 66% discount. And Notion supports flexible writing, planning, and organization with one month of its Plus plan free. Clip Studio Paint22 brings precision drawing and painting tools for digital art with a six-month trial and 20% off the first subscription.
In addition to these apps, users can explore a broader range of options that support different needs. MyScript Math instantly solves handwritten equations and shows the steps behind each one, while MyScript Notes summarizes handwritten notes into study materials with built-in AI tools to explain concepts or generate quizzes. Noteshelf offers customizable layouts for capturing and organizing ideas, while ArcSite converts rough field sketches into precise CAD drawings.
Availability
The Galaxy Tab S12 series will be available starting Oct. 7 in select markets and offered in two colors, Gray and Silver.
Built for lasting and confident use, Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Galaxy Tab S12+ support up to seven times of OS upgrades and security updates.
For added peace of mind, Samsung Care+ offers comprehensive coverage tailored to users' device needs, including fast repairs for accidental damage, extended warranty, and certified expert support available both at home and abroad. Additionally, Galaxy mobile phone users running One UI 9 can easily check the Samsung Care+ status of their Galaxy Tab and enroll through the Warranty and care menu in the Settings. It provides quick access to warranty information, self-diagnostics, repair requests, and remote support for connected devices—all directly from the mobile phone.
4 Comments on Samsung Introduces Galaxy Tab S12 Series
I appreciate the displays over the standard 10", but I'll pass on Samsung's software alone.

articles.title: The US just approved its first small nuclear reactor built for the AI power crunch
articles.text:
Forward-looking: The Tennessee Valley Authority has received the federal go-ahead to build a BWRX-300 small modular reactor at its Clinch River site near Oak Ridge, Tennessee. The approval makes TVA the first US utility authorized to build the GE Vernova Hitachi reactor design, one of several small reactor technologies now being positioned as a source of round-the-clock power for a grid facing fast-rising demand.
The Nuclear Regulatory Commission completed its review in 14 months, four months ahead of schedule. The permit gives TVA the green light to construct the 300-megawatt unit, but the utility will still need a separate operating license before it can load fuel or generate electricity. "This construction permit is more than a regulatory achievement – it's foundational for America's nuclear future," TVA interim president Mike Skaggs said in a statement.
The BWRX-300 is based on boiling-water reactor technology, which has been used in commercial nuclear plants for decades. It is designed to produce 300 megawatts of electricity, or about one-fourth the output of the newest large reactors at Georgia's Vogtle plant.
The technology is meant to simplify the traditional reactor model. The BWRX-300 uses water as a coolant and relies on natural circulation to move water through the system. Its design also incorporates passive safety features that can use gravity, pressure and stored water rather than depending entirely on powered equipment.
GE Vernova Hitachi and its utility customers are betting that a smaller reactor can be built with fewer components, a smaller footprint and more factory-made parts. That could reduce construction time and make projects easier to finance. It remains an unproven argument in the United States, where large nuclear projects have often run late and far over budget.
TVA is evaluating the possibility of building as many as four BWRX-300 units at Clinch River. The utility has not set a construction start date or disclosed a final cost estimate.
The main appeal of the BWRX-300 is not simply its size. It is the prospect of building multiple units from the same design.
Ontario Power Generation is preparing to build a fleet of BWRX-300 reactors in Canada and has installed the foundation for its first unit. TVA and Ontario Power Generation expect that using the same reactor design could help lower costs through shared procurement, manufacturing and construction experience.
Blue Energy is taking a similar approach in Texas. The company has applied for a permit to build BWRX-300 reactors intended to serve data centers and says it plans to manufacture reactor components at scale.
That push reflects growing concern over the power demands of AI data centers. Grid operators and utilities are looking for generation that can operate around the clock without relying on weather conditions. Nuclear power is one of the few low-carbon options that can provide steady output, although new plants remain expensive and slow to build.
Cost is the main driver behind the industry's effort to revive nuclear construction. Vogtle's two newest reactors cost roughly $35 billion and entered service years behind schedule. Developers of small modular reactors say standardized designs and factory production can avoid some of the problems that affected Vogtle.
That claim will be tested at Clinch River. TVA's approval lets the utility begin construction, but the project still must prove the BWRX-300 can be built on time and at a cost utilities and large electricity users will accept.

articles.title: How to Develop Software Engineering Skills in the Age of AI
articles.text:
Software engineering skill development requires slowing down. Tools and AI can accelerate outcomes, but they may not support skill development, Chelsea Troy mentioned in her presentation Leveling up as a Programmer in the Age of AI at Craft conference. Engineers must understand how systems work to learn things. Senior developers can coach juniors by using learning techniques.
There are two modes of software engineering: figuring stuff out and doing stuff. When we want to do stuff, we often speed up. To figure stuff out, we need to slow down, Troy argues. And if doing stuff depends on figuring stuff out, then we’re going to be stuck the faster we try to go: we have to downshift to get anywhere.
Activities that promote learning are, by design, inefficient. They require attention and engagement, to add insult to injury on something that we feel bad at, Troy explained:
We have to sit with something that we feel bad at, and we have to struggle with it. It is that uncomfortable emotion, the confusion, the frustration, that is necessary for us to build cognitive capacity.
Using tools as outcome accelerants often doesn’t support skill development. Even with AI available to us, we need to understand how the systems we are trying to modify work, Troy said.
One concept of the neuroscience of learning is spaced repetition. Skill development reduced to its essentials requires focused attention interspersed with quality sleep, Troy said. She suggested helping junior colleagues by spreading out learning across several bouts of quality sleep, to make it stick.
We internalize information better if we try to guess it first; learning happens when we teach a brain that is already thinking. Troy explained how this concept of outcome prediction works:
As you are learning how something works, you can just stop at each step and ask yourself, "What do I think the next step should be and why, given what I know right now?" And once you have answered, keep going with your learning to find out what the answer actually is. By stopping to ask yourself that question, you can drastically increase the likelihood that you’re going to internalize the answer.
Troy also mentioned the concept of format diversification: people learn information better when they see the same information in multiple different formats rather than repeatedly in the same format:
The reason people think they’re kinesthetic learners is that they read it, listen to it, or see it first, and then they try it and break it. It is the second or sometimes the third way in which they are encountering this information; that’s when it sticks.
Generative AI has changed the landscape of skill development for software engineering. But the biology and psychology of how we solve problems has not changed so quickly, Troy argued. For us to use tools effectively, it’s helpful to understand how they work, but it’s critical to understand how we work and continue to both train ourselves and coach our junior colleagues in techniques and strategies that work with the way we learn, she concluded.
InfoQ interviewed Chelsea Troy after her talk.
InfoQ: What are the cognitive barriers to learning as a software developer in an AI-enabled world?
Chelsea Troy: The cognitive barriers to learning remain largely what they’ve been, because our cognitive structure and potential have not fundamentally changed. But the expectation of an ever-increasing pace of work makes those barriers higher stakes.
Frequently, learning a subject means slowing down and sitting with it. When that becomes a non-option for professional success, developers feel forced to take shortcuts, and they never come back for the learning objective. That’s a systemic barrier, incumbent on managers to guardrail against by managing upwards.
InfoQ: How can we enable learning with junior developers?
Troy: A problem we face often today is the potential for learners to conflate "work completed" with "learning objective accomplished."
When I teach in a classroom of 25 students, I’m not asking them to write a compiler for a small arithmetic language because I personally require 25 copies of this compiler. The actual compilers these students produce are, in fact, of no practical use to me. I’m asking them to do this assignment because the exercise of designing the compiler gives them personal experience with design questions that we discuss for the rest of the quarter. Sure, Claude can write the compiler, but that completely misses the point, because the point was never the compiler. The compiler is a toy problem for learning how to think about harder problems.
Learners, academic or professional, benefit from reflecting on how they, as practitioners, want to change in the course of doing their learning. That change—not the quality of the exercise artifact—is the key performance indicator. When folks are new to the industry, they may require the guidance of a more senior developer to determine what change in their thinking an exercise should target. And to succeed in that guidance, senior developers must develop the capacity to pay close attention to a junior developers’ work—not their assumptions about what juniors do, but this developer’s actual work—and respond to that work in their coaching.

articles.title: The Hidden Challenges of Edge AI Design
articles.text:
As models evolve faster than silicon cycles, chip architects must balance flexible compute, data movement, and defense-in-depth security.
Key Takeaways:
The rapid buildout of the edge is forcing chip architects and design teams to rethink how they add AI to vertical market applications. The fundamental challenge is a mismatch in timelines, because engineering teams must design for AI models, workloads, and deployment requirements that inevitably will shift long after silicon decisions are locked in.
Compounding this, real-world edge performance rarely depends on peak NPU TOPS. More often, it depends on memory bandwidth, latency, power budgets, security, and data movement. To keep pace with evolving models, architects are leaning heavily into flexibility — embracing heterogeneous compute, programmable data paths, expandable memory, secure field updates, and tight hardware-software co-design.
But flexibility alone isn’t enough. AI introduces broad attack vectors across models, data, keys, firmware, and inference pipelines, so robust security must be architected into hardware from day one. At the same time, fragmented toolchains across runtimes and frameworks make hardware-aware optimization just as important as raw compute.
This structural shift is redefining standard component boundaries.
“CPUs are becoming more GPU-like as they try to do more and more parallel processing,” observed Rob Fisher, senior director of product management at Imagination Technologies. “NPUs are becoming more GPU-like as they try to become more flexible, and the convergence point is with the CPU, NPU, and GPU in the middle. We’re finding more customers are trying to hedge their bets against the future than trying to squeeze out every last drop of performance today. That means we’re no longer just looking at a GPU you can slot in that just does GPU-like things. This has system-level impacts on the whole SoC.”
When designing edge applications with AI as a product feature, chip architects and design teams have many considerations. Hardware choices drive these broader architectural decisions, but the challenge reaches well beyond NPU TOPs.
“AI model performance depends on architectural details for memory, latency, power, and security,” said Eduardo Montanez, vice president and head of PSOC Edge MCUs & Edge AI Solutions for Infineon’s IoT, Compute & Wireless Business. This is why the company’s edge microcontrollers include memory expandability, a low-latency architecture, and energy efficiency to enable battery-powered applications at the edge. They also include security features that are designed to protect data and software IP.
AI applications at the edge are already challenging chip architects and design teams to keep up with rapid changes in models and workloads.
“As new networks are continually popping up, any solution needs to be programmable to accommodate new networks and ever-changing activation functions and corresponding data types,” said George Wall, product marketing group director at Cadence. “At the same time, there are hard performance requirements that must also be met.”
This makes hardware-software co-design increasingly important. “AI models, NPUs, memory hierarchy, and optimization techniques such as quantization, pruning, and distillation must be jointly optimized to achieve efficient deployment,” noted Niranjan Sitapure, group product manager for generative AI at Siemens EDA.
The entire pipeline also must be optimized, because success depends on sensor ingestion, data preprocessing, inference, post-processing, and ongoing model lifecycle management.
Ideally, chip architects and design teams would have a detailed view of what an edge application will do, including the models it will use, required performance, available memory, and power constraints, so they can design a chip for optimal PPA.
“Unfortunately, that isn’t reality,” said Paul Karazuba, vice president of marketing, Silicon IP at Rambus. “Even compressed, the chip design cycle will predate the release of any product that contains the chip by a year or more. During that time, it’s reasonable to assume the edge application will evolve, including changes to the underlying model(s) and perhaps the available memory and power. This application evolution forces chip designers to concentrate their efforts on creating chips that can adapt to changing requirements, including but not limited to a focus on moving data efficiently and securely.”
For others, AI acceleration isn’t the biggest challenge. What limits chip performance and efficiency may depend on the rest of the application.
“But architects and designers don’t design for that. They focus on neural network acceleration, claiming very high but theoretical TOPS numbers that no real application even comes close to achieving,” said Graham Gobieski, chief technology officer and co-founder of Efficient Computer. “In fact, in many real workloads (e.g., sensor fusion, autonomy), a majority of the application still runs on whatever general-purpose but very inefficient core exists on the SoC. The real opportunity to enable intelligent applications isn’t a faster NPU; it’s making the other 80% of the application as efficient as the AI portion.”
Beyond efficiency, edge AI applications add numerous design challenges.
Core design challenges
Performance depends on more than the compute capabilities of the programmable processor being used. “For example, memory bandwidth must be sufficient to keep the computational units fed with data, and the data needs to be in a location that is easily accessible by the processor,” explained Cadence’s Wall. “Otherwise, the computational elements will basically sit underutilized. Determining workload requirements is difficult because chip designers won’t necessarily have insight into the networks consumers will be running 3 or 5 years from now.”
This challenge is compounded by the fact that edge AI is fundamentally a constraint-driven design problem. “You are dealing with tight power budgets, limited memory, mixed sensor inputs, and latency expectations that users feel immediately. The architecture has to be efficient before it can be intelligent,” Rambus’ Karazuba said.
As AI models evolve rapidly, system architectures need memory scalability for large data sets and AI models, along with enough memory for the non-AI portions of a design.
“Also, the design must allow for end-to-end, secure provisioning and deployment, allowing for field updates without compromising valuable data and software IP,” Infineon’s Montanez noted.
Moving model weights and activations between DRAM and compute engines can consume more power than the AI computation itself. “AI models evolve faster than silicon development cycles. New architectures, operators, and generative AI workloads emerge continuously, creating pressure for hardware platforms to remain adaptable,” Siemens’ Sitapure said. “For critical/high-risk applications, edge systems such as ADAS, industrial automation, and robotics require predictable latency, high reliability, and operation even with limited connectivity.”
While data movement can dominate performance and efficiency, other challenges may be overlooked. “The first is simple but challenging,” said Efficient Computer’s Gobieski. “The intelligence has to fit on the device. This means a lot of engineering goes into squeezing a neural network into on-device memory before any application code runs. The second has a standard answer that backfires. Splitting the application across an NPU, CPU, and DSP might seem like playing to each block’s strengths, but it complicates development by requiring many different toolchains, and it spends the savings moving data between them.”
Hardware teams also face non-negotiable physical constraints, especially strict low-power budgets. Thermal dissipation limits and battery constraints dictate computational efficiency, along with demanding reliability requirements for mission- and safety-critical edge deployments, Sylvain Guilley, co-founder and chief technology officer at Secure-IC, a Cadence company, noted. “Solving these core challenges requires moving beyond proprietary, siloed hardware tricks toward broader industry-wide alignment on architectural standards. To build standard open framework specifications for edge hardware, Cadence is tackling this in a new OCP FCSA Sub-Project Workstream.”
Security from the start
Electronics developers looking to add AI to edge devices should incorporate several security technologies from the beginning of system design.
The starting point is a secure platform, followed by a secure application. “A secure platform is fundamental,” said Dana Neustadter, senior director of product management for security solutions at Synopsys. “It establishes the foundation, but it does not automatically make the application — or the AI’s output — trustworthy. Developers must still address authorization, data protection, output validation, connected-service security, and component assurance at the application layer. Assume the AI platform already provides a root of trust, secure boot, attestation, encrypted communications, and trusted execution environments. That establishes the foundation, but it does not automatically make the application — or the AI’s output — trustworthy.”
At the application layer, Neustadter said developers must address additional controls, including:
A common misconception is that an AI result must be trustworthy simply because the AI runs on a secure platform. Consider a mobile robot whose model reports that a hallway is empty. If the software accepts that result without further checks, the robot could move and collide with an unexpected obstacle. “The AI provides an input to the decision. It should not be the sole basis for the final decision,” Neustadter explained. “The application should evaluate the model’s confidence score and complete additional checks before authorizing an action. It should also apply relevant rules and safety policies and confirm the environment before the device acts.”
Establishing a resilient platform also does not guarantee privacy. Secure hardware does not compensate for insecure application-level data handling. For example, a smart camera in a mall may analyze shopper behavior. Even if the device is secure, storing those analytics in an unencrypted database could let an attacker access private customer information.
“Secure hardware does not compensate for insecure application-level data handling. Developers should encrypt sensitive data and enforce access controls throughout its lifecycle. They should also retain data only as long as necessary and limit its use to authorized people and services,” she said.
Models should also be authenticated with controls comparable to secure boot. Before loading a model, the system should verify its identity, integrity, signature, and provenance. This is another reason a strong root of trust is essential. “Model confidentiality and access control should also be incorporated into the system’s key-management strategy,” Neustadter explained.
Edge AI systems may require additional keys. A third-party model provider, for example, may want to prevent the device owner or other parties from accessing the model without authorization. Model confidentiality and access control, therefore, become part of the overall key-management strategy.
All models and components can introduce software supply-chain risks. Developers often rely on open-source models, AI engines, plugins, and other external components. A model that contains a hidden backdoor can generate incorrect or malicious outputs, and secure hardware may still execute it if the system accepts the model as trusted.
“Secure hardware will still execute a compromised model if the system accepts it as trusted. To reduce the risk, developers should therefore verify provenance and integrity, validate suppliers, use trusted repositories, and maintain software bills of materials,” Neustadter added.
When designing security into edge applications and mitigating attack vectors introduced by AI, engineering leadership should involve high-level product management as early as possible. That allows developers to perform risk analysis and determine where mitigations are needed across both hardware interfaces and software layers, Cadence’s Guilley said.
“This early architectural grounding directly informs overall device strategy in terms of cyber-resiliency,” he noted. [“Establishing this foundation early] allows us to treat cybersecurity not as a cost but as an investment that enables subsequent operations to unfold safely 24/7 and to turn incidents away from emergencies and rather have them be seen as a business continuity plan.”
This unified security and governance framework becomes especially important when engineering complex cyber-physical systems that must comply with cybersecurity, AI, and data privacy mandates.
“Design teams must continuously navigate strict regulatory boundaries, specifically around the E.U. Cyber Resilience Act, statutory requirements concerning capturing personal data in personally identifiable information, and the overarching statutory mandates enforced under the broader E.U. AI Act,” Guilley said.
A root of trust and separation between secure and non-secure code are also important. “Having a bootloader that manages code authentication is critical,” Infineon’s Montanez said. “With AI moving to the edge, most products still have a hybrid approach with the cloud, allowing for OTA or other communication. Therefore, edge AI applications can require additional security for the connectivity link.”
Big picture, security must be anchored in hardware, from secure boot and trusted firmware to protected keys, memory, and model assets. AI increases the stakes because models, inputs, and outputs can all have significant economic value.
“One should consider that economic value is not just the models themselves or the data inside those models, but also the financial and legal implications of a third party tampering with that data,” Karazuba noted.
Introducing AI into an edge device adds capabilities and features that were often unavailable in prior non-AI-enabled versions. “Device makers must design AI-enabled edge devices with a stronger security profile, given the increased financial and legal implications of a security breach,” he said.
Encryption is another key element, Siemens’ Sitapure said. Model weights, training data, and inference pipelines should be encrypted and protected from tampering, extraction, and unauthorized access.
Above all, security cannot be an afterthought. “Malicious actors could try to hack the underlying model weights and insert their own model that disrupts subsystem operation or exploits other security vulnerabilities in the system,” Cadence’s Wall said. “Fortunately, approaches range from localized encryption/decryption engines to a dedicated security island.”
More broadly, the most dangerous failure in edge AI is not a crash, but a live system that keeps operating while silently believing the wrong state. Real-time decisions increasingly depend on the integrity of on-device inference because edge AI is deployed in cameras, robotics, vehicles, and industrial systems that rely on NPUs, GPUs, and TPUs for performance and efficiency, but are not typically designed to ensure inference integrity under fault conditions.
In a recent white paper that includes the experimental block diagram and physical setup used for fault injection and measurement, Keysight security researchers showed that precisely timed fault injection (FI) can corrupt the output of a production-class edge AI pipeline without modifying firmware, model weights, software configuration, or input data. On a commercial Rockchip RK3568 platform running YOLOv5s_ReLU, most faults had no observable effect or only shifted confidence scores, but a smaller fraction induced missed detections, phantom objects, and rare high-confidence misclassifications while the system continued to operate normally. The impact can reach beyond individual inference errors. When corrupted detector outputs feed downstream tracking systems, even brief or low-probability errors can be filtered as transient noise, latched into persistent tracked objects, or amplified into denser and longer-lived false system states.
In the observed sequences, repeated, bounded faults transformed transient detector errors into sustained false perceptions that persisted beyond the original fault window. Once represented as system state, these errors can influence alerts, automation logic, and operator decisions while the platform appears healthy, which has implications for product teams. Here, traditional measures of resilience, such as uptime or fault recovery, may be insufficient for AI-driven systems. Resilience also must include inference integrity and the ability to prevent corrupted outputs from becoming trusted system state.
At the same time, decentralizing compute offers a foundational safety advantage in some applications, reducing how much sensitive information can leave the device. “Running inference on the device means sensitive data never travels, so there is no communication channel to intercept, and decentralized processing means there is no central repository of sensitive data to breach,” Efficient Computer’s Gobieski said. “A compromise costs you one device, not the fleet. The model itself carries the usual concerns about what it exposes, but those are far smaller than the ones you eliminate by keeping the data on the device.”
Conclusion
Navigating the edge AI landscape requires a mindset shift for engineering teams. Success no longer hinges just on maximizing theoretical peak compute, but on balancing silicon longevity with rapid software evolution. By prioritizing flexible architectures, hardware-software co-design, and defense-in-depth security from day one, chip designers can build resilient platforms that adapt to whatever AI workloads emerge — even after the chip architecture is finalized.

As AI, post-quantum cryptography, chiplets, and custom silicon expand the attack surface, semiconductor security is shifting from isolated safeguards to full-stack verification.

articles.title: The new Kindle ditches the bezel in a push toward a smaller, lighter e-reader | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Amazon is giving the Kindle its most significant physical redesign in years, introducing a refreshed lineup of e-readers built around a deceptively simple idea: getting rid of the bezel.
The redesigned Kindle unveiled Thursday replaces the traditional raised bezel surrounding the display with a flush-front design, creating a cleaner, more seamless look. But bezels also give readers a place to rest their fingers without accidentally touching the screen and triggering a page turn or another touchscreen command. Amazon says it has designed around that problem.
At a press briefing, Kevin Keith, Amazon’s vice president of devices, said the company is using “Cap” (capacitive) touch technology and haptics to create what he describes as a “dead zone.” As a reader grips the Kindle, the device detects where a finger is resting and adjusts the touch-sensitive area accordingly.
“When you’re gripping the Kindle, wherever you put your thumb, it will self-detect a dead zone in the Cap touch. It will just readjust, and it’ll know that the finger is there,” Keith said.
Alongside the bezel-free redesign, the standard six-inch Kindle is now 6.8 millimeters thick and weighs 140 grams, making it both thinner and lighter than its predecessor. Amazon is positioning it as the most pocket-friendly Kindle in the lineup.
Amazon said the new display is also 30% faster at page turns than the previous generation. The lineup also introduces new colors, including Ube, Alpine Sky, Seaglass Green, Graphite, and Fig.
The new Kindle starts at $149.99 and is available in Ube and Graphite. For the first time, Amazon is also offering an aluminum-backed version, with 32GB of storage and color options, including Alpine Sky and Seaglass Green.
The redesign extends to the Kindle Paperwhite, which is also thinner and lighter than the previous generation.
Amazon describes the Paperwhite as having the largest display in the Kindle lineup, along with the highest contrast ratio. The company says the combination is designed to deliver “deep blacks and crisp text, and images that pop off the screen, whether you’re reading in bright sunlight or under the covers at night.”
The standard Paperwhite comes with 16GB of storage and costs $199.99 in Graphite. A 32GB Signature Edition costs $249.99 and is available in Graphite and Seaglass Green.
The Kindle Colorsoft, which Amazon introduced in 2024 as its first Kindle with a color display, also adopts the thinner, lighter, flush-front design used across the refreshed lineup. The standard Colorsoft has 16GB of storage and starts at $289.99 in Graphite. A 32GB Signature Edition is available in Graphite and Fig for $319.99.
The new Kindle and its aluminum version are available starting today in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Brazil, the U.K., Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Sweden, Poland, Japan, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Egypt, and Australia.
The new Kindle Paperwhite and Kindle Colorsoft are available for preorder across the same regions.
Amazon is also continuing to offer its Kids lineup. The Kids Kindle is currently available for purchase, whereas the Kids Kindle Colorsoft is available for preorder in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Germany, and Japan.

articles.title: I can’t live without a 4K Blu-ray player for high-quality movie viewing — this Panasonic is among the best and is now down 25%
articles.text:
I can’t live without a 4K Blu-ray player for high-quality movie viewing — this Panasonic is among the best and is now down 25%
Physical media for the win!
With video streaming services seemingly on a constant mission to increase monthly prices in the name of ‘better content’, it’s perhaps no surprise that the idea of collecting physical media is becoming more popular.
We’ve seen it with the post-Covid resurgence of vinyl records, and more recently, CDs have been slowly but surely coming back. It’s not just music where physical media can offer a better experience though – the same can be said of movies. Naturally, we here at TechRadar value the best-possible picture and sound when watching films, so we’d consider a 4K Blu-ray player an essential part of any true movie buff’s setup.
If you’re keen on going physical and don’t yet own a player (or need an upgrade), the five-star Panasonic UB820 has had AU$230 shaved off its price at PB Tech, making it a very easy recommendation.
This Panasonic 4K Blu-ray player delivers on multiple fronts. It includes support for all major HDR formats, and serves up a hugely immersive and impactful picture, backed up with a strong audio performance.
While it is possible to spend less on a 4K Blu-ray player, doing so often can potentially involve some compromises, such as missing out on what many could consider essential features — support for all the major HDR formats, for example.
That’s not the case with the Panasonic DP-UB820. In our review of the 4K Blu-ray player, we said it “offers fantastic 4K image reproduction with vivid colours, deep black levels and stunning contrast, particularly when it comes to Dolby Vision”, and even its 4K upscaling is effective.
It’s a similar story for audio, which we said is “superb, with Dolby Atmos effects coming through clear and adding that extra layer of immersion to any movie”.
So while its price may seem like quite the investment, if you’re a serious film lover you’ll be well rewarded with a cinema-like experience from the comfort of your home.
I did notice this player is also discounted in the Amazon Prime Big Deal Days sale, where it’s dropped to AU$745. It’s the same price at The Good Guys, too.
However, it’s PB Tech that has the best price by some margin at AU$699.86.
Still, it’s worth mentioning that the DP-UB820 is significantly more expensive than Panasonic’s next model down, even at its discounted price — especially as some users may have little use for features such as analogue audio outputs for older receivers and slightly more advanced upscaling.
If the high-end model is still a bit too rich for you, the Panasonic DP-UB450 is the mid-range option, and is available at its (more affordable) regular price of AU$449 at Amazon, while the entry-level DP-UB150, which lacks a dedicated HDMI output for audio, is available for AU$337 at Appliances Online or Appliance Central.
The UB150 supports basic HDR10 and HLG, but lacks Dolby Vision and HDR10+, and misses out on Wi-Fi connectivity. The UB450 adds Dolby Vision and HDR10+ support, along with Dolby Atmos audio. It also misses out on Wi-Fi connectivity.
Of course, with any 4K Blu-ray player, you’ll need to consider the cost of building your physical disc collection. The upside is you’ll get better quality compared to streaming via a video-on-demand service, and that you’ll actually own your movies and shows — something which sounds increasingly appealing on the back of the news that Sony recently remotely deleted over 500 ‘purchased’ movies from their owners’ digital libraries.

articles.title: Grab this 10-port gigabit PoE+ switch with up to 60W of power for under $38, a new record low — Ugreen switch upgrades your home network with eight power-delivery ports for cameras and Wi-Fi extenders
articles.text:
Grab this 10-port gigabit PoE+ switch with up to 60W of power for under $38, a new record low — Ugreen switch upgrades your home network with eight power-delivery ports for cameras and Wi-Fi extenders
Unlock super-fast speeds for your network with up to 60W of power delivery
If you want to expand your home network with cameras, WiFi extenders, and other smart home tech, you'll want to invest in a good power-over-Ethernet switch. At the minute, a Ugreen 10-port PoE+ switch is on sale for just $37.79 on Amazon. That's a new record low for this model, and it unlocks eight extra PoE+ ports (and 10 in total) for your network, at a price that's much more affordable than many of its rivals.
● Check out this deal on Amazon
Ugreen is a brand that you'll see a lot on Amazon, from network gear like this to wall chargers and peripherals. It's budget-focused, with reasonable prices that hide some pretty well-designed hardware. Here, you're getting a 10-port switch that supports the PoE+ standard (IEEE 802.3at), which means it can deliver up to 30W of power for devices on each individual port.
In practice, that means you can hook up newer and much faster devices to this switch, with power and data both being delivered over a single Ethernet cable. The switch supports 60W in total using a cascade system. If the power draw hits 60W, it'll shut down ports to prevent overload, starting from port 8 to port 1, so you can prioritize the ports you want and need the most. The switch will automatically detect PoE devices, so it won't short out a normal device like your PC or laptop by accident. Extended power delivery mode means that you can connect devices as far as 820 feet away, too.
The Ugreen 10-port PoE+ network switch offers Gigabit speeds and 30W per-port of power over each Ethernet cable across eight different ports, with two ports used as uplink ports for data connection to your main network.
If you're building a smart home network with plenty of devices to power, a switch like this will prove useful. This particular Ugreen switch is unmanaged, so there isn't a huge setup process to work through, and it should work immediately when you plug it into your existing hardware. That does mean it'll lack some of the extra customization that a more expensive managed switch could offer, but for most users, the ease of use will be the bigger draw anyway.
Almost any Ethernet-ready device will work with this switch, even if they aren't able to take advantage of its power delivery. Laptops, PCs, NAS drives, printers, TVs, game consoles, IP cameras, and more will work with this switch.
You're also getting the bonus of speed here. This Ugreen switch delivers gigabit speeds across your network, so you can leave WiFi latency and lag issues far behind when you're playing games or streaming Netflix shows. Ethernet connections using this switch will help you max out the bandwidth from your ISP. You've also got two uplink ports which you can hook up to your existing network for the best bandwidth.
The $37.79 sale price for this 10-port Ugreen switch is a great one, but it's only around for a limited-time only. If you want to pick up this fanless, lightning-protected, compact Gigabit PoE+ switch, you'll need to get your order in before the deal runs out.
Ben Stockton is a deals writer at Tom’s Hardware. He's been writing about technology since 2018, with bylines at PCGamesN, How-To Geek, and Tom’s Guide, among others. When he’s not hunting down the best bargains, he’s busy tinkering with his homelab or watching old Star Trek episodes.

articles.title: Apple Pay finally launches in India; DBS Foundation’s Karen Ngui on uplifting communities
articles.text:
Apple Pay finally launches in India; DBS Foundation’s Karen Ngui on uplifting communities
Apple has launched its mobile payments service, Apple Pay, in India after years of waiting. The rollout gives iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch users a new way to make contactless payments at stores and online.
Dear Reader,
Corporate drama at Tata Sons has intensified over the past few months. Now, Venu Srinivasan, a member of two Tata Trusts and also of Tata Sons, has asked the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner to inquire into the governance structure of the Trust, according to a media report.
Srinivasan had alleged serious governance lapses in the Trusts and also its involvement in Tata Sons, which is a commercial enterprise. He has also written a letter in this regard to the Charity Commissioner of Maharashtra.
Moving on to the world of mobility, electric two-wheeler maker Simple Energy has raised Rs 1,750 crore in its Series C funding round, marking the third-largest funding round in a growing E2W space.
The fresh funding round was led by the Dr Arokiaswamy Velumani Family Office, alongside Simple Energy’s Founder and CEO Suhas Rajkumar and Co-founder and CFO Ankit Gupta, with participation from Bengaluru-based HNI Amit Mishra and the Haran Family Office.
Meanwhile, renewable energy company Inox Clean Energy has filed draft papers with the market regulator SEBI to raise up to Rs 10,000 crore through an initial public offering.
According to the Draft Red Herring Prospectus filed on Tuesday, the company is launching India's largest private-sector renewable energy IPO to date. The Rs 10,000 crore offering includes a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 8,000 crore and an Offer-for-Sale (OFS) of Rs 2,000 crore by promoter Devansh Jain.
Elsewhere, US-based local commerce platform DoorDash on Wednesday opened its talent hub in Hyderabad, its first India office. The company is starting with 500 professionals and plans to scale its headcount to more than 3,000 within the next two years, PTI reported citing a press release.
Lastly, Vithya Ramraj has displayed a stellar performance at the 2026 Asian Games, winning gold in the women’s 4x400m relay, silver in the mixed 4x400m relay and bronze in the 400m hurdles. She clocked 54.75 seconds to win bronze in 400m and break the Indian national record held by athletics legend PT Usha for 42 years.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- Apple Pay launches in India
- DBS Foundation’s Karen Ngui on uplifting communities
Here’s your trivia for today: Which Japanese multimedia giant gets its name from the shortened combination of its original corporate title, Nippon Kogaku? (Scroll down for answer)
Fintech
Apple Pay launches in India
Apple has launched its mobile payments service, Apple Pay, in India after years of waiting. The rollout gives iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch users a new way to make contactless payments at stores and online.
The launch kicks off with exclusive support for Axis Bank credit cards on the Visa and Mastercard networks. Users can add their cards to Apple Wallet and use Apple Pay at participating merchants and websites that support the service.
Key takeaways:
- Apple Pay does not currently support UPI, India’s dominant digital payments system, or RuPay cards, the country’s domestic card network.
- Payments provider PayU has integrated Apple Pay across its merchant network as well, making it instantly available at thousands of digital storefronts and physical retail outlets.
- According to Apple, security remains its key focus. Actual card numbers are never stored directly on the user's device or on Apple servers, nor are they shared with merchants during a transaction.

DBS Foundation’s Karen Ngui on uplifting communities
Karen Ngui, Head of DBS Foundation, outlines the foundation's decade-long evolution in an interview with SocialStory. Set up in 2014, the foundation expanded its initial focus from supporting social enterprises to directly empowering vulnerable communities through social and financial resilience initiatives.
DBS Bank has committed SGD 1 billion over 10 years (approx. SGD 100 million annually) alongside 1.5 million employee volunteer hours across its key markets. In India, DBS Foundation collaborates with local ground partners and social enterprises to address education, skill development, financial literacy, and demographic shifts around ageing.
Key takeaways:
- Ngui says the foundation’s focus is on uplifting the lives and livelihoods of vulnerable communities in Asia, predominantly across six key markets: Singapore, India, Indonesia, Hong Kong, China, and Taiwan.
- Beyond standard grant-giving, DBS Foundation uses seed/early-stage capital to de-risk innovative social business models (like Life Circle Health Services).
- Rather than imposing top-down solutions, DBS Foundation co-creates programs directly with on-the-ground Indian partners.

articles.title: On-demand GPU infrastructure startup GMI Cloud raises $263M to fuel global expansion - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
On-demand GPU infrastructure startup GMI Cloud raises $263M to fuel global expansion
Taiwan-based neocloud GMI Cloud Inc. wants to capitalize on what it says is an “unprecedented” demand for artificial intelligence computing power after raising a massive $663 million in funding from two sources.
The startup said today it has just closed on a $223 million Series B round of funding led by the robotics and AI-focused investment firm ARCHIV, with participation from Nvidia Corp., Redwood, DSC Investment, KT Corp., Kyobo Life, KB Investment and Trend Micro Inc. At the same time, it has secured a $440 million credit facility from ChinaTrust Commercial Bank, one of the largest financial institutions in Taiwan.
GMI Cloud is one of a host of specialized cloud infrastructure providers that have emerged in recent years to cater to the growing demand for access to graphics processing units and other resources needed to power AI workloads. The best-known of these neoclouds is CoreWeave Inc., which went public last year and has quickly become one of the darlings of Wall Street amid the AI boom. In Europe, there’s Nebius Group N.V., which rebranded from Yandex N.V. after selling off its Russian search engine firm Yandex.
Like its rivals, GMI Cloud offers an AI infrastructure-as-a-service platform that’s specially designed for resource-intensive AI training and inference workloads. It provides on-demand access to some of the most powerful GPUs available, including Nvidia’s H100 and H200 chips and its even newer Vera Rubin GPUs.
Its platform is powered by a proprietary Kubernetes-based infrastructure management system it calls the Cluster Engine, which automates resource allocation and instance provisioning so that developers can focus on their applications only. It’s a powerful advantage, because it means developers can spin up GPU clusters based on preconfigured environments in a matter of seconds. On traditional cloud infrastructure platforms, developers would have to manually configure these environments themselves.
GMI Cloud’s strong presence in the Asia-Pacific region is another key advantage, especially compared with CoreWeave and Nebius, whose data centers are mostly centered on the U.S. and Europe. The startup has dozens of data centers dotted around Taiwan, Thailand and Malaysia, which puts it in a strong position to cater to enterprises that want to run AI workloads locally in the region. However, it’s also building up a presence in the U.S., as well as a sovereign AI initiative in Japan that was launched earlier in the year.
Founder and Chief Executive Alex Yeh said demand for AI compute infrastructure has gone global. U.S.-based hyperscalers and AI startups are desperate to find more GPU capacity in Asia, where they have significant customer bases. In addition, there are thousands of APAC-based enterprises spearheading AI projects too, and all of these need a local source of compute.
“Our customers are scaling faster than ever and they need infrastructure that keeps pace,” Yeh said. “AI is driving a new renaissance and reliable compute is its foundation. Our goal is to build that foundation across continents, with an ecosystem of products on top of it.”
Being based in Taiwan gives GMI Cloud another major advantage, because the country also happens to be the world’s biggest factory for the AI server systems that populate data centers around the globe. Its close proximity to so many suppliers means the startup has an extremely secure supply chain and the ability to quickly procure all of the systems it needs to get its new data centers up and running, no matter where in the world they’re located.
“In AI infrastructure, a delivery date is a promise,” Yeh explained. “Customers plan launches, hiring and revenue around those dates. Our place in Taiwan’s supply chain is how we keep that promise, cluster after cluster globally.”
This reliability has already paid off for GMI Cloud in a big way. The startup said the amount of annual recurring revenue it has under contract is set to grow 10-fold at the end of the year from what it was in December 2025. As for ARR that’s already being realized, this is up five-fold in the last year, with its inference platform processing an average of more than 4 trillion tokens per week. It boasts a number of major enterprise customers, including Higgsfield Inc., OpenRouter, Nous Research Inc., Fireworks AI Inc. and Trend Micro.

articles.title: „Wie biologische Überbrückungskabel“: So wollen Forscher Querschnittsgelähmten helfen
articles.text:
Therapien bei Querschnittslähmung: Wie Forscher um jede kleine Bewegung kämpfen
Sommer 2025, ein Urlaub in Mexiko, ein Autounfall – und das Leben der Familie Staub aus Königsbrunn gerät aus den Fugen. Den jüngsten Sohn Oliver erwischte es am schlimmsten. Kopf und Wirbelsäule waren regelrecht auseinandergebrochen. „Es handelte sich um eine Verletzung im oberen Halswirbelbereich, eine vollständige Lähmung, bei der sowohl das Rückenmark als auch die Nerven, die Bänder und die Knochen völlig zertrümmert waren“, sagt später der behandelnde Neurochirurg.
Dieser Text erscheint in der Ausgabe 7/2026 von MIT Technology Review. Darin beschäftigen wir uns damit, wie KI die IT-Sicherheit auf den Kopf stellt. Das Heft ist ab sofort in unserem Online-Shop und im Zeitschriftenhandel erhältlich.
Oliver überlebte. Doch die Perspektive, dass er sein ganzes Leben im Rollstuhl verbringen würde, abhängig von einem Beatmungsgerät, nicht in der Lage, seine Hände zu benutzen oder selbstständig Blase und Darm zu leeren, ließ die Eltern verzweifeln. „Das sollte alles gewesen sein?“, schreiben sie auf ihrem Blog Olivers Journey. Das Paar begann zu recherchieren und stieß auf eine neue Therapie für Querschnittsgelähmte: die Stammzelltherapie – und damit auf Mohamad Bydon. Der US-Chirurg von der University of Chicago hatte eine erste klinische Studie zur Stammzelltherapie abgeschlossen. Einige Teilnehmende konnten an zuvor tauben Stellen wieder etwas spüren und gewannen an Muskelkraft, ein Patient kann heute sogar wieder gehen.
Die Staubs kontaktierten Bydon von Mexiko aus, wo sie seit dem Unfall bei Mutter Lauras Familie leben. Für den Arzt war es ein „Wunder“, dass Oliver überhaupt überlebt hatte. Er operierte den damals Zweijährigen, fixierte Kopf und Wirbelsäule über eine Metallplatte im Nacken. Eine zweite von vorne separiert Rückenmark und Rachen. Für die Stammzelltherapie fehlt noch eine Genehmigung. Es wäre das erste Mal, dass ein Kind damit behandelt wird.

articles.title: Rakuten France ferme ce soir, voici comment récupérer vos factures et vos points avant qu'il ne soit trop tard
articles.text:
La plateforme Rakuten France ferme ce mercredi 30 septembre à 23h59, faute de repreneur. Si vous y avez déjà acheté un produit, deux échéances à retenir : les points Club R expirent ce soir, et l’accès à votre compte, avec l’historique de vos commandes, sera définitivement fermé le 10 novembre. Voici comment ne rien perdre.
Une fermeture actée après l’échec de plusieurs reprises
À partir de jeudi 1er octobre, il ne sera plus possible d’acheter ni de vendre sur la plateforme, ex-PriceMinister, lancée en 2000 et rachetée par le groupe japonais Rakuten en 2010. Environ 180 salariés sont concernés. La fermeture touche aussi l’Espagne, qui dépend de la même structure.
Rakuten France cherchait un repreneur depuis plusieurs mois. Selon la direction, citée par Le Monde, aucune offre ne remplissait les trois critères fixés : préservation des emplois, conditions financières et pérennité de l’activité à long terme. Le comité économique et social a rendu un avis négatif sur ces propositions. Pixmania, l’un des candidats évincés, avait dénoncé en juillet le rejet de son offre, qu’il disait « financièrement soutenue » par ses actionnaires, et craint que sa candidature n’ait servi qu’à remplir l’obligation légale de rechercher un repreneur avant une fermeture (loi Florange).
En cause, un déclin engagé depuis une dizaine d’années : le nombre de clients a chuté de 33 % en dix ans, et le trafic de 42 % sur la même période, sous l’effet notamment du succès des plateformes chinoises comme Shein et Temu.
Vendeurs : vos fonds restent en sécurité
Si vous vendiez sur Rakuten, votre argent n’est pas géré directement par la plateforme mais par Mangopay, son partenaire de paiement agréé. « Vos fonds restent en sécurité et la continuité des paiements liés à vos ventes demeure une priorité absolue », assure Rakuten sur sa page dédiée aux vendeurs. Les sommes qui n’auraient pas encore été reversées au 10 novembre resteront disponibles : après cette date, il faudra simplement s’adresser directement à Mangopay pour les récupérer. Rakuten conseille de finaliser sans tarder toute vérification d’identité en attente, pour faciliter le versement.
Récupérez vos factures avant le 10 novembre
Rakuten n’édite pas de facture lui-même : c’est le vendeur qui la fournit. Si vous avez acheté à un professionnel et que vous n’avez pas votre facture, demandez-la depuis le suivi de commande, dans votre compte. Sans réponse, une réclamation ouverte au même endroit permet de relancer le vendeur. Pour un achat effectué auprès d’un particulier, Rakuten fournit à la place une attestation d’achat, qui fait office de reçu : rendez-vous dans « Tous mes achats », puis « Imprimer l’attestation d’achat », uniquement depuis le site, l’application mobile ne proposant pas cette option.
Dans tous les cas, mieux vaut agir avant le 10 novembre, 23h59, car c’est la date à laquelle l’accès à votre compte et à tout votre historique de transactions sera définitivement fermé. Pensez aussi à conserver de votre côté les e-mails de confirmation, des captures d’écran des annonces, ainsi que les coordonnées et le nom officiel des vendeurs : dans deux ans, un simple pseudonyme ne suffira plus.
Trois dates à retenir
- Ce mercredi 30 septembre, 23h59 : dernier moment pour acheter, vendre ou utiliser vos points Club R
- 10 novembre, 23h59 : fermeture définitive de l’accès aux comptes et à l’historique de commandes
- 30 novembre : dernier jour pour joindre le service client au sujet des transactions en cours, paiements et reversements
Vos points Club R expirent ce soir
Vous avez encore des points Club R ? Rakuten indique que vous pouvez les utiliser normalement jusqu’à la fermeture de la plateforme, ce mercredi 23h59, mais ils seront ensuite « définitivement perdus ». Trois options avant l’échéance : les dépenser sur le site, les échanger contre des cartes cadeaux, ou demander leur virement sur votre compte bancaire.
Vos garanties restent valables, mais le recours change
La fermeture de la plateforme n’annule pas vos garanties. La Garantie Rakuten couvre les litiges pendant 14 jours après la livraison, ou 30 jours après la confirmation de commande si le colis n’avait pas de numéro de suivi, y compris si ce délai se termine après la fermeture. Le service client reste joignable par téléphone, chat ou formulaire.
Passé ce délai, c’est la garantie légale de conformité qui prend le relais, pour deux ans après la livraison d’un produit neuf. Le vendeur professionnel en reste seul responsable, que Rakuten existe encore ou non. Si Rakuten promet de le relancer « dans la mesure du possible » en cas de silence du vendeur, le traitement de la demande dépendra ensuite entièrement de lui, d’où l’intérêt de conserver une preuve d’achat.
Rakuten précise enfin que les données personnelles restent traitées dans le cadre du RGPD, avec un engagement à prévenir les clients en cas d’évolution.

articles.title: QNAP Launches QSW-M5218 Series L3 Lite Managed 25 GbE Switches
articles.text:
Wednesday, September 30th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
QNAP Launches QSW-M5218 Series L3 Lite Managed 25 GbE Switches
QNAP Systems, Inc., a leading computing, networking, and storage solution innovator, today announced the new QSW-M5218 Series L3 Lite managed switches, including the QSW-M5218-6F12T and the PoE-capable QSW-M5218P-6F12T. Aimed at SMBs and applications that demand high-speed network infrastructure—such as AV over IP transmission—the series features twelve 10GbE RJ45 ports and six 25GbE SFP28 uplink ports, with a switching capacity of up to 540 Gbps. By combining L3 Lite routing, MC-LAG high availability, and IEEE 1588v2 PTP precise time synchronization, it helps enterprises overcome core network bandwidth bottlenecks and build a stable, high-performance IT infrastructure with a seamless upgrade path.
As NAS devices, servers, and workstations move to 10GbE, traditional 1G/2.5G ports and a single 10G uplink are increasingly becoming performance bottlenecks. The QSW-M5218 Series uses high-density 10GbE interfaces to connect high-speed NAS, virtualization servers, and multimedia workstations, while its 25GbE SFP28 ports act as a high-bandwidth backbone that aggregates traffic into the enterprise core—delivering up to 2.5 times the per-port uplink bandwidth of 10G. At the endpoints, existing Cat 6a copper cabling can be reused without the need to lay new fiber, streamlining core network upgrades.High-speed connectivity alone is not enough. Enterprises that need both 25GbE high-speed uplinks and inter-subnet routing have traditionally had to deploy complex, costly L3 core switches. The QSW-M5218 Series is the ideal solution, designed around a core philosophy: the simplicity and low barrier to entry of near-L2 deployment, combined with the L3 routing capabilities every enterprise needs. Compared with L2 managed switches that offer only VLAN/QoS, the QSW-M5218 Series has built-in L3 Lite, handling IPv4 / IPv6 static routing, a DHCP server, and inter-VLAN routing locally to offload the core router and cut latency. And compared with L3 Full models that add OSPF/BGP dynamic routing, it significantly reduces costs, making it a perfect fit for the real-world needs of SMBs and multi-segment environments.
Ruby Chan, Product Manager at QNAP"As 10GbE moves out of the core server room and onto the work floor, the real bottleneck shifts from the endpoints to the uplinks and power. The QSW-M5218 Series brings 25GbE uplinks, L3 Lite routing, MC-LAG redundancy, and PoE power delivery together in a single switch, letting enterprises build a stable, scalable, and easy-to-manage high-speed backbone with a leaner investment."

- L3 Lite Advanced Routing to Ease the Core Load: Built-in IPv4 / IPv6 dual stack, DNS, static routing, DHCP server, SNTP, and inter-VLAN routing let the switch map inter-segment traffic paths locally, improving internal network efficiency and reducing the load on the core router.
- MC-LAG High Availability and LACP: Multi-Chassis Link Aggregation (MC-LAG) consolidates the links between multiple switches into a single logical connection, so the network keeps running even if some physical links fail. Paired with QNAP NAS High Availability (HA), it provides dual-layer protection across the storage and network layers, while Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) support increases throughput and connection reliability.
- Hardware-Level PTP and IGMP Snooping for Professional AV Synchronization: Support for IEEE 1588v2 PTP and Transparent Clock provides sub-microsecond time synchronization at the hardware level and compensates for switching latency. Together with IGMP Snooping, which precisely manages multiple multicast streams and prevents surplus traffic from saturating bandwidth, media servers, NAS, and video walls stay in frame-accurate synchronization in AVoIP environments.
- PoE Model for Leaner Cabling (QSW-M5218P-6F12T): The PoE version supplies up to 90 W per port and a total power budget of 470 W, fully powering as many as 12 PoE+ (30 W) wireless access points or IP surveillance cameras, and can also drive high-power devices such as Wi-Fi 7 access points and PTZ cameras—with no need for extra power cabling or separate power injectors. VLAN isolation and 25GbE uplinks keep the backbone free of congestion when high-speed wireless traffic converges.
- Built-in Cybersecurity Ecosystem: Integrates with ADRA NDR X Network Detection and Response on QNAP NAS to proactively detect and isolate ransomware and abnormal traffic, and supports the QNAP Airgap+ isolated backup solution to reduce the risk of the backup environment being compromised in a network attack.
- QSS Pro Intelligent Management and AMIZcloud Centralized Cloud Control: Featuring an intuitive web GUI, QSS Pro (QNAP Switch System Pro) simplifies L2/L3 Lite management and online firmware updates. Through the AMIZcloud cloud platform, it can monitor switches across multiple sites with no additional hardware or software, enabling remote IT troubleshooting while lowering operating costs.

- QSW-M5218P-6F12T: 12x 10GbE RJ45 PoE ports, 6x 25GbE SFP28 uplink ports, and a switching capacity of up to 540 Gbps, with PoE++ (IEEE 802.3bt) power delivery of up to 90 W per port and a total power budget of 470 W, plus L3 Lite managed features.

articles.title: Attackers have been exploiting critical Zimbra flaw to steal emails
articles.text:
Hackers have been exploiting a critical vulnerability in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite in an attempt to obtain email backups and authentication credentials of vulnerable organzations, Microsoft has warned.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-73570, lets attackers remotely issue operating system commands without authentication. Zimbra maintainer Synacor issued a patch on July 20, but didn’t disclose the vulnerability for more than three weeks after that. The security-focused Shadowserver Foundation said last week that its scans found that 274 separate instances of the Zimbra Collaboration Suite had been compromised. The number of servers running the software has fluctuated from 19,000 in the week following the patch to about 12,000 in the weeks following that. Currently, Shadowserver is tracking about 10,000 instances.
Look, ma, no authorization
From July 28 to August 7, Microsoft said Wednesday, the company detected two distinct scanning tools probing the Internet for vulnerable endpoints. The attackers first validated their exploit worked by sending HTTP, requests and DNS, ICMP, and out-of-band identity checks to domains hosted on public services. The probes allowed the attackers to confirm the exploit successfully executed commands on vulnerable servers without actually compromising them. Eventually, the attackers began using their command injection capability to install malicious payloads. Microsoft wrote:
Following successful exploitation, observed activity included deployment of JSP web shells and reverse shells, privilege escalation, persistent remote-access tooling, and memory-backed execution. Threat actors also accessed email and collected authentication and mailbox data, with archive creation and subsequent transfer activity observed. The activity included both automated payload delivery and hands-on-keyboard operations on compromised mail servers. Microsoft observed affected organizations in more than one region and industry. Based on the environments investigated, exploitation was not limited to a single sector or geographic area.
CVE-2026-73570 allows remote attackers with no credentials to run operating system commands through a crafted email that targets the ZCS SNMP notification path but only when an optional zimbra-snmp package is in place and SNMP notifications are enabled.

articles.title: Suas fotos podem “desaparecer”: Samsung encerra integração com Microsoft • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Suas fotos podem “desaparecer”: Samsung encerra integração com Microsoft
Fotografias salvas na nuvem não ficarão mais disponíveis na galeria, mas podem ser baixadas no app da Microsoft.
Os usuários de celular Samsung devem notar, a partir de hoje (30/09), o fim da integração do Galaxy com o OneDrive, serviço de nuvem da Microsoft. Isso significa que todas as fotografias armazenadas no serviço digital vão “desaparecer” da galeria nativa da Samsung, segundo um comunicado da própria Microsoft.
Para não perder suas fotos e vídeos no celular Galaxy, é necessário baixar as fotos manualmente na galeria até o fim do dia, segundo a Samsung australiana. Todo o conteúdo já sincronizado com o Microsoft OneDrive seguirá disponível na nuvem da Microsoft, mas será necessário baixar o app oficial para acessá-lo.
Os adeptos do OneDrive ainda poderão fazer o backup das fotos, mas será necessário instalar o app dedicado a isso, que está disponível na Google Play Store. É necessário ativar a função de backup de câmera, de modo que as fotografias feitas com o smartphone sejam enviadas automaticamente para a nuvem.
O passo a passo é o seguinte:
Se você foi pego de surpresa, provavelmente suas fotos já não estão mais disponíveis na galeria. A boa notícia é que elas não foram deletadas, mas sim retiradas do app da Samsung. Para acessá-las, basta usar o app Microsoft OneDrive no celular.
A Microsoft australiana divulgou os passos abaixo:
Também é possível fazer o procedimento com fotos específicas:
Os smartphones da Samsung não devem ficar sem backup nativo de fotos. Nós fizemos testes com o Galaxy S26 Ultra e notamos que o aparelho ofereceu a opção de “desvincular o OneDrive da Galeria” já na manhã desta quarta-feira.
Essa informação apareceu por um aviso no topo do app de Galeria. Ao tocar nele, surge uma nova tela explicando que, ao adotar este procedimento, o usuário encerra a sincronização entre a Galeria e o OneDrive “em todos os seus aparelhos”.
Na sequência, o Galaxy oferece a sincronização das imagens de “todos os seus aparelhos” com o Google. O usuário precisa escolher qual conta Google será usada na integração e, na tela seguinte, passar por ajustes como o upload em redes móveis e a seleção das pastas que serão enviadas para a nuvem.
A Samsung já havia confirmado uma parceria com o serviço do Google, pensando nas TVs com inteligência artificial.
