articles.title: Windows 11 da otro paso para que uses Linux sin reiniciar el PC
articles.text:
Usar Windows y Linux en un solo ordenador ha sido posible gracias al dual boot. Esta opción es una de las más recomendadas para aquellos entusiastas que no están listos para abandonar el sistema operativo de Microsoft. La buena noticia es que los de Redmond han implementado una nueva función en Windows 11 que puede reducir la necesidad de reiniciar en Linux.
De acuerdo con una publicación en su blog, Microsoft lanzó los contenedores de WSL, una función que permite ejecutar aplicaciones empaquetadas de Linux dentro de Windows 11 de forma nativa. Tras una fase de pruebas que comenzó hace meses, la compañía ha liberado esta característica para todos los usuarios. Esto podría ayudar a probar aplicaciones, bases de datos o ejecutar cargas de IA sin necesidad de instalar todo en Windows.
Los contenedores funcionan como una caja aislada que incluye la aplicación, sus bibliotecas y dependencias, así como también su configuración. Si bien la idea no es nueva (Linux los usa desde hace años), la implementación en Windows 11 implica que ya no tendremos que usar herramientas de terceros para ejecutarlos. Microsoft los integra de forma nativa, lo que facilita ejecutar cargas de trabajo sin depender de software adicional.
La nueva característica se apoya en el subsistema de Windows para Linux (WSL), que ya permite ejecutar distribuciones como Ubuntu o Debian dentro de Windows, abrir una terminal, compilar código con GCC, lanzar scripts de Bash y usar herramientas nativas del ecosistema Linux.
En el caso de los contenedores WSL, Microsoft incluyó nuevas funciones como comprobaciones de salud, transmisión de eventos en tiempo real, más control sobre la red y una ruta de almacenamiento configurable. También se añaden comandos nuevos para reiniciar contenedores, copiar archivos hacia dentro y hacia fuera, conectar redes o consultar el estado general del entorno.
Microsoft sigue añadiendo funciones de Linux en Windows 11
En su anuncio oficial, Microsoft afirma que ve a Linux en Windows como "una plataforma estratégica de ejecución" para cargas de IA y aplicaciones nativas de la nube. Aunque estos cambios están más enfocados hacia los desarrolladores, los usuarios entusiastas pueden beneficiarse de las nuevas funciones. Para ciertos flujos de trabajo, los contenedores han sido una de las razones para recurrir a una instalación nativa de Linux.
Aunque el cambio es bienvenido, vale la pena ser realistas y no esperar milagros. Docker Desktop sigue siendo una de las mejores opciones para gestionar contenedores, gracias a su ecosistema maduro. Otro detalle es que falta soporte para compose, la función más pedida por los usuarios. Microsoft ya confirmó que está trabajando en que wslc compose up funcione con tus archivos compose.yaml sin modificarlos, aunque todavía no tiene una fecha definida para que esto ocurra.
Sumado a los contenedores, Microsoft reveló que están investigando cómo mejorar el subsistema de Windows para Linux. La versión actual ofrece el doble de rendimiento al acceder a archivos de Windows desde Linux, uno de los cuellos de botella más comunes de los sistemas operativos. La tecnológica también integró un nuevo modo de red optimizado para flujos de trabajo con contenedores, el cual mejora la compatibilidad de red entre desarrolladores y empresas.
“Seguiremos invirtiendo en el rendimiento, la compatibilidad y la integración que hacen de Windows un lugar ideal para construir con Linux”, dijo Logan Iyer, vicepresidente de la plataforma Windows y Desarrolladores.

articles.title: Hackers stole millions of US military personnel records during months-long data breach | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The U.S. government is alerting millions of current and former U.S. military service members and staff that their personal information was stolen during a months-long breach of the Pentagon’s personnel records, the latest in a spate of thefts involving federal workers’ data in recent months.
A data breach notification from the Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) shared on Reddit says that several unauthorized users exploited a security vulnerability in an unspecified file-sharing system over several months between October 2025 and mid-July 2026.
The breach exposed personally identifiable information, including Social Security numbers, alongside a person’s name, date of birth, sex, race, and other information about their military service. The notice says that the personnel records were not encrypted.
According to CNN and Federal News Network, a Pentagon official said the breach affects about 2.8 million living people, and close to 300,000 people who are deceased.
The U.S. military has 1.3 million active service members as of March.
Susan Gough, a spokesperson for the Department of Defense, confirmed the number of those affected in an emailed statement, but did not answer TechCrunch’s questions about the incident, such as if U.S. officials had any communications from the hackers, whose identities are not yet known.
The DMDC may not be widely known to the general public, but serves as one of the Department of Defense’s records-keeping units. The DMDC maintains over 60 million records for U.S. military and civilian staff and their family members to help determine benefits and entitlements, such as healthcare and retirement. The unit also provides a critical service as the military’s “leading identity management provider,” which links active service members, employees, and contractors to credentials, such as smart cards and passwords. These are used to access Pentagon computer systems, buildings, and bases.
“We make sure that the right people get access and the wrong people don’t: security of identity information is paramount,” the DMDC’s website reads.
The Department of Defense, which oversees the DMDC, said it does not have any indication that the information was misused, but did not say how it reached that conclusion.
This is the latest major breach of federal workers’ personal information in recent months, following a recent breach at the FBI earlier in September attributed to the ShinyHunters hacking group. The hackers told TechCrunch that they had taken the personal information of most of the FBI’s agents and staffers, including applicants. The breach has been billed as a “counterintelligence disaster” amid the risks that a foreign government could obtain and use the information to profile, target, or coerce federal workers into handing over sensitive information.
The ShinyHunters hackers have said that they will not publicly release the stolen FBI data.
Both breaches involving the FBI and the DMDC mirror similar thefts of government personnel records in the past. In 2015, a breach of the U.S. government’s human resources department, known as the Office of Personnel Management, was broadly attributed to China. The theft allowed the hackers to steal the private records of more than 22 million U.S. government employees, many of whom had security clearances.
Did you receive a notice about this data breach? We want to hear from you. You can contact this reporter securely on Signal at zackwhittaker.1337, or reach him by email at zack.whittaker@techcrunch.com.
Updated with comment from the Department of Defense.

articles.title: Open Security Foundations Are Only The Beginning: Deploying Caliptra Hardware in Production
articles.text:
Roots of trust are beginning to assume a broader role as platform security orchestrators.
As AI models, training data, and proprietary workloads become more valuable, the need to protect them rises concurrently. Data center security has always been mission critical, but the imperative for more robust and effective safeguards is higher than ever. This is occurring in an environment of growing complexity where data center architectures are becoming increasingly heterogeneous, with CPUs, accelerators, SmartNICs, DPUs, memory subsystems, and specialized controllers working together to execute ever more demanding workloads. This architectural evolution delivers impressive performance gains, but it also creates a significant challenge: trust must be established across a large and complex collection of devices.
With attackers increasingly motivated to target the lower layers of the system stack, security can no longer begin at the operating system. It must start in hardware, with a trusted foundation that establishes device identity, verifies the integrity of code, protects cryptographic assets, and enables trusted attestation throughout a device’s lifecycle. In other words, it must start with a Root of Trust in hardware.
This growing need for a common trust framework is one of the reasons the industry is exploring Caliptra technology, an open-source silicon Root of Trust architecture designed for data center-class devices.
Hardware Roots of Trust have traditionally been tailored to the security, performance, and lifecycle requirements of individual products. These purpose-built implementations remain essential for many applications, but differences in architecture, interfaces, and trust models can make it more complex for cloud providers and infrastructure operators to establish consistent trust across hardware from multiple suppliers.
Caliptra provides an open-source silicon Root of Trust architecture for data center-class devices. It defines common mechanisms for device identity, measured boot, and attestation that can help improve consistency across implementations. With support from several cloud and semiconductor companies, the project is emerging as one approach to greater alignment on hardware trust.
Its open development model allows security architects to review the architecture, firmware, documentation, and implementation details. This transparency supports evaluation, collaboration, and interoperability across the ecosystem. For organizations considering Caliptra, it provides a shared technical framework that can complement the differentiated security capabilities required for production deployments.
End-customer requirements are also driving increased adoption. Cloud and data center operators increasingly expect chip suppliers to provide Caliptra trademark-compliant implementations, giving customers greater confidence that Caliptra has been integrated in accordance with the project’s defined requirements. To qualify, vendors must complete a conformance process in which their architecture and implementation are evaluated against the Caliptra integration checklist.
Caliptra’s growing momentum raises an important question. Once the decision to adopt Caliptra has been made, what comes next?
For many engineering teams, selecting a Root of Trust architecture appears to be the difficult decision. In practice, however, the real work often begins after that choice has been made. An open-source Root of Trust establishes a valuable foundation, but commercial deployment introduces requirements that extend well beyond the baseline implementation. Development teams must determine how trust will be extended across the wider SoC, how cryptographic services will be exposed to software, how secure boot will be coordinated across multiple subsystems, and how attestation will integrate with platform management frameworks.
Additional challenges quickly emerge. Certification objectives must be defined. Secure provisioning flows must be implemented. Lifecycle management policies must be established. Software interfaces, drivers, and applications must be developed and maintained. Organizations also need a strategy for long-term maintenance, support, and vulnerability remediation.
These requirements are not unique to Caliptra. They are realities associated with operationalizing any hardware security architecture. However, they often become visible only after teams move beyond the evaluation phase and begin preparing a product for deployment. As a result, the industry conversation is increasingly shifting from Root of Trust adoption toward Root of Trust deployment.
There is another important trend that is reshaping hardware security architectures. Traditionally, a Root of Trust functioned primarily as an isolated security anchor. It protected keys, verified software integrity, and established an initial chain of trust. While these capabilities remain essential, today’s complex platforms often require something more comprehensive.
Modern data center devices contain multiple processors, memories, accelerators, firmware domains, and management subsystems, often supporting workloads from multiple tenants on shared infrastructure. Security policies must therefore span the entire platform, protecting tenant data, workloads, and cryptographic assets across these interconnected components rather than within a single security block. As a result, Roots of Trust are beginning to assume a broader role as platform security orchestrators.
This orchestration function can include coordinating secure boot across multiple domains, managing lifecycle states, supporting system-level attestation, enforcing security policies, and maintaining trust relationships across the entire SoC. Rather than acting solely as an isolated security module, the Root of Trust becomes the coordinator of platform-wide trust.
As systems continue to become more heterogeneous, this broader visibility and control may prove just as important as the traditional security functions themselves.
Moving from a reference implementation to a deployable security architecture requires more than adding features. Production readiness typically includes secure execution environments, protected key storage, lifecycle management frameworks, integration software, certification preparedness, and robust software interfaces. It must also account for cryptographic change, providing the agility to adopt new classical, post-quantum, or regional algorithms as standards and requirements evolve. Development teams additionally require documentation, maintenance processes, and a clear model for long-term ownership and support.
Side-channel resistance and fault injection protections become increasingly important as products move into real-world deployment environments. Certification-oriented development often requires clearly defined security boundaries and supporting documentation. Even seemingly straightforward tasks such as software integration can consume significant engineering resources when they must be developed entirely from scratch.
Viewed collectively, these requirements illustrate why deployment often becomes the most demanding phase of the security journey.
This deployment challenge is the motivation behind Rambus CryptoManager Root of Trust for Use with the Caliptra Specification. Rather than modifying or replacing Caliptra, it operates alongside an unchanged Caliptra implementation. This allows chip vendors to retain the implementation needed to pursue Caliptra trademark compliance, while the CryptoManager Root of Trust extends trust across the broader SoC and adds the infrastructure required for commercial deployment.
Fig. 1: CryptoManager Root of Trust and Caliptra integration.
CryptoManager provides a secure execution environment, protected key and data storage, platform-level security orchestration, dedicated Caliptra drivers, system applications, and an integration framework intended to simplify deployment. It also supports a broad range of classical, post-quantum, and regional cryptographic algorithms through a programmable architecture designed to accommodate crypto agility for future evolution.
At the platform level, the CryptoManager Root of Trust helps coordinate secure boot, attestation, lifecycle management, and security policy enforcement across the wider SoC. Advanced side-channel and fault-injection countermeasures provide additional protection for security-sensitive operations, while certification-oriented design principles help support development efforts targeting frameworks such as FIPS 140-3, PSA Certified, and SESIP.
The objective is straightforward: allow engineering teams to spend less time constructing security infrastructure and more time focusing on product differentiation.
Open security foundations are becoming an increasingly important part of the semiconductor industry. Caliptra is helping establish a common framework for trust across data center and AI infrastructure, providing a foundation that many organizations are now choosing to build upon.
But adopting a common foundation is only the first step. Engineering teams must still transform that foundation into a secure, supportable, and production-ready deployment capable of protecting increasingly valuable workloads and data. CryptoManager Root of Trust for use with Caliptra specification is designed to help bridge this gap by operating alongside an unchanged Caliptra implementation and adding platform security orchestration, certification readiness, cryptographic agility, lifecycle management, and the integration infrastructure required for commercial deployment.
The question facing the industry is no longer whether a common Root of Trust framework is needed. The question is how to operationalize that trust across increasingly complex systems. By combining Caliptra’s common foundation with the production-ready capabilities of CryptoManager, organizations can accelerate their path toward secure AI and cloud infrastructure.

articles.title: StuckInProfit, AFAZ partner on Africa–Azerbaijan enterprise development pilot - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
African SME-focused business education company StuckInProfit has partnered with the Africa–Azerbaijan Cooperation (AFAZ) to launch a three-week virtual professional and enterprise development programme, to kick off in November.
The StuckInProfit × AFAZ Professional & Enterprise Development Programme 2026 will see participants coached by a network of AFAZ instructors across 11 areas, including project presentation, emotional intelligence, leadership, virtual collaboration, time management, finance for non-finance professionals, entrepreneurship, critical thinking, creativity and intercultural communication.
The programme’s instructors are drawn largely from Azerbaijan’s academic, corporate and development sectors. They include ADA University senior instructor Aygün Mammadova, international development specialist Nadir Guluzade, former Ministry of Economy official Natig Madatov, and Hokuma Karimova, director of public relations and corporate communications at Nar (Azerfon).
Beyond the pilot, the partners say the longer-term goal is to build practical bridges between African entrepreneurs, SMEs and professional talent and international ecosystems through education, capacity development and market knowledge.

articles.title: Temporary Disaster Roaming has been activated to keep users connected during natural disasters - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Australia’s three major mobile operators – Telstra, Optus and Vodafone – have today activated Temporary Disaster Roaming (TDR) to keep remote and regional Australians connected in the event of a natural disaster causing mobile network outages.
TDR can be activated in designated areas where another mobile network is available and can support additional call traffic.
This way communities can stay connected and communicate as well as find information through an available network service during an emergency.
In the event of a natural disaster or other circumstances, people whose usual mobile network is down will still be able to make calls and send and receive text messages and access data via another available network.
TDR will be provided at no extra cost to customers.
“If your usual mobile network is impacted by a natural disaster, TDR will enable you to make calls, send texts, and use basic data via another mobile network where there’s one available,” says Australian Telecommunications Alliance CEO Luke Coleman. “There is no additional cost to use it, and for most customers, connection will occur automatically once TDR has been activated and is available.
“Australians have always been able to use any available mobile network to call Triple Zero – even when their usual network is impacted by an outage or out of coverage.
“TDR takes this even further. When it is activated and available, it is designed to allow customers to stay in touch with family and friends via voice calls and texts, and access basic data to use emergency service apps, WhatsApp, and iMessage.”
The activation of TDR will be managed between the mobile network operators themselves through their Network Operations Centre (NOC) which is operational 24/7.
If an operator recognises their network has been disrupted by a natural disaster, it can then contact one of the surviving networks to assess whether they still have coverage and capacity to support the affected area.
Each of the operators has conducted field testing to ensure the capability is prepared for the high-risk weather season.
TDR will also work hand in hand with the existing Camp-On setup for Triple Zero calling.
Camp-On allows users to still connect to emergency services using another mobile network when their usual network is unavailable.
But an important consideration of TDR is ensuring the still-active networks have enough coverage and capacity to handle the additional customers without putting their existing services, including Triple Zero, at risk.

articles.title: TGC 2026: Students pitch Maharashtra's innovation roadmap to CM Fadnavis
articles.text:
TGC 2026: Students pitch Maharashtra's innovation roadmap to CM Fadnavis
Six finalist teams from ISB, IIM Mumbai, IIT Bombay and more present deep tech solutions to CM Devendra Fadnavis at the Summit Round of The Governance Challenge 2026, India's first governance-focused competition.
What would it take for Maharashtra to become India's innovation hub by 2035? Six teams of business and public policy students are putting their answers directly to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis today.
The fourth edition of The Governance Challenge (TGC), billed as India's first governance-focused competition, reaches its Summit Round on 30 September at the Jamshed Bhabha Theatre, NCPA, Mumbai. The six finalists were whittled down from 4,429 teams over three months of competition.
A 2035 brief with a deep tech lens
This year's edition is hosted by the Government of Maharashtra and supported by the Gates Foundation. Its theme, Catalysing Innovation, came with a single question for participants: what can the state government do to make Maharashtra an innovation hub by 2035?
The brief builds on moves the state has already made. These include the Maharashtra Startup, Entrepreneurship and Innovation Policy 2025, the Rs 500 crore Chief Minister MahaFund, and the proposed Maharashtra Innovation City.
Teams were asked to push further, with a particular focus on deep tech. Solutions had to target one of six domains: agriculture, healthcare, education, governance, financial inclusion, and urban development.
TGC runs annually across 30 business and public policy institutions. Earlier editions partnered with the governments of Haryana, Odisha, and Uttar Pradesh.
Record turnout at the campus stage
The competition opened with a Campus Round in August 2026. It drew the largest participation in TGC's history: 4,429 teams and 13,287 students across the 30 institutions.
After evaluation, each institution picked one Campus Winner to move on to the Nationals Round.
Bureaucrats and domain experts on the jury
On 11 and 12 September, the 30 Campus Winners presented virtually to a jury pairing a senior state official with a domain expert for each of the six domains.
The jury shortlisted six teams for the Summit. The same 12 members then mentored the finalists they had selected, helping them sharpen their proposals before today's presentations.
Six finalists, one stage
The teams presenting today come from Indian School of Business, BITS School of Management, SJMSOM at IIT Bombay, Masters' Union, IIM Mumbai, and IIM Ranchi.
They pitch to CM Fadnavis, joined by Rajesh Aggarwal, Chief Secretary of Maharashtra, and Deepak Karanjikar, Member of the Governing Council of the Maharashtra Institute for Transformation.
The top three teams will share a prize pool of Rs 9 lakh. They also receive certificates and individual pre-placement interview opportunities with Samagra.
Why it matters
TGC gives students a rare line of sight into how policy is actually made, and gives the state a pipeline of fresh ideas vetted by the officials who would implement them. With the MahaFund and Innovation City already in motion, today's pitches land at a moment when Maharashtra is actively shaping its innovation agenda.
The competition is organised by Samagra, a governance consulting firm that works only with governments. It partners with senior political and bureaucratic leaders at the state and national levels on systemic reforms, using technology and data to improve delivery across education, agriculture, skilling, employment, health, and public services.

articles.title: KI-Agenten für KMU: So entlastet Agentic AI den Mittelstand
articles.text:
Warum KI-Agenten für KMU jetzt relevant werden
Der Mittelstand steht unter Druck: knappe Ressourcen, komplexere Lieferketten, mehr Dokumentationspflichten und steigende Erwartungen an Geschwindigkeit. Genau hier können KI-Agenten ansetzen. Sie übernehmen nicht einfach einzelne Textaufgaben, sondern können Informationen bündeln, Daten prüfen und Arbeitsschritte beschleunigen.
Eine aktuelle YouGov-Umfrage im Auftrag von Alibaba.com und dem Bundesverband E-Commerce und Versandhandel (bevh) zeigt: Rund ein Drittel der KMU sieht administrative Überlastung als konkretes Problem. Rund 40 Prozent nennen Auftragsabwicklung und Kundenservice als besonders zeitintensive Bereiche. Mehr als die Hälfte der KMU ab zehn Mitarbeitern sieht zudem das Potenzial, durch KI-Agenten mindestens zehn Prozent operativer Routineaufgaben einzusparen.
Vom Admin-Overload zu mehr Entscheidungsstärke
Der größte Hebel liegt dort, wo Unternehmen heute besonders viel Zeit verlieren: in fragmentierten Informationen, wiederkehrenden Prüfungen und manuellen Abstimmungen. KI-Agenten können Daten aus verschiedenen Quellen zusammenführen, Dokumente vorstrukturieren, Kriterien abgleichen und nächste Schritte vorbereiten oder ausführen.
Das entlastet Teams im Tagesgeschäft und schafft bessere Grundlagen für Entscheidungen. Besonders relevant ist das in Bereichen wie Auftragsabwicklung, Kundenservice, Compliance, Produktrecherche, Angebotsvorbereitung und internationaler Beschaffung.
Jüngere Entscheider treiben die Nutzung voran
Besonders dynamisch ist die Entwicklung bei jüngeren Führungskräften. In der Gruppe der unter 35-Jährigen nutzen mehr als 62 Prozent bereits Agentic AI. Gleichzeitig investiert in dieser Altersgruppe fast jeder Vierte gezielt in KI-Weiterbildung und ein Drittel sieht ohne KI-Agenten mittelfristig Risiken für die eigene Wettbewerbsfähigkeit. Auch beim Vertrauen in KI-gestützte Ergebnisse liegen jüngere Entscheider klar vorn, etwa bei der Prüfung von Produktinformationen, Lieferantenangaben oder der Vorbereitung von Geschäftsdokumenten. Die Entwicklung ist damit weniger ein Hinweis auf Zurückhaltung im Mittelstand als vielmehr ein positives Signal: Eine neue Generation von Entscheidern zeigt, wie schnell KI-Agenten vom Experiment zum produktiven Werkzeug werden können.
Accio: Agentische KI für den B2B-Alltag
Accio zeigt, wie dieser Wandel praktisch aussehen kann. Die Agentic AI-Plattform unterstützt Unternehmen dabei, Produktideen zu entwickeln, Markt- und Trenddaten zu analysieren, Lieferanteninformationen zu vergleichen, Spezifikationen und Zertifikate schneller einzuordnen und Geschäftsprozesse von Anfang bis Ende zu automatisieren.
Damit adressiert Accio zentrale Engpässe im B2B-Alltag: Recherche, Datenabgleich, Dokumentenprüfung, Angebotsvorbereitung und Beschaffungsentscheidungen. Unternehmen gewinnen Zeit, reduzieren Routineaufwand und können sich stärker auf Bewertung, Strategie und Wachstum konzentrieren.
Alibaba.com lädt Unternehmer aus Deutschland und ganz Europa ein, diese technologischen Möglichkeiten durch den CoCreate Pitch Europe in die Praxis umzusetzen. Der Startup-Wettbewerb unterstützt kleine Unternehmen dabei, den nächsten Schritt in der KI-Nutzung zu gehen. In diesem Jahr werden alle Bewerbungen über Accio eingereicht, von der Marktforschung über Produktideen bis hin zur Bewertung geschäftlicher Chancen. Die europäischen Finalrunden finden am 19. und 20. November in London statt. Weitere Informationen finden Sie auf der Event-Seite zum CoCreate Pitch.
Fazit: Die Chance liegt im Jetzt
Für den Mittelstand liegt die Chance nicht in einem radikalen Bruch, sondern in einem pragmatischen Produktivitätsschub. Wachstumsstarke KMU und jüngere Entscheider machen bereits vor, wie KI-Agenten operative Arbeit erleichtern können. Wer jetzt erste Anwendungsfelder identifiziert, kann Effizienzpotenziale heben, bevor aus Vorsprung Nachholbedarf wird.

articles.title: Non, ce n'est pas l'Etoile noire, mais incroyables aurores boréales (vidéo)
articles.text:
La vision est cauchemardesque et rappelle la plus meurtrière des armes de l’univers de Star Wars, l’Étoile noire.
Pourtant, il s’agit bien de la Terre vue par le satellite Smile. Lancée le 19 mai, la mission européano-chinoise a reçu le 23 septembre le feu vert pour démarrer ses observations scientifiques. Elle sort de trois mois de mise en service de ses instruments, depuis son arrivée sur son orbite définitive le 20 juin.
Ce que l’on voit dans cette vidéo dévoilée ce mercredi 30 septembre par l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA), c’est notre planète vue par la caméra UVI, un télescope ultraviolet qui capte la lumière entre 160 et 180 nanomètres de longueur d’onde. C’est pourquoi ni les nuages ni les continents ne sont présents puisque l’imageur ne capte pas le spectre de la lumière visible.
Les tempêtes solaires vues depuis l’espace
En revanche, on distingue bien cet anneau tourbillonnant qui fait ressembler notre planète à l’Étoile noire. Il s’agit d’aurores boréales visibles ce jour-là au niveau de l’Arctique. Les images ont été prises le 24 juillet, seulement deux semaines après la mise en route de l’imageur UVI.
Les aurores naissent quand des particules du vent solaire, guidées vers les pôles par le champ magnétique terrestre, percutent les molécules de la haute atmosphère, qui se mettent alors à briller. La vidéo montre une sous-tempête aurorale : une perturbation du champ magnétique causée par un afflux de particules du vent solaire.
On touche là le cœur de cible de la mission Smile, puisque son but est justement de comprendre comment fonctionnent les tempêtes solaires, et comment elles influent sur la magnétosphère terrestre.
En plus des aurores, ces tempêtes peuvent perturber, voire endommager, les satellites en orbite et des infrastructures au sol comme les réseaux électriques et les communications radio, malgré la protection qu’offre le champ magnétique.
L’ESA précise qu’UVI peut désormais filmer les aurores pendant 45 heures d’affilée, un record, là où les engins précédents ne dépassaient pas une quinzaine d’heures d’observation continue. Or une tempête géomagnétique dure en général deux à trois jours.
Encore trop de lumière parasite
Un autre instrument de Smile a, lui aussi, pris ses premières images. SXI, principale contribution européenne à la mission, est un télescope à rayons X « mous », c’est-à-dire peu énergétiques. Il doit observer pour la première fois en rayons X la frontière du champ magnétique terrestre, en captant la lueur émise quand les particules du vent solaire heurtent la haute atmosphère. Ses premières images de test montrent les restes d’étoiles qui ont explosé en supernova : l’un dans le Grand Nuage de Magellan, une galaxie voisine de la nôtre, l’autre, Cassiopée A, dans la Voie lactée. Pointé vers la Terre, l’instrument n’a en revanche pas encore livré d’image exploitable.
L’ESA explique que la caméra fonctionne bien, mais qu’elle capte pour l’instant trop de lumière parasite lorsqu’elle est tournée vers la Terre. Les équipes européennes et chinoises modifient actuellement des réglages et installent des mises à jour logicielles à bord pour réduire cette lumière parasite.
La gêne diminue aussi d’elle-même, à mesure que Smile pointe plus loin de la Terre et que le pôle Nord, à l’approche de l’hiver, émet moins de lumière. Elle devrait atteindre son minimum à la mi-octobre. SXI pourrait alors prendre sa première image exploitable de la magnétopause, la frontière où le vent solaire rencontre le champ magnétique terrestre, ou du cornet polaire nord, une brèche du champ magnétique au-dessus du pôle.

articles.title: Russian state hackers use new RedFlick technique to push malware
articles.text:
The Russian state actor Star Blizzard has been using a new malware installation tactic dubbed “RedFlick” to deploy its signature CosmicPulse backdoor.
Although the tactic is not a new cybersecurity technique, it is a new delivery approach for the threat actor, allowing it to further automate attacks and reduce victim interaction.
Microsoft researchers say that Star Blizzard expanded its phishing operations and streamlined malware delivery in 2026.
Star Blizzard, active since 2017, is known for exploring new payload delivery avenues like ClickFix or WhatsApp, and for continually developing and deploying new malware families.
New RedFlick technique
RedFlick attacks begin with a phishing email, such as an invitation, followed by a second message containing a password-protected ZIP or RAR archive.
The archive contains a VHDX virtual disk with an LNK file disguised as a PDF. When the file is opened, it launches a command in a hidden window while displaying a decoy PDF to the victim.
The commands download and run an MSI installer that creates three scheduled tasks posing as legitimate maintenance components, each with a specific purpose:
- Internet Quality Test Connection: sends the computer/network name and username to the attackers and can execute a remote DLL.
- Network Configuration Manager: prepares Windows’ WebDAV functionality so remote web resources can be accessed through file-style paths.
- System Health Monitor: uses control.exe to execute a remotely hosted next-stage payload.
Since the new method uses multiple scheduled tasks with distinct roles, it helps the attacker evade detection at different stages of the attack.
The next-stage payload is a downloader known as NOROBOT and BAITSWITCH, delivered in the form of a Control Panel applet (.cpl). Its purpose is to fetch and execute the CosmicPulse backdoor.
BAITSWITCH downloads two ZIP archives, one of them containing the Python 3.8 64-bit package and a Python file acting as a bootstrapper for CosmicPulse.
"The bootstrapper reads the encrypted key from the registry, recovers it using an embedded key in AES-ECB mode, and then uses the recovered key to decode the CosmicPulse payload," Microsoft says.
Microsoft notes that the backdoor’s capabilities in the observed attacks remain the same as described in a report from Google in October 2025, including the execution of attacker-supplied Python code to download and run files or retrieve documents from infected systems.
From a practical perspective, RedFlick only requires the victim to open the malicious shortcut file to trigger an automated infection chain, whereas in the ClickFix attacks, Star Blizzard required victims to take multiple manual actions.
Microsoft's report provides technical analysis of the infection chain and the components used in the attacks.
The company says that since the beginning of the year, it has observed at least 13 distinct large-scale phishing campaigns impacting more than 100 organizations, primarily in the United States and the United Kingdom.
“The RedFlick campaigns have targeted Ukrainian individuals and institutions, as well as international NGOs, think tanks, governments, and financial institutions that have supported Ukraine politically or financially,” the researchers say.
Despite changing its tactics, techniques, and procedures, StarBlizzard continues to target users by impersonating trusted contacts or organizations, and still relies on free email providers to deliver phishing messages.
Microsoft recommends that companies use phishing-resistant authentication, Conditional Access policies, email protection, and independently verify suspicious messages through established contact details.
Additionally, using an endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions in block mode should prevent infections by blocking malicious artifacts even if they are not caught by the antivirus agent.

articles.title: Cómo cuidar los alimentos que están en el refrigerador cuando hay un apagón de energía
articles.text:
Un corte de luz prolongado pone en riesgo algo más que la comodidad del hogar: compromete la seguridad de los alimentos guardados en el refrigerador. La decisión de qué conservar y qué desechar no depende del aspecto ni del olor, sino del tiempo y la temperatura que esos productos soportaron durante el apagón.
Mantener la calma y actuar con método permite salvar buena parte de la comida. La clave está en anotar la hora del corte, evitar aperturas innecesarias y revisar cada alimento por separado cuando regresa la electricidad.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué hacer mientras no hay electricidad
La recomendación más repetida por los organismos de seguridad alimentaria es simple: mantener cerradas las puertas del refrigerador y el congelador. Cada apertura deja entrar aire caliente y acorta el margen de tiempo en el que la comida permanece fría.
Según la guía de seguridad alimentaria del Gobierno de Estados Unidos, un refrigerador sin abrir conserva el frío durante unas cuatro horas. Un congelador lleno puede aguantar unas 48 horas; si está medio lleno, el margen baja a 24 horas.
Contar con hieleras herméticas, paquetes de gel o bloques de hielo antes de que ocurra un corte ayuda a extender ese tiempo. Trasladar los alimentos perecederos a una nevera portátil con hielo es preferible a abrir el frigorífico de forma repetida para comprobarlos.
PUBLICIDAD
Si el agua de una tormenta se acumula cerca de enchufes o cables, lo primero es atender la seguridad eléctrica y no tocar los electrodomésticos hasta confirmar que no hay riesgo.
Cómo decidir qué alimentos conservar al volver la luz
Cuando regresa la electricidad, la revisión debe hacerse producto por producto. Un documento de la Agencia Española de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutrición señala que, con la puerta cerrada, un corte de menos de cuatro horas no obliga en principio a desechar nada del refrigerador.
Si el corte se prolongó por más tiempo, es probable que se hayan superado los 5 °C. En ese caso, la recomendación es tirar carne, pescado, pollo, huevos, leche, queso fresco y las sobras, junto con frutas y verduras cortadas o ensaladas preparadas.
PUBLICIDAD
El aspecto y el olor no son indicadores confiables. La misma agencia advierte que algunos microorganismos peligrosos pueden estar presentes sin producir ningún cambio perceptible. Tampoco conviene probar la comida “para ver si está bien”.
Un termómetro dentro del refrigerador facilita esta decisión. Si se desconoce cuánto tiempo estuvo un alimento perecedero a una temperatura insegura, lo prudente es descartarlo directamente. La zona de peligro para estos productos se ubica entre los 4,4 °C y los 65 °C, el rango en el que las bacterias se multiplican con mayor rapidez.
Qué hacer con el congelador de la nevera
El congelador tolera cortes más largos que el refrigerador, pero también necesita una inspección específica al recuperar la corriente. Los paquetes que todavía conservan cristales de hielo o se mantienen a 4 °C o menos pueden cocinarse o volver a congelarse sin problema.
PUBLICIDAD
Si los alimentos se descongelaron por completo y no hay certeza de cuánto tiempo permanecieron templados, la recomendación es descartarlos sin excepción, para evitar la propagación bacteriana.
Para los alimentos no congelados, una alternativa antes de seguir almacenándolos es cocinarlos de inmediato. Eso elimina posibles bacterias y permite empaquetarlos después para prolongar su vida dentro de una hielera hermética.
Alimentos que resisten sin refrigeración
No todos los productos dependen del frío para mantenerse seguros. Entre las frutas y verduras enteras, las manzanas duran entre 5 y 7 días a temperatura ambiente, los cítricos entre 5 y 10 días, y las patatas y cebollas pueden mantenerse semanas en un ambiente seco y ventilado.
PUBLICIDAD
Los quesos duros también ofrecen margen: el parmesano puede durar varios días sin cambios importantes, mientras que el manchego curado, el gruyère y el comté aguantan entre 1 y 2 días envueltos en papel o un paño seco.
En panadería, el pan común se conserva entre 2 y 3 días a temperatura ambiente, las galletas secas se mantienen intactas durante una semana o más, y los bizcochos simples resisten entre 2 y 4 días. Refrescos, conservas cerradas y chocolate tampoco requieren frío para seguir siendo seguros.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Plus de 19 000 films : la justice française s'en prend à l'hébergeur OVH pour bloquer deux sites pirates
articles.text:
Le tribunal judiciaire de Paris a ordonné à OVH, dans un jugement du 17 septembre 2026, d’empêcher l’accès depuis la France à deux sites pirates de films et de séries hébergés sur son infrastructure. La mesure, réclamée par Columbia Pictures, Disney, Netflix, Universal et deux autres sociétés américaines, doit être en place au plus tard 15 jours après la signification du jugement. Elle durera 18 mois, aux frais de l’hébergeur.
C’est l’hébergeur qui est visé ici, et non les fournisseurs d’accès à internet (Orange, SFR, Free, Bouygues Telecom), cibles habituelles de ce type de demande. L’information a d’abord été relayée par Univers Freebox. Le texte du jugement permet d’en préciser la portée.
Un blocage fondé sur l’article L. 336-2
Les studios ont assigné OVH le 4 juin 2026 selon la procédure accélérée au fond, sur la base de l’article L. 336-2 du code de la propriété intellectuelle. Ce texte permet au juge d’ordonner des mesures à l’encontre de « toute personne susceptible de contribuer à y remédier ». Avec l’accord des parties, l’affaire a été jugée sans audience.
Les deux sites concernés s’appellent « tekfullfilmizle » et « fullhdfilmizlesene ». Des agents assermentés de l’ALPA ont constaté qu’ils s’adressent à un public francophone. Le premier donnait accès sans autorisation à 2 611 films et 175 séries, le second à 19 738 films. Sur un échantillon de 15 liens vérifiés à la main pour chaque site, 14 renvoyaient vers des œuvres contrefaisantes, soit un taux annoncé de 93,33 % pour chacun, avec une marge d’erreur annoncée d’environ 3,4 %.
Le tribunal relève aussi que ces sites n’affichent aucune des mentions légales exigées par la loi pour la confiance dans l’économie numérique et qu’ils sont intégralement anonymisés via plusieurs prestataires. Pour les juges, cela tend à montrer que leurs exploitants connaissent le caractère illicite des liens, et cela rend difficile de les poursuivre directement.
Ce que doit faire OVH, et ce qu’il n’a pas à faire
OVH doit empêcher l’accès depuis le territoire français, outre-mer compris, aux noms de domaine et sous-domaines listés dans une annexe du jugement. Le moyen est laissé à son choix. OVH doit informer les studios dès que le blocage est en place, et ces derniers doivent lui signaler les domaines qui disparaissent, pour éviter des coûts inutiles.
Si les sites changent de nom de domaine ou de chemin d’accès, les studios pourront revenir devant le tribunal, en procédure accélérée au fond ou en référé, pour faire actualiser la mesure. Le jugement est exécutoire malgré un éventuel appel.
Les demandeurs voulaient davantage : un délai de cinq jours, la possibilité de suspendre les services d’hébergement des exploitants, un rappel du rôle de l’Arcom pour les sites miroirs et 15 000 euros de frais de justice. Le tribunal a retenu 15 jours et le blocage des noms de domaine. Il n’a pas repris la mention de l’Arcom dans son dispositif, et il a rejeté les demandes financières des deux côtés, OVH réclamant de son côté 5 000 euros. Chaque partie garde ses dépens.
Ce que disait OVH
OVH contestait le caractère contrefaisant des deux sites, jugeait les mesures disproportionnées et s’opposait à un blocage étendu à toute autre adresse IP. Le tribunal a estimé les constats de l’ALPA suffisamment probants. Il rappelle qu’il doit ménager un équilibre entre le droit d’auteur, la liberté d’entreprise des intermédiaires et la liberté d’information, en citant deux arrêts de la Cour de justice de l’Union européenne, et il écarte tout contrôle général et sans limite de durée.
Une question reste ouverte
Le jugement demande à OVH d’empêcher l’accès aux deux sites depuis la France « par tout moyen efficace », en citant notamment le blocage des noms de domaine. Les studios réclamaient aussi la possibilité de suspendre les services d’hébergement des exploitants, une option que le dispositif ne reprend pas expressément. Il vise par ailleurs des « abonnés » d’un contrat souscrit en France, une notion qui pourrait renvoyer plus naturellement aux fournisseurs d’accès qu’à un hébergeur. Comment OVH, qui héberge les serveurs, mettra concrètement le blocage en œuvre n’est pas précisé par la décision.

articles.title: El Instituto Geográfico Nacional acaba de actualizar todos sus mapas de España a alta resolución y se pueden descargar gratis desde su web
articles.text:
Hubo un tiempo en que un mapa de España se desplegaba sobre el capó, se plegaba mal y terminaba en la guantera, oliendo a bocadillo de tortilla y marcas a boli. Ese mundo no se fue del todo. Sigue vivo en las imprentas del Instituto Geográfico Nacional (IGN), que acaba de renovar tres de sus láminas más clásicas, de entre todos sus mapas topográficos y cartográficos nacionales y autonómicos. Y puedes descargarlas gratis y en un par de minutos.
Tres láminas nuevas. El Centro Nacional de Información Geográfica (CNIG), el organismo del IGN que reparte su cartografía, las anotó en sus novedades en dos tandas. El 15 de septiembre llegó la edición 2026 del mapa físico de España, a escala 1:1.800.000. El 21, el mapa físico de Europa (1:8.235.000) y el político del mundo (1:49.410.000).
En el mapa de España, un centímetro de papel equivale a 18 kilómetros de tierra. En el de Europa, a 82. En el del mundo, a casi 494. Es un pequeño prodigio de la escala. El de España pesa unos 33 megas en JPG y es la versión digitalizada de la edición impresa. El catálogo de mapas físicos y políticos de España se publica con licencia CC BY 4.0. Es decir, puedes usarlo, imprimirlo o remezclarlo, siempre que cites al IGN.
Cómo conseguirlos, paso a paso
- Entra en el Centro de Descargas. La puerta es centrodedescargas.cnig.es. Allí se descarga gratis la información geográfica digital que produce el IGN.
- Abre el catálogo. Pulsa en «Catálogo de productos» y entra en Mapas de España y del mundo. Esa sección reúne la cartografía de España, Europa y el planeta.
- Elige el mapa. Para el de España, abre "Mapas físicos y políticos" y busca el "Mapa físico de España 1:1.800.000 (edición impresa)", fechado en 2026. Para Europa y el mundo, el atajo más seguro es la página de Novedades, que los lista.
- Pulsa en "Descarga". Cada archivo ofrece dos botones: "Descarga", para bajarlo ya, y "Añadir a la cesta", útil si te llevas varios a la vez.
Eso sí, solo la versión digital es gratis. La de papel se vende en la Tienda Virtual del CNIG, aunque siempre puedes imprimir el archivo en casa o en una copistería.
¿Referencia geodésica? Por si no lo sabías, esta es la forma de decir dónde está cada cosa. España habló durante décadas el ED50, un sistema regional cuyo nombre ya delata su edad. Desde el Real Decreto 1071/2007 habla ETRS89, anclado a la parte estable de la placa europea y compatible con GPS, GLONASS y Galileo. En Canarias manda REGCAN95, plenamente compatible con el anterior. La ficha del IGN añade que ETRS89 es compatible con WGS84, el idioma del GPS del móvil.
El archivo. El catálogo de mapas físicos y políticos de España guarda 71 ficheros, desde un mapa del Estrecho de Gibraltar de 1988 hasta la edición de 2026. La ficha habla de coordenadas geográficas (longitud y latitud) y de proyecciones diversas. La más habitual es la cónica conforme de Lambert, que respeta los ángulos aunque deforme las distancias. Si buscas por coordenadas UTM, se ven los cuatro husos que cubren el país, del 28 al 31.
Y ojo con el formato: según la ficha, solo los GeoTIFF y GeoPDF llevan georreferenciación. Los JPG y PDF, no. El mapa de 2026 es un JPG de 32,74 MB: sirve para mirarlo y imprimirlo, no para cargarlo sobre un SIG. Y no olvidemos la condición: la licencia compatible con CC BY 4.0 obliga a citar origen y propiedad, con la fórmula “Mapas físicos y políticos de España - 1993-2026”.
Un mapa a tu medida. El IGN también cuenta con Mapa a la Carta que se resume en lo siguiente: eliges la zona y la escala (1:25.000 o 1:50.000), pones título, dibujas tu ruta y en saegundos sale un PDF gratuito. A 1:25.000, un centímetro son 250 metros. Imprimirlo en papel ya cuesta lo suyo, porque mide 52 por 76,5 centímetros.
Sin embargo, si no quieres hacer gasto de papel, no está de más recordar que existe una app gratuita, Mapas de España Básicos, disponible también en iOS, la cual lleva la cartografía del IGN al móvil. Funciona con GPS y sin conexión, siempre que descargues los mapas antes de salir.

articles.title: MIT’s tiny flying robot gets 450% faster with AI
articles.text:
MIT’s tiny flying robot gets 450% faster with AI
MIT’s tiny AI-powered flying robot can now move almost like an insect, performing rapid turns and 10 flips in just 11 seconds.
- Date:
- September 22, 2026
- Source:
- Massachusetts Institute of Technology
- Summary:
- A new AI control system lets MIT’s tiny flying robot move with insect-like agility, boosting its speed by about 450 percent and allowing it to pull off 10 somersaults in 11 seconds. The technology could eventually enable miniature robots to search earthquake rubble and navigate dangerous spaces that conventional drones cannot reach.
- Share:
Tiny flying robots may one day help rescuers search for people trapped beneath collapsed buildings after earthquakes. Because of their small size, these robotic insects could potentially move through narrow spaces that larger drones cannot enter while avoiding walls, debris, and falling objects.
Until recently, however, aerial microrobots have been far less nimble than the insects that inspired them. They typically moved slowly and followed relatively simple flight paths.
Researchers at MIT have now demonstrated a new approach that gives an insect-scale flying robot much greater speed and agility. The team developed an AI-based controller that allows the robotic bug to perform demanding aerial maneuvers, including repeated body flips.
Using a two-part control system designed to balance performance with computational efficiency, the researchers increased the robot's speed by about 450 percent and its acceleration by about 250 percent compared with their previous best results.
The robot was agile enough to complete 10 consecutive somersaults in 11 seconds, even while wind disturbances tried to knock it away from its intended path.
"We want to be able to use these robots in scenarios that more traditional quadcopter robots would have trouble flying into, but that insects could navigate. Now, with our bioinspired control framework, the flight performance of our robot is comparable to insects in terms of speed, acceleration, and the pitching angle. This is quite an exciting step toward that future goal," says Kevin Chen, an associate professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS), head of the Soft and Micro Robotics Laboratory within the Research Laboratory of Electronics (RLE), and co-senior author of a paper on the robot.
Chen is joined on the paper by co-lead authors Yi-Hsuan Hsiao, an EECS MIT graduate student; Andrea Tagliabue PhD '24; and Owen Matteson, a graduate student in the Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AeroAstro); as well as EECS graduate student Suhan Kim; Tong Zhao MEng '23; and co-senior author Jonathan P. How, the Ford Professor of Engineering in the Department of Aeronautics and Astronautics and a principal investigator in the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (LIDS). The research was published in Science Advances.
AI Gives the Robot a Smarter Flight Controller
Chen's group has spent more than five years developing robotic insects.
The team recently created a more durable version of their tiny robot, which is about the size of a microcassette and weighs less than a paperclip. This newer design has larger flapping wings that support more agile flight. The wings are driven by soft artificial muscles that contract rapidly enough to produce extremely fast wingbeats.
The physical design had improved, but the robot's controller remained a major limitation. This controller acts as the robot's "brain," determining where the robot is and deciding how it should move. In earlier versions, a human had to tune the controller by hand.
For the robot to fly with the speed and aggressiveness of a real insect, the researchers needed a system that could handle uncertainty while rapidly solving complex control problems.
A controller powerful enough to do that would normally demand too much computation to operate in real time, especially because the aerodynamics of such a lightweight flying machine are highly complex.
To solve this problem, Chen's group collaborated with How's team to develop a two-step AI-driven control system. The design combines the robustness needed for difficult, high-speed maneuvers with enough computational efficiency to work in real time.
"The hardware advances pushed the controller so there was more we could do on the software side, but at the same time, as the controller developed, there was more they could do with the hardware. As Kevin's team demonstrates new capabilities, we demonstrate that we can utilize them," How says.
Teaching a Tiny Robot to Plan Difficult Maneuvers
The first part of the system uses what is known as a model-predictive controller. This type of controller relies on a dynamic mathematical model to predict how the robot will behave and determine the best sequence of actions for safely following a desired flight path.
Although this method requires substantial computing power, it can plan difficult movements such as aerial flips, sharp turns, and aggressive changes in body angle. The planner also takes into account limits on the amount of force and torque the robot can produce, helping it avoid movements that could lead to a crash.
Repeated flips are particularly challenging. To perform one somersault after another, the robot must slow down in exactly the right way so that it begins each new flip under the proper conditions.
"If small errors creep in, and you try to repeat that flip 10 times with those small errors, the robot will just crash. We need to have robust flight control," How says.
The researchers then used this expert planner to train a "policy" built on a deep-learning model through a process called imitation learning. The policy serves as the robot's real-time decision-making system, determining how and where it should fly.
In effect, imitation learning allows the team to capture the behavior of the more computationally demanding controller in a faster AI model that can operate quickly enough for real-time flight.
A major part of the challenge was generating enough useful training data to teach the policy how to handle aggressive maneuvers without creating an unnecessarily large data set.
"The robust training method is the secret sauce of this technique," How explains.
During flight, the AI-based policy receives information about the robot's position and converts it into real-time commands controlling factors such as thrust force and torques.
Insect-Like Speed and Agility
Experiments showed that the two-step control system dramatically improved the robot's performance. The insect-scale machine flew 447 percent faster and achieved a 255 percent increase in acceleration.
It also completed 10 somersaults in only 11 seconds while remaining within about 4 or 5 centimeters of its planned flight path.
"This work demonstrates that soft and microrobots, traditionally limited in speed, can now leverage advanced control algorithms to achieve agility approaching that of natural insects and larger robots, opening up new opportunities for multimodal locomotion," says Hsiao.
The team also demonstrated a movement known as a saccade. In insects, this involves pitching the body sharply, rapidly moving to a new position, and then pitching in the opposite direction to stop. This quick acceleration and braking can help insects determine their position and maintain clear vision.
"This bio-mimicking flight behavior could help us in the future when we start putting cameras and sensors on board the robot," Chen says.
Toward Autonomous Flying Microrobots
One major goal for future research is to equip the microrobots with onboard cameras and sensors. That could eventually allow them to fly outdoors without depending on a sophisticated external motion capture system.
The team also plans to investigate whether onboard sensing could help groups of the robots avoid crashing into one another and coordinate their movements while navigating.
"For the micro-robotics community, I hope this paper signals a paradigm shift by showing that we can develop a new control architecture that is high-performing and efficient at the same time," says Chen.
This research is funded, in part, by the National Science Foundation (NSF), the Office of Naval Research, Air Force Office of Scientific Research, MathWorks, and the Zakhartchenko Fellowship.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Yi-Hsuan Hsiao, Andrea Tagliabue, Owen Matteson, Suhan Kim, Tong Zhao, Jonathan P. How, YuFeng Chen. Aerobatic maneuvers in insect-scale flapping-wing aerial robots via deep-learned robust tube model predictive control. Science Advances, 2025; 11 (49) DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.aea8716

articles.title: Google lance Gemini 4 Argon, une IA qui bat GPT-6 Astra sur le papier mais que presque personne ne peut utiliser
articles.text:
Google a dévoilé Gemini 4 Argon, son nouveau modèle d'IA de pointe, qui surpasse GPT-6 Astra et Claude Opus 5.5 sur plusieurs tests, selon ses propres mesures. Proposé à bas prix, il reste pour l'instant réservé aux experts en cybersécurité.
Avec Gemini 4 Argon, présenté mercredi soir, on peut dire que Google répond à la salve de nouveaux modèles d'IA tirée par OpenAI et Anthropic ces derniers jours. D'après ses propres mesures, le géant de Mountain View décroche la première place sur une bonne partie des tests de référence, du développement logiciel au droit en passant par la finance, pour le prix d'un modèle intermédiaire. Mais ce podium, Google l'a dressé lui-même, sans y convier deux rivaux vendus au même tarif, et il faudra en plus patienter avant de le vérifier.
Google entraîne Gemini 4 Argon à traquer les failles
Google cachait-il son jeu, ou a-t-il sorti du bois Gemini 4 Argon pour ne pas perdre la face ? Quoi qu'il en soit, dans le tableau publié par la firme au moteur de recherche, Argon fait plus que regarder GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 et Claude Opus 5.5 dans les yeux, puisqu'il termine en tête sur plus de la moitié des épreuves.
En programmation au long cours, il atteint 77,9 % sur DeepSWE, contre 74,1 % pour Astra et 74,2 % pour Opus 5.5. Il domine aussi le Vals Index, qui chiffre l'impact économique d'une IA en finance, fiscalité, droit et code, chaque secteur pesant selon sa part du PIB américain. En droit, l'écart devient vertigineux, avec un 19,6 % sur le test juridique conçu par Harvey, quand ses rivaux oscillent entre 3,8 et 6,7 %.
Google nous apprend qu'Argon peut générer jusqu'à un million de tokens d'un seul tenant, contre 64 000 auparavant. Un token correspondant grosso modo à un morceau de mot, et cela représente des centaines de milliers de mots de raisonnement ou de code. Sonnet 5.5 et GPT-6.1 Sol, eux, s'arrêtent à 128 000 en usage standard. Chez Google, des agents Argon ont même déniché et appliqué des optimisations qui libèrent plus de 300 tébioctets de mémoire une fois déployées. D'autres s'attaquent à la conversion de code C/C++ vers Rust, un langage qui protège mieux la mémoire, jusqu'aux plus de 800 000 lignes du noyau Zircon de Fuchsia.
Argon a aussi été entraîné pour la défense informatique. Il est capable de trouver, vérifier et corriger seul des failles critiques. Les défenseurs de confiance et les équipes de Google pourront même l'utiliser sans garde-fous en cybersécurité. Chez Wiz, la plateforme de sécurité cloud qui appartient désormais au mastodonte américaine, il a mis au jour une faille pourtant passée sous le radar des modèles précédents, qui exposait des données personnelles sensibles dans des logiciels hospitaliers utilisés partout dans le monde. En parallèle, Google surveille le raisonnement et les actions du modèle pour le stopper s'il dépasse les intentions de l'utilisateur. Face aux consignes malveillantes cachées dans un contenu pour détourner l'IA, les fameuses injections de prompt, le taux de réussite des attaques plafonne à 0,7 %, même sur quinze tentatives.
Un Gemini à prix plancher, mais pas seul au sommet
Comme ses concurrents, Google essaie de marquer le coup sur les prix. Pour les développeurs et les entreprises, Argon sera facturé au volume de texte traité, à 2 dollars par million de tokens envoyés au modèle (la question posée, les documents joints) et 10 dollars par million de tokens qu'il rédige en réponse. Quand un même contenu revient d'une requête à l'autre, comme un long document déjà analysé, Google le garde en mémoire et le facture 95 % moins cher. Ces tarifs sont deux fois plus bas que ceux de Claude Opus 5.5, lancé le 22 septembre, et cinq fois plus bas que ceux de GPT-6 Astra ou Claude Fable 5.1. Il s'agit toutefois d'un prix « d'introduction », prévient Google, qui pourrait donc évoluer à la hausse, on imagine.
À ce tarif, Argon croise pourtant deux rivaux aux mêmes prix d'entrée et de sortie, absents de son comparatif : Claude Sonnet 5.5, sorti lundi, et GPT-6.1 Sol, dévoilé le lendemain. D'après ses propres mesures, Anthropic annonce 70,6 % pour Sonnet 5.5 sur Terminal-Bench 4.0, qui évalue l'autonomie d'une IA dans la ligne de commande. Dans le tableau de Google, Argon n'y obtient que 57,4 %, le plus faible score des quatre modèles comparés. Astra le devance aussi sur OSWorld, qui teste le pilotage d'un ordinateur. En cybersécurité, Google revendique pour Argon une première place partagée sur CWE-bench, à 68 %, avec Astra et Grok 4.7.
Pour le moment, rares sont ceux qui peuvent l'essayer. Comme OpenAI avec Astra ou Anthropic avec Mythos, Google commence par un cercle restreint. À cette heure, l'entreprise a réuni des spécialistes en cybersécurité dans son tout nouveau programme dédié Fairwind. L'entreprise participe aussi au dispositif volontaire qui permet au gouvernement américain d'accéder aux modèles avant leur sortie, histoire d'éviter toute mauvaise surprise. Les clients payants de l'API et les abonnés Google AI Ultra suivront « dès que possible », écrit l'entreprise. Pendant ce temps, Sonnet 5.5 est déjà dans les applications Claude, et GPT-6.1 Sol chez les abonnés payants de ChatGPT, dans Work et Codex. D'ici là, ces scores restent ceux de Google, qui a d'ailleurs détaillé sa méthodologie d'évaluation pour Argon, en attendant le verdict des tests indépendants.

articles.title: Nouveau Fire TV Stick 4K : avant d'acheter, vérifiez bien ce détail qui fâche
articles.text:
Nouveau Fire TV Stick 4K : avant d'acheter, vérifiez bien ce détail qui fâche
Plus fine, plus rapide, escortée d'une télécommande enfin dessinée pour la main, la nouvelle clé HDMI d'Amazon débarque en France à 74,99 euros. Elle tourne aussi le dos à Android, et ce virage risque de faire grincer des dents chez tous ceux qui installaient leurs propres applications.
Amazon a dévoilé ce mercredi 30 septembre la nouvelle génération de son Fire TV Stick 4K, disponible dès aujourd'hui en France, en Europe, en Amérique du Nord, au Japon et en Océanie.
Le calendrier doit peu au hasard : la clé débarque quelques jours avant la grande braderie d'octobre réservée aux abonnés Prime. Sur le papier, la promesse tient en un mot : la vitesse. Le géant de Seattle affirme que son stick atteint les contenus 20 à 40 % plus vite qu'une clé 4K concurrente de prix équivalent, avec des applications lancées plus de 35 % plus rapidement. Le rival n'est jamais nommé et la méthodologie reste confidentielle, ce qui invite à attendre les premiers tests avant de s'emballer.
Sous le capot, rien de spectaculaire : processeur quadricœur à 1,7 GHz, 8 Go de stockage, Wi-Fi 6 et Bluetooth 5.3. La clé décode l'AV1, gère le HDR10, le HDR10+ et le HLG jusqu'en 2160p à 60 images par seconde. Le Dolby Vision reste l'apanage du Fire TV Stick 4K Max. Le boîtier s'affine et gagne un port USB-C, avec une alimentation directe par le port USB du téléviseur grâce au câble fourni. Adieu le bloc secteur qui encombrait la multiprise.
Vega OS : la fin du sideloading sur le Fire TV Stick 4K
Voilà le vrai sujet. Comme le Fire TV Stick HD sorti au printemps, ce modèle délaisse Fire OS, dérivé d'Android, pour Vega OS, le système maison bâti sur Linux. Conséquence directe : impossible d'y installer une application Android glanée hors de la boutique officielle. Les bidouilleurs devront se replier sur le 4K Max, désormais la seule clé de la gamme restée sous Fire OS.
Télécommande repensée, prix et gamme simplifiée
La télécommande, livrée d'office, adopte une silhouette asymétrique : plate sur le dessus, arrondie et lestée en dessous, avec des touches creusées ou modelées pour être reconnues au toucher sans quitter l'écran des yeux. Un bouton étoile personnalisable complète l'ensemble. Elle sera vendue seule 15,99 euros, avec des expéditions prévues fin octobre.
Côté tarif, la clé affiche 74,99 euros, mais Amazon la brade déjà à 35,99 euros pour son lancement. Le catalogue se resserre enfin sur trois échelons, HD, 4K et 4K Max, le Select et le Plus s'effaçant au fil de l'écoulement des stocks.

articles.title: Fintech Kora brings stablecoins to its pan-African payment network
articles.text:
Kora, a Nigerian-founded fintech that provides payment rails for businesses across African markets, has launched One Rail, a product that integrates stablecoin payment and settlement options into its existing network.
The new product allows eligible merchants in supported markets to accept payments in dollar-backed stablecoins USDT and USDC, convert between supported assets, and settle funds to bank accounts, mobile wallets, or stablecoin wallets through Kora’s existing infrastructure. Kora said it is expanding access in stages, with supported functions varying by market and the payment rails enabled for each merchant.
The move comes as African fintech infrastructure providers, including Onafriq and Fincra, are increasingly turning to stablecoin-based options for cross-border payments. For payment companies, stablecoins offer a potential alternative to move dollar-denominated value between markets.
If firms can convert those balances into local currencies when needed, they may reduce the amount of working capital tied up in prefunded accounts. The savings would depend on the availability and cost of local liquidity, foreign exchange (FX) conversion, and payout services.
One Rail brings that settlement layer into Kora’s existing payment infrastructure, allowing merchants to receive and send stablecoins without managing the underlying blockchain infrastructure themselves. The fintech said it wants stablecoin payments to work like any other payment method, without requiring businesses to manage wallets, blockchain infrastructure, or use separate reconciliation systems.
“If you go into your bank in Nigeria to do a wire to, say, China, it’s going to take you at least three days—the money goes from Nigeria to New York, from New York to Hong Kong, then from Hong Kong to mainland China,” Dickson Nsofor, Kora’s founder and chief executive officer, told TechCabal in an interview. “If you do the same transaction with a stablecoin, it’s less than two minutes end to end, at a fraction of the cost.”
A stablecoin can move between compatible blockchain wallets within minutes. Yet, the time and cost of a full cross-border payment depend on factors including fiat conversion, FX transactions, compliance checks, and the destination market’s payout infrastructure.
Stablecoin adoption and its potential to reduce frictions in cross-border payments are driving interest in the technology. Nigeria has accounted for roughly 60% of stablecoin inflows into Sub-Saharan Africa since 2019, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
US dollar-backed stablecoins also play an important role in this market. About 99% of the stablecoin market value is denominated in US dollars as the underlying currency, helping to increase digital dollar accessibility for emerging markets facing shortages.
Cross-border payment companies often maintain local-currency balances across multiple markets to meet payout needs, tying up capital until those funds are used. In 2022, the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), the Basel-based global bank that serves central banks, identified funding costs and liquidity management as key challenges in cross-border multicurrency payments.
Now, the global bank is testing whether tokenised central bank reserves and commercial bank deposits—digital versions of money banks hold—could improve multicurrency settlement, underscoring a broader interest in using digital representations of financial assets to move money across borders.
“Prefunding is still [a] fundamental way companies do business today,” Nsofor said. “That does not negate the fact that stablecoins will, in the future, be the best way to avoid prefunding altogether; you just hold a stablecoin, and based on the payment need, you convert. That’s where the whole world is tending.”
However, stablecoins do not remove the need for local currency liquidity. A payment company still needs access to Tanzanian shillings, Kenyan shillings, or other local currencies when a recipient needs to be paid. That liquidity can come from the company’s own balance, an FX provider, a bank, or a local payout partner.
Kora said it currently prefunds markets where local liquidity is limited, citing Tanzania, where Kora launched in April, as an example. Stablecoins could eventually let the company hold liquidity in digital currencies and convert it into local currency when a payment is needed, reducing the capital tied up across individual markets, according to Nsofor.
Other fintechs seem to be experimenting with that thesis. In May, Tanzanian-founded remittance fintech NALA secured up to $50 million in debt funding from private credit firm Liquidity to prefund transfers, expand payment corridors, and support larger enterprise clients. NALA is building stablecoin payment infrastructure to support faster settlement and reduce FX costs, the fintech said in April.
Much ado about stablecoins
Stablecoins are attracting interest as a payment and settlement tool, although their use for commercial payments remains limited relative to traditional payment systems. At a Bank of Japan seminar in April 2026, Pablo Hernández de Cos, general manager of the BIS, said stablecoins accounted for an estimated $390 billion in real economy payments globally in 2025. However, that was still a small fraction of the estimated $200 trillion in annual global cross-border payments, according to a 2026 paper presented at the BIS Annual Conference.
Kora operates in more than eight markets, including Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Egypt, Côte d’Ivoire, Cameroon, and Tanzania. For merchants, One Rail adds stablecoin wallets to Kora’s existing payment infrastructure. Businesses can receive USDT or USDC, track and reconcile transactions through Kora’s dashboard, hold balances in digital dollars, or convert funds into supported local currencies for transfer to local bank accounts.
“Cross-border commerce in Africa is hindered by high friction and remittance costs,” Nsofor said. “One Rail levels the playing field, enabling merchants to integrate stablecoin payments into their existing payment stack, delivering the speed, cost efficiency, and access needed to drive business growth across the continent.”
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: You call that a foldable? The Vivo X Fold 6 is the iPhone Duo dialed up to 11 — I'm obsessed
articles.text:
The Vivo X Fold 6 takes better photos than my iPhone 18 Pro and weighs less than the iPhone Duo — I'm obsessed
Can raw specs beat novelty? Vivo thinks so, and it might be right
Vivo's latest foldable just hit the global market, after first appearing in China in June. I'll rip the band-aid off early: the X Fold 6 won't be launching in the UK or US, but it will be available in select European markets (as per usual).
The Vivo X Fold 6 is launching at a very interesting time. Apple's first-ever foldable, the iPhone Duo, is just about to land, and Samsung shook things up with its passport-sized Galaxy Z Fold 8 earlier this year, too. Vivo keeps things a little more traditional; the X Fold 6 is the normal book-style fold that Android users are accustomed to. And to keep it appealing, Vivo has maxed out the specs in every department.
Choosing a foldable over a bar phone has always come with compromises, whether that be size and weight, battery capacity, or camera performance. Vivo has been working to eliminate every single one of these limitations, and it's getting really close. I've been using the X Fold 6 as my main device for the past week to see if it lives up to the hype.
The polar opposite of the iPhone Duo
At the moment, it feels like all eyes are on Apple, as the official launch of the Duo draws closer. I get the impression Vivo is more interested in one-upping the likes of the Honor Magic V6 and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, but the launch timing means that many will be weighing up the difference between it and Apple's first attempt at the foldable form factor. It's an interesting comparison, because the two devices couldn't be more different.
The X Fold 6 looks and feels like a Pro Max-sized flagship when folded shut. The cover screen isn't narrow like the Z Fold 8 Ultra's, nor is it shorter like the Duo. It's meant to feel like a regular phone that can unfold into a spacious tablet when you need it, and it succeeds at doing so.
It almost feels like this form factor is going out of style, and I think that's a real shame. The utility is plain to see; apps are all perfectly designed for the cover screen, and when you open it, you can have two apps side by side in their intended aspect ratio. I loved using the Z Fold 8, but I ran into software optimization hiccups on many occasions.
The X Fold 6 is a fairly big and heavy phone, especially compared to the slender Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, but somehow, it's still lighter than the iPhone Duo. The Vivo tips the scales at 235g, while the smaller iPhone Duo weighs 254g. That chunky camera bump on the Vivo is sure to be divisive, though.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
On the other hand, the camera bump is there for a good reason. While the Duo forgoes a telephoto camera entirely, the X Fold 6 has the most impressive telephoto I've ever seen on a foldable. Plus, if you really want to take things to the next level, it supports the same external teleconverter lens as the X300 Ultra.
